rubric: editorial meaning 35 (human review) + theme 25 + author 15 + provenance 15 + memorability 10

quotes.text: Idleness is fatal only to the mediocre.
quotes.author: Albert Camus

quotes.text: To aspire to be superhuman is a most discreditable admission that you lack the guts, the wit, the moderating judgment to be successfully and consummately human.
quotes.author: Aldous Huxley

quotes.text: Laziness may look inviting, but only work gives you true satisfaction.
quotes.author: Anne Frank
quotes.source: Variant translation: Laziness may appear attractive but work gives satisfaction.

quotes.text: One swallow does not make a summer, nor does one day; and so too one day, or a short time, does not make a man blessed and happy.
quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.text: Therefore only an utterly senseless person can fail to know that our characters are the result of our conduct.
quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.text: If you are not prepared for discouragements and disillusions; if you will not be content with a small result for a big effort, then do not begin.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — Precautions Before Beginning

quotes.text: One may have spent one's time badly, but one did spend it; one did do something with it, however ill-advised that something may have been. To do something else means a change of habits.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — Remember Human Nature

quotes.text: Infinite toil would not enable you to sweep away a mist, but by ascending a little you may often look over it altogether. So it is with our moral improvement; we wrestle fiercely with a vicious habit, which could have no hold upon us if we ascended to a higher atmosphere.
quotes.author: Arthur Helps

quotes.text: Be always asham'd to catch thy self idle.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin

quotes.text: Work while it is called to-day, for you know not how much you may be hindered to-morrow.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: The Way to Wealth (Poor Richard's Almanack, 1758)

quotes.text: Choose the course which you adopt with deliberation; but when you have adopted it, then persevere in it with firmness.
quotes.author: Bias of Priene
quotes.source: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers (c. 230)

quotes.text: Nothing ever comes to me, that is worth having, except as the result of hard work.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington

quotes.text: Make at least one definite move daily toward your goal.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee
quotes.source: Part 6 "Beyond System — The Ultimate Source of Jeet Kune Do"

quotes.text: What you HABITUALLY THINK largely determines what you will ultimately become.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee
quotes.source: p. 120; This probably derives from a Rosicrucian proverb, "As you think, so shall you become", which is itself probably derived from Proverbs 23:7 "As…

quotes.text: And he who lives a hundred years, idle and weak, a life of one day is better if a man has attained firm strength.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter VIII. The Thousands, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter II. On Earnestness, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter IX. Evil, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: He who does not rouse himself when it is time to rise, who, though young and strong, is full of sloth, whose will and thought are weak, that lazy and idle man will never find the way to knowledge.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XX. The Way, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: If an earnest person has roused himself, if he is not forgetful, if his deeds are pure, if he acts with consideration, if he restrains himself, and lives according to law,—then his glory will increase.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter II. On Earnestness, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter VIII. The Thousands, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise!
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XVIII. Impurity, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XXIII. The Elephant, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life.
quotes.author: Charles Darwin
quotes.source: volume I, chapter VI: "The Voyage", page 266; letter to sister Susan Elizabeth Darwin (4 August 1836)

quotes.text: I never could have done what I have done, without the habits of punctuality, order, and diligence, without the determination to concentrate myself on one object at a time.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.text: Constant practice devoted to one subject often prevails over both ability and skill.
quotes.author: Cicero
quotes.source: Variant translation: Constant practice given to one matter often conquers both genius and art.

quotes.text: Above all, don't be satisfied to do only fairly well what ought to be done very well. Someone is going to do it better than anyone else; why not you?
quotes.author: Clarence Monroe Bookman
quotes.source: Business Arithmetic (1914), p. 4 To The Pupil

quotes.text: Striving for success without hard work is like trying to harvest where you haven't planted.
quotes.author: David Bly
quotes.source: Peace of Mind : Daily Meditations for Easing Stress (1995) by Amy Dean, p. 187.

quotes.text: The home is the first and most effective place to learn the lessons of life: truth, honor, virtue, self control, the value of education, honest work, and the purpose and privilege of life. Nothing can take the place of home in rearing and teaching children, and no other success can compensate for failure in the home.
quotes.author: David O. McKay
quotes.source: Mormon Parenting Secrets: Time-Tested Methods for Raising Exceptional Children, p. 11

quotes.text: We swallow greedily any lie that flatters us, but we sip only little by little at a truth we find bitter.
quotes.author: Denis Diderot

quotes.text: You must aim high, not in what you are going to do at some future date, but in what you are going to make yourself do to-day. Otherwise, working is just a waste of time.
quotes.author: Edgar Degas

quotes.text: Habit is necessary; it is the habit of having habits, of turning a trail into a rut, that must be incessantly fought against if one is to remain alive.
quotes.author: Edith Wharton

quotes.text: Procrastination is the thief of time.
quotes.author: Edward Young

quotes.text: The practice of perseverance is the discipline of the noblest virtues. To run well, we must run to the end. It is not the fighting but the' conquering that gives a hero his title to renown.
quotes.author: Elias Lyman Magoon
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 450.

quotes.text: And the things in our power are by nature free, not subject to restraint or hindrance; but the things not in our power are weak, slavish, subject to restraint, in the power of others.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Every habit and faculty is confirmed and strengthened by the corresponding actions, that of walking by walking, that of running by running. If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For first, and what causes most trouble, a habit of not attending is formed in you; then a habit of deferring your attention.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if you are not yet in this state, fly from your former habits, fly from the common sort, if you intend ever to begin to be something.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if you once gain time and delay, you will more easily master yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Generally then if you would make anything a habit, do it; if you would not make it a habit, do not do it, but accustom yourself to do something else in place of it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If it be abusive words, you will find it to be patience. And if you have been thus formed to the (proper) habit, the appearances will not carry you along with them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If it is good to use attention tomorrow, how much better is it to do so today? if tomorrow it is in your interest to attend, much more is it today, that you may be able to do so tomorrow also, and may not defer it again to the third day.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If it is habit which annoys us, we must try to seek aid against habit.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If then you wish not to be of an angry temper, do not feed the habit: throw nothing on it which will increase it: at first keep quiet, and count the days on which you have not been angry.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If you do not wish to be prone to anger, do not feed the habit; give it nothing which may tend its increase.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Lxxv, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: If you have given way to anger, be sure that over and above the evil involved therein, you have strengthened the habit, and added fuel to the fire.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Lxxv, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: Is then the fruit of a fig-tree not perfected suddenly and in one hour, and would you possess the fruit of a man’s mind in so short a time and so easily?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Keep neither a blunt knife nor an ill-disciplined looseness of tongue.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — V, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: No man is free who is not master of himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Try, therefore, in the first place, not to be bewildered by appearances. For if you once gain time and respite, you will more easily command yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xx, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Greatness is more than potential. It is the execution of that potential. Beyond the raw talent. You need the appropriate training. You need the discipline. You need the inspiration. You need the drive.
quotes.author: Eric A. Burns

quotes.text: Seek freedom and become captive of your desires. Seek discipline and find your liberty.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: Little by little we human beings are confronted with situations that give us more and more clues that we aren't perfect.
quotes.author: Fred Rogers
quotes.source: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: Thoughts For All Ages

quotes.text: The second half of a man's life is made up of nothing but the habits he has acquired during the first half.
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.source: Peter's Quotations: Ideas for Our Time (1979) by Laurence J. Peter, p. 299

quotes.text: One gets a bad habit of being unhappy.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: The reward of one duty is the power to fulfil another.
quotes.author: George Eliot
quotes.source: Daniel Deronda (1876), Book VI, Chapter XLVI.

quotes.text: Everything that liberates our mind without at the same time imparting self-control is pernicious.
quotes.author: Goethe

quotes.text: In the conduct of life, habits count for more than maxims, because habit is a living maxim, becomes flesh and instinct. To reform one's maxims is nothing: it is but to change the title of the book. To learn new habits is everything, for it is to reach the substance of life. Life is but a tissue of habits.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: He who is false to present duty breaks a thread in the loom, and will find the flaw when he may have forgotten its cause.
quotes.author: Henry Ward Beecher

quotes.text: Do not put your work off till to-morrow and the day after; for a sluggish worker does not fill his barn, nor one who puts off his work: industry makes work go well, but a man who puts off work is always at hand-grips with ruin.
quotes.author: Hesiod

quotes.text: Work is no disgrace; it is idleness which is a disgrace.
quotes.author: Hesiod

quotes.text: Do not say: ‘When I am free, I will study’; perhaps you will never be free.
quotes.author: Hillel

quotes.text: Anger is a momentary madness so control your passion or it will control you.
quotes.author: Horace

quotes.text: Habit is a cable. We weave a thread of it every day, and at last we cannot break it.
quotes.author: Horace Mann

quotes.text: Unfaithfulness in the keeping of an appointment is an act of clear dishonesty. You may as well borrow a person's money as his time.
quotes.author: Horace Mann
quotes.source: quoted in: Kiplinger's Personal Finance, Vol. 12, nr. 2, Feb. 1958. p. 48

quotes.text: Idleness is emptiness; the tree in which the sap is stagnant, remains fruitless.
quotes.author: Hosea Ballou

quotes.text: CALMNESS of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom. It is the result of long and patient effort in self-control.
quotes.author: James Allen

quotes.text: It is a question whether the great majority of people do not ruin their lives and mar their happiness by lack of self-control.
quotes.author: James Allen

quotes.text: Men imagine that thought can be kept secret, but it cannot; it rapidly crystallizes into habit, and habit solidifies into circumstance.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Circumstances

quotes.text: The body is a delicate and plastic instrument, which responds readily to the thoughts by which it is impressed, and habits of thought will produce their own effects, good or bad, upon it.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Health And The Body

quotes.text: The calm man, having learned how to govern himself, knows how to adapt himself to others; and they, in turn, reverence his spiritual strength, and feel that they can learn of him and rely upon him.
quotes.author: James Allen

quotes.text: It is so easy to overestimate the importance of one defining moment and underestimate the value of making small improvements on a daily basis.
quotes.author: James Clear
quotes.source: Speaking on the dire need for small improvements.

quotes.text: The virtues, like the body, become strong more by labor than by nourishment.
quotes.author: Jean Paul

quotes.text: It is no use running; to set out betimes is the main point.
quotes.author: Jean de La Fontaine
quotes.source: quoted in: Forty Thousand Sublime and Beautiful Thoughts Gathered from the Roses, Clover Blossoms, Geraniums, Violets, Morning-glories, and Pansies of…

quotes.text: Temperance is reason's girdle and passion's bridle, the strength of the soul, and the foundation of virtue.
quotes.author: Jeremy Taylor
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 576.

quotes.text: We must all suffer from one of two pains: the pain of discipline or the pain of regret. The difference is discipline weighs ounces while regret weighs tons.
quotes.author: Jim Rohn

quotes.text: We must discipline ourselves to convert dreams into plans, and plans into goals, and goals into those small daily activities that will lead us, one sure step at a time, toward a better future.
quotes.author: Jim Rohn
quotes.source: Five Major Pieces To the Life Puzzle (1991).

quotes.text: Constantly wrestle with your thought, and whenever it wanders call it back to you.
quotes.author: Johannes Climacus
quotes.source: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, as translated by Archimandrite Lazarus Moore (Holy Transfiguration Monastery: 1959), § 4:92, p. 43

quotes.text: We must use time as a tool, not as a couch.
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.source: "Address in New York City to the National Association of Manufacturers (496)," December 5, 1961, Public Papers of the Presidents: John F. Kennedy, 196…

quotes.text: Rest is not idleness, and to lie sometimes on the grass under the trees on a summer's day, listening to the murmur of water, or watching the clouds float across the blue sky, is by no means waste of time.
quotes.author: John Lubbock

quotes.text: When my information changes, I alter my conclusions. What do you do, sir?
quotes.author: John Maynard Keynes
quotes.source: Reply to a criticism during the Great Depression of having changed his position on monetary policy, as quoted in "The Keynes Centenary" by Paul Samuel…

quotes.text: The discipline of the written word punishes both stupidity and dishonesty.
quotes.author: John Steinbeck
quotes.source: "In Awe of Words," The Exonian, 75th anniversary edition, Exeter University (1930)

quotes.text: The middle gear of any man is self-discipline.
quotes.author: John le Carré

quotes.text: When you suffer, think not on how you can escape suffering, but concentrate your efforts on what kind of inner moral and spiritual perfection this suffering requires.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: A Calendar of Wisdom, P. Sekirin, trans. (1997)

quotes.text: Know the true value of time; snatch, seize, and enjoy every moment of it. No idleness, no laziness, no procrastination: never put off till to-morrow what you can do to-day.
quotes.author: Lord Chesterfield

quotes.text: I have always been a quarter of an hour before my time, and it has made a man of me.
quotes.author: Lord Nelson
quotes.source: quoted in: The Gentleman's Magazine, Vol. 30, 1848. p. 577

quotes.text: I have learnt through bitter experience the one supreme lesson to conserve my anger, and as heat conserved is transmuted into energy, even so our anger controlled can be transmuted into a power which can move the world.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Young India (15 September 1920), reprinted in Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, Vol. 21 (electronic edition), p. 252.

quotes.text: Remember that there is always a limit to self-indulgence but none to self-restraint, and let us daily progress in that direction.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Article in Young India (2 February 1928, Volume 10, Page 35)

quotes.text: Does the light of a lamp shine and keep its glow until its fuel is spent? Why shouldn't your truth, justice, and self-control shine until you are extinguished?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present,—I am rising to the work of a human being.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: In your actions, don't procrastinate. In your conversations, don't confuse. In your thoughts, don't wander. In your soul, don't be passive or aggressive. In your life, don't be all about business.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Man is made for action, not for idleness or pleasure.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: You're better off not giving the small things more time than they deserve.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The most necessary disposition to relish pleasures is to know how to be without them.
quotes.author: Marquise de Lambert
quotes.source: A Mother's Advice to Her Son (1726), p. 160.

quotes.text: We must set out to do a good job irrespective of race. We must seek to do our life's work so well that nobody could do it better.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.source: 1960s / The Rising Tide of Racial Consciousnes (1960)

quotes.text: Diligence is the mother of good fortune, and idleness — its opposite — never brought a man to the goal of any of his best wishes.
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes
quotes.source: Don Quixote de la Mancha (1605-1615), Part II, Book IV, chapter 38.

quotes.text: When your opponent is hurrying recklessly, you must act contrarily and keep calm. You must not be influenced by the opponent. Train diligently to attain this spirit.
quotes.author: Miyamoto Musashi
quotes.source: Go Rin No Sho (1645) / The Wind Book

quotes.text: Men take on the nature and the habits and the power of thought of those with whom they associate in a spirit of sympathy and harmony.
quotes.author: Napoleon Hill

quotes.text: It takes extraordinary wisdom and self-control to accept that many things have a logic we do not understand that is smarter than our own.
quotes.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
quotes.source: The Bed of Procrustes: Philosophical and Practical Aphorisms (2010) Epistemology and Subtractive Knowledge, p. 78.

quotes.text: Always I will take another step. If that is of no avail I will take another, and yet another. In truth, one step at a time is not too difficult. I will persist until I succeed.
quotes.author: Og Mandino
quotes.source: Ch. 10 : The Scroll Marked III, p. 65.

quotes.text: The mode in which the inevitable comes to pass is through effort.
quotes.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
quotes.source: "Ideals and Doubts", Collected Legal Papers (1937), p. 305

quotes.text: A man must work hard and study hard to counteract the narrowing, hardening tendency of his occupation.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: All great men have been noted for their power of concentration which makes them oblivious of everything outside their aim.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: Discipline the passions, curb pride and impatience, restrain all hasty impulses. Deny yourself the gratification of any desire not sanctioned by reason.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Don't waste life on doubts and fears. Spend yourself on the work before you, well assured that the performance of this hour's duties will be the best preparation for the hours or ages that follow it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Dreaming without effort will only waste your power. It is holding your vision, together with persistent, concentrated endeavor on the material plane, that wins.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Go to the bottom if you would get to the top. Be master of your calling in all its details.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: Great men have found no royal road to their triumph. It is always the old route, by way of industry and perseverance.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVI

quotes.text: He who scatters his efforts in this intense, concentrated age, cannot hope to succeed.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: He who would succeed must hold all his faculties under perfect control; they must be disciplined, drilled, until they obey the will.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If a man lacks self-control he seems to lack everything. Without it he can have no patience, no power to govern himself, he can have no self-reliance, for he will always be at the mercy of his strongest passion.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If unhappiness is a bad habit, you are to turn about by sheer force of will and practice cheerfulness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If you can concentrate your thought and hold it persistently, work with it along the line of your greatest ambition, nothing can keep you from its realization.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If you have the grit and stamina to stick, to persevere to the end, if you persistently maintain the victorious attitude toward your vision victory will crown your efforts.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: In fact, the only real happiness and unalloyed satisfaction we get out of life, is the product of self-control.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is not lack of ability that holds men down but lack of industry.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXI

quotes.text: It is the idle man, not the great worker, who is always complaining that he has no time or opportunity.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter I

quotes.text: Learn, then, to will strongly and decisively; thus fix your floating life and leave it no longer to be carried hither and thither, like a withered leaf, by every wind that blows.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVIII

quotes.text: Let duty be the guiding-star, and success will surely be the crown, to the full measure of one's ability and industry.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter IX

quotes.text: Life should be lived in earnest. It is no idle game, no farce to amuse and be forgotten.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Man is a bundle of habits. We perform most of our life functions with greater or less regularity, so that they become practically automatic.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Never allow yourself to think that you are not complete master of yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIII

quotes.text: Nothing can take the place of push. Push means industry and endurance and everlasting stick-to-it-ive-ness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Nothing is good enough unless it reflects our best.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIV

quotes.text: Nothing will sap one's vitality and blight one's ambition or detract from one's real power in the world more than the worrying habit.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: Practically all the achievements of the human race are but the accomplishments of habit.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Remember that habit is an arrangement, a principle of human nature, which we must use to increase the efficiency and ease of our work in life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLVII

quotes.text: Success is the child of two very plain parents—punctuality and accuracy.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIV

quotes.text: The ability to do hard work, and to stick to it, is the right hand of genius and the best substitute for it,—in fact, that is genius.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIV

quotes.text: The fact is, Nature never made any provision for the idle man.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: The forth-putting of will-power is a means of strengthening will-power. The will becomes strong by exercise.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The habit of conquering ourselves is the habit of victory; it strengthens all the faculties.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The majority of people do not even try to practise self-control; are not willing to sacrifice present enjoyment, ease, for larger future good.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXI

quotes.text: The man who controls himself works to live rather than lives for work.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The man who has a habit of dawdling or listlessness will show it in everything he does.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The man who is punctual, as a rule, will keep his word, and may be depended upon.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIV

quotes.text: The quality which you put into your work will determine the quality of your life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLII

quotes.text: The road to distinction must be paved with years of self-denial and hard work.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XL

quotes.text: The weakest living creature, by concentrating his powers upon one thing, can accomplish something; the strongest, by dispersing his over many, may fail to accomplish anything.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: The will becomes strong by exercise. To stick to a thing till you are master, is a test of intellectual discipline and power.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The will can be educated. That which most easily becomes a habit in us is the will.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: The worst of all foes to success is sheer, downright laziness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Whatever a man's natural advantages may be, great or small, industry and perseverance are his, if he chooses.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Wisdom will not open her doors to those who are not willing to pay the price in self-sacrifice, in hard work. Her jewels are too precious to scatter before the idle, the ambitionless.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LII

quotes.text: You can realize what you desire if you are willing to pay the price, and that is honest, earnest, persistent effort to make it yours.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You must believe what you affirm; you must constantly strive to be what you assert you are, or your affirmations are but idle breath.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You will never become a giant if you only make a pygmy's claim for yourself; if you only expect small things of yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Nothing is stronger than habit.
quotes.author: Ovid
quotes.source: Variant translation: Nothing is more powerful than custom.

quotes.text: Success is not an accident. It is hard work, perseverance, learning, studying, sacrifice and most of all, love of what you are doing or learning to do.
quotes.author: Pelé

quotes.text: Be moderate when prosperous, but prudent when unfortunate.﻿
quotes.author: Periander
quotes.source: The Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, by Diogenes Laërtius

quotes.text: True is the proverb, one's hair will change before one's habits.
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.text: A wise man rules his passions, a fool obeys them.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: Practice justice in word and deed, and do not get in the habit of acting thoughtlessly about anything.
quotes.author: Pythagoras
quotes.source: Divine Harmony: The Life and Teachings of Pythagoras by John Strohmeier and Peter Westbrook. (1999)

quotes.text: Sobriety is the strength of the soul, for it preserves its reason unclouded by passion.
quotes.author: Pythagoras
quotes.source: The History of Philosophy: From the Earliest Times to the Beginning of the Present Century (1819) by William Enfield

quotes.text: How respectable the life that clings to its objects! Youthful aspirations are fine things, your theories and plans of life are fair and commendable:—but will you stick?
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Being successful doesn’t make you manage your time well. Managing your time well makes you successful!
quotes.author: Randy Pausch
quotes.source: Presentation slides from Randy Pausch's Time Management Lecture on November 27, 2007

quotes.text: You don’t find time for important things, you make it.
quotes.author: Randy Pausch
quotes.source: Presentation slides from Randy Pausch's Time Management Lecture on November 27, 2007

quotes.text: I know you've heard it a thousand times before. But it's true — hard work pays off. If you want to be good, you have to practice, practice, practice. If you don't love something, then don't do it.
quotes.author: Ray Bradbury
quotes.source: Ray Bradbury: The Uncensored Biography (2006) by Gene Beley, p. 284

quotes.text: Happiness,” Jubal stated, “lies in being privileged to work hard for long hours in doing whatever you think is worth doing.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: If you happen to be one of the fretful minority who can do creative work, never force an idea; you'll abort it if you do. Be patient and you'll give birth to it when the time is ripe. Learn to wait.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: Everybody, they say Roberto just swings the bat and hits the ball. I work hard. No one works harder than I do. People think things come easy to me. They don't.
quotes.author: Roberto Clemente
quotes.source: "Clemente Says Hitting Does Not Come Easy" by Ralph Bernstein (AP), in The Reading Eagle (March 26, 1968)

quotes.text: Remember, every professional was once an amateur, and every master started as a beginner. Ordinary people can accomplish extraordinary feats, once they’ve routinized the right habits.
quotes.author: Robin Sharma
quotes.source: Talking the importance of building as masters once started small

quotes.text: A man used to vicissitudes is not easily dejected.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: If you are idle, be not solitary; if you are solitary, be not idle.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson
quotes.source: Letter to James Boswell, October 27, 1779, p. 433

quotes.text: Resolve to spend a certain number of hours every day amongst your books.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: A man may possess only his industry, his frugality, his integrity, and yet stand high in the rank of true manhood.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Although success is the guerdon for which all men toil, they have nevertheless often to labour on perseveringly, without any glimmer of success in sight.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: An easy and luxurious existence does not train men to effort or encounter with difficulty; nor does it awaken that consciousness of power which is so necessary for energetic and effective action in life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Better to be under the necessity of working hard and faring meanly, than to have everything done ready to our hand and a pillow of down to repose upon.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: But it is not tools that make the workman, but the trained skill and perseverance of the man himself.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: But the discipline will be always found most valuable which is acquired by resisting small present gratifications to secure a prospective greater and higher one.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Character is formed by a variety of minute circumstances, more or less under the regulation and control of the individual. Not a day passes without its discipline, whether for good or for evil.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Energy of temperament, with a moderate degree of wisdom, will carry a man further than any amount of intellect without it. Energy makes the man of practical ability.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Every great work is the result of vast preparatory training. Facility comes by labour.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Habit is formed by careful training. And it is astonishing how much can be accomplished by systematic discipline and drill.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: He must also be a temperate man, and exercise the virtue of self-denial, than which nothing is so much calculated to give strength to the character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Hence the lesson of self-denial—the sacrificing of a present gratification for a future good—is one of the last that is learnt.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: If a man have not self-control, he will lack patience, be wanting in tact, and have neither the power of governing himself nor of managing others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: If we would be really wise, we must diligently apply ourselves, and confront the same continuous application which our forefathers did; for labour is still, and ever will be, the inevitable price set upon everything which is valuable.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: If you seriously resolve to be energetic and industrious, depend upon it that you will for your whole life have reason to rejoice that you were wise enough to form and to act upon that determination.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Indeed character consists in little acts, well and honourably performed; daily life being the quarry from which we build it up, and rough-hew the habits which form it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is by patience and self-control that the truly heroic character is perfected.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is good habits, which insinuate themselves into the thousand inconsiderable acts of life, that really constitute by far the greater part of man’s moral conduct.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is idleness that is the curse of man—not labour.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is indeed marvellous what continuous application will effect in the commonest of things. It may seem a simple affair to play upon a violin; yet what a long and laborious practice it requires!
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is only by noble patience and noble labour that the masterpieces of genius have been achieved.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is the laborious and painstaking men who are the rulers of the world. There has not been a statesman of eminence but was a man of industry.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is there that we find our chief sphere of duty, that we learn the discipline of work, and that we educate ourselves in that patience, diligence, and endurance which shape and consolidate the character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: It is true, there are men who die of overwork; but many more die of selfishness, indulgence, and idleness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It may be of comparatively little consequence how a man is governed from without, whilst everything depends upon how he governs himself from within.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It was not by luck or accident that these men achieved distinction, but by sheer industry and hard work.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Labour is not only a necessity and a duty, but a blessing: only the idler feels it to be a curse.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Many are the valiant purposes formed, that end merely in words; deeds intended, that are never done; designs projected, that are never begun; and all for want of a little courageous decision.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Nothing great and durable was ever improvised.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Nothing that is of real worth can be achieved without courageous working.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Of all qualities, good temper is the one that wears and works the best in married life. Conjoined with self-control, it gives patience—the patience to bear and forbear, to listen without retort, to refrain until the angry flash has passed.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Our habits or our temptations are not our masters, but we of them.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Practical industry, wisely and vigorously applied, always produces its due effects. It carries a man onward, brings out his individual character, and stimulates the action of others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Precept may point to us the way, but it is silent continuous example, conveyed to us by habits, and living with us in fact, that carries us along.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Such failures, in sensible men, incite to better self-management, and greater tact and self-control, as a means of avoiding them in the future.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: That which is put into us by others is always far less ours than that which we acquire by our own diligent and persevering effort.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: That which the easiest becomes a habit in us is the will.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The best relief is WORK, engaged in with interest and diligence.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The best sort of character, however, cannot be formed without effort. There needs the exercise of constant self-watchfulness, self-discipline, and self-control.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The diligent man is quick to find employment for his leisure; and he is able to make leisure when the idle man finds none.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The habit of application becomes easy in time, like every other habit. Thus persons with comparatively moderate powers will accomplish much, if they apply themselves wholly and indefatigably to one thing at a time.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The habit of working teaches method. It compels economy of time, and the disposition of it with judicious forethought.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The most self-reliant, self-governing man is always under discipline: and the more perfect the discipline, the higher will be his moral condition.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The road of human welfare lies along the old highway of steadfast well-doing; and they who are the most persistent, and work in the truest spirit, will usually be the most successful.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The small events of life, taken singly, may seem exceedingly unimportant, like snow that falls silently, flake by flake; yet accumulated, these snow-flakes form the avalanche.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The solitary thought of a great thinker will dwell in the minds of men for centuries until at length it works itself into their daily life and practice.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The spirits may be exhausted and wearied by employment, but they are utterly wasted by idleness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The tortoise in the right road will beat a racer in the wrong. It matters not though a youth be slow, if he be but diligent.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The truth is, that through our lives nothing brings any good fruit except what is earned by either the work of the hands, or by the exertion of one's self-denial.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The will, which is the central force of character, must be trained to habits of decision—otherwise it will neither be able to resist evil nor to follow good.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Thus the mind and character may be trained to an almost perfect discipline, and enabled to act with a grace, spirit, and liberty, almost incomprehensible to those who have not passed through a similar experience.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: To be morally free—to be more than an animal—man must be able to resist instinctive impulse, and this can only be done by the exercise of self-control.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We can bring the power of the will to bear in making the choice, and thus cultivate the habit of being happy or the reverse.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We may train ourselves in a habit of patience and contentment on the one hand, or of grumbling and discontent on the other.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Wherever formed, habit acts involuntarily, and without effort; and, it is only when you oppose it, that you find how powerful it has become.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: And it is a priceless good to be master of oneself.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 75 (On The Diseases Of The Soul), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Every emotion at the start is weak. Afterwards, it rouses itself and gains strength by progress; it is more easy to forestall it than to forgo it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 116 (On Self-Control), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Everyone approaches courageously a danger which he has prepared himself to meet long before, and withstands even hardships if he has previously practised how to meet them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 107 (On Obedience To The Universal Will), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Good material often stands idle for want of an artist; make the experiment, and you will find it so.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 47 (On Master And Slave), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Much toil remains; to confront it, you must yourself lavish all your waking hours, and all your efforts, if you wish the result to be accomplished.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 27 (On The Good Which Abides), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Neither is knowledge thereof to be won by light effort or small toil; but toiling is worth while when one is about to win all goods at a single stroke.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 76 (On Learning Wisdom In Old Age), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The much occupied man has no time for wantonness, and it is an obvious commonplace that the evils of leisure can be shaken off by hard work.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 56 (On Quiet And Study), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The whole duty of man is embraced in the two principles of abstinence and patience: temperance in prosperity, and courage in adversity.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 576.

quotes.text: The wise man can safely control himself without becoming over-anxious; he can halt his tears and his pleasures at will; but in our case, because it is not easy to retrace our steps, it is best not to push ahead at all.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 116 (On Self-Control), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should so learn them that words may become deeds.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 108 (On The Approaches To Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Wisdom does not show itself so much in precept as in life—in a firmness of mind and mastery of appetite. It teaches us to do, as well as to talk; and to make our actions and words all of a color.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: You must have no dependence on your own genius. If you have great talents, industry will improve them; if you have but moderate abilities, industry will supply their deficiency.
quotes.author: Sir Joshua Reynolds

quotes.text: The being of all virtues, and chiefly of temperance, depends on the practice of them.
quotes.author: Socrates

quotes.text: Never give way to melancholy; resist it steadily, for the habit will encroach.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith

quotes.text: I don't pity any man who does hard work worth doing. I admire him. I pity the creature who does not work, at whichever end of the social scale he may regard himself as being.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: Remarks to the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen in Chattanooga, Tennessee (8 September 1902).

quotes.text: In the last analysis it is the thrift, energy, self-mastery, and business intelligence of each man which have most to do with deciding whether he rises or falls.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Promise And Performance

quotes.text: It is easy to say what we ought to do, but it is hard to do it; and yet no scheme can be devised which will save us from the need of doing just this hard work.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Speech At The Formal Opening Of The Pan-American Exposition, Buffalo

quotes.text: The great man is always the man of mighty effort, and usually the man whom grinding need has trained to mighty effort.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: There is no need of envying the idle. Ordinarily, we can afford to treat them with impatient contempt; for when they fail to do their duty they fail to get from life the highest and keenest pleasure that life can give.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: Genius is one percent inspiration, ninety-nine percent perspiration.
quotes.author: Thomas Edison

quotes.text: Moderation is the silken string running through the pearl-chain of all virtues.
quotes.author: Thomas Fuller
quotes.source: The Holy State and the Profane State (1642), Book III. Of Moderation. See also Bishop Hall—Christian Moderation. Introduction.

quotes.text: Nothing is more dangerous than discontinued labor; it is habit lost. A habit easy to abandon, difficult to resume.
quotes.author: Victor Hugo
quotes.source: Chapter I: The Field of the Lark

quotes.text: Any man may attain self-control if he only will.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: It is conscious formation of mental habits, not mere acquisition of information.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is only the progressive installment plan Nature recognizes. No man can make a habit in a moment or break it in a moment.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Love without manifestation does not feed the heart any more than a locked bread-box feeds the body; it does not illuminate and brighten the round of daily duties any more than an unlit lamp lightens a room.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Man cannot raise himself to higher things by what he would like to accomplish, but only by what he endeavors to accomplish. To be of value, ambition must ever be made manifest in zeal, in determination, in energy consecrated to an ideal.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: No man can make a habit in a moment or break it in a moment. It is a matter of development, of growth.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: No man has made a great success of his life or a fit preparation for immortality by doing merely his duty.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Procrastination is the father of a countless family of things that come too late.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The individual can attain self-control in great things only through self-control in little things.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: The patience man expends in bearing the little trials of his daily life Nature stores for him as a wondrous reserve in a crisis of life.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: The power of self-control is one of the great qualities that differentiates man from the lower animals.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Time is the supreme test, the final court of appeals that winnows out the chaff of false claims, pretended revelation, empty boast, and idle dreams.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: To be ready for the great crises of life we must learn serenity in our daily living. Calmness is the crown of self-control.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: What duty creeps to laboriously, love reaches in a moment on the wings of a dove.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Those who can command themselves, command others.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt

quotes.text: Fewer people are bent from hard work than are crooked from avoiding it.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar

quotes.text: There is no such thing as a lazy person; he is either sick or uninspired.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar

quotes.text: I've been scared my whole damn life. I'm not scared anymore.
quotes.author: Buddy

quotes.text: What's more real than a person trying to help someone they love?
quotes.author: Buddy

quotes.text: Don't have a good day, have a great day.
quotes.author: Guy

quotes.text: I know this world is just a game, but this place, these people, that's all I have. So I'm not gonna be the good guy. I'm gonna be a great guy.
quotes.author: Guy

quotes.text: Life doesn't have to be something that just happens to us.
quotes.author: Guy

quotes.text: As love can do, somewhere along the way it changed me.
quotes.author: Gary Johnson

quotes.text: Seize the identity you want for yourself.
quotes.author: Gary Johnson

quotes.text: Sometimes you just gotta make a move.
quotes.author: Madison Figueroa Masters

quotes.text: All your gifts, and you squander them for your own personal gain?
quotes.author: Megamind

quotes.text: I guess destiny isn't the path chosen for us, but the path we choose for ourselves.
quotes.author: Megamind

quotes.text: Well, maybe I don't want to be the bad guy anymore!
quotes.author: Megamind

quotes.text: There's a yin for every yang. If there's bad, good will rise up against it. It's taken me a long time to find my calling. Now, it's time you found yours.
quotes.author: Metro Man

quotes.text: You can't give up! The Megamind I know would never run from a fight, even if he knew he had no chance of winning! It was your best quality!
quotes.author: Roxanne Ritchi

quotes.text: Courage is poorly housed that dwells in numbers; the lion never counts the herd that are about him, nor weighs how many flocks he has to scatter.
quotes.author: Aaron Hill

quotes.text: The opposite of freedom is not determinism, but hardness of heart. Freedom presupposes openness of heart, of mind, of eye and ear.
quotes.author: Abraham Joshua Heschel

quotes.text: Determine that the thing can and shall be done, and then we shall find the way.
quotes.author: Abraham Lincoln
quotes.source: Speech in the House of Representatives (20 June 1848)

quotes.text: It is easy to be brave from a safe distance.
quotes.author: Aesop

quotes.text: There is always a philosophy for lack of courage.
quotes.author: Albert Camus

quotes.text: Hail to the man who went through life always helping others, knowing no fear, and to whom aggressiveness and resentment are alien. Such is the stuff of which the great moral leaders are made.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: That the situation is hopeless should not prevent us from doing our best.
quotes.author: Aldo Leopold
quotes.source: letter to Bill Vogt, 21 January 1946, quoted in Curt Meine, Aldo Leopold: His Life and Work, p. 478.

quotes.text: Meanings are not determined by situations, but we determine ourselves by the meanings we give to situations.
quotes.author: Alfred Adler
quotes.source: What Life Should Mean to You (1937), p. 14

quotes.text: The most common way people give up their power is by thinking they don't have any.
quotes.author: Alice Walker
quotes.source: The Best Liberal Quotes Ever : Why the Left is Right (2004) by William P. Martin, p. 173.

quotes.text: Fear is real and there is nothing you can do about it except to keep functioning, keep your hands and legs and body moving, your mind focused on the task at hand.
quotes.author: Alvah Bessie
quotes.source: Men in Battle: A Story of Americans in Spain (1939), p. 241

quotes.text: The new dawn blooms as we free it. For there is always light. If only we're brave enough to see it. If only we're brave enough to be it.
quotes.author: Amanda Gorman

quotes.text: The most difficult thing is the decision to act. The rest is merely tenacity. The fears are paper tigers. You can do anything you decide to do. You can act to change and control your life and the procedure. The process is its own reward.
quotes.author: Amelia Earhart
quotes.source: The Official Website of Amelia Earhart - Quotes

quotes.text: Life shrinks or expands according to one's courage.
quotes.author: Anaïs Nin
quotes.source: French Writers of the Past (2000) by Carol A. Dingle, p. 126.

quotes.text: People living deeply have no fear of death.
quotes.author: Anaïs Nin
quotes.source: The Diary of Anais Nin, Volume Two (1934-1939)

quotes.text: A hero is an average person who has done something extraordinary.
quotes.author: Ann E. Dunwoody

quotes.text: Where there's hope, there's life. It fills us with fresh courage and makes us strong again.
quotes.author: Anne Frank

quotes.text: Don't wish me happiness — I don't expect to be happy; it's gotten beyond that, somehow. Wish me courage and strength and a sense of humor — I will need them all.
quotes.author: Anne Morrow Lindbergh
quotes.source: Letter to Corliss Lamont on her engagement (1928)

quotes.text: Life is difficult for those who have the daring to first set out on an unknown road. The avant-garde always has a bad time of it.
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.text: He who has overcome his fears will truly be free.
quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.text: Why should one be afraid of something merely because it is strange?
quotes.author: Arthur C. Clarke

quotes.text: The only thing I am afraid of is fear.
quotes.author: Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of Wellington
quotes.source: Philip Henry, Earl of Stanhope, Notes of Conversations with the Duke of Wellington, published 1888 (November 3, 1831).

quotes.text: There is more courage in avoiding danger than in conquering it
quotes.author: Baltasar Gracián

quotes.text: What resolution is to the will, clarity is to the intellect
quotes.author: Baltasar Gracián

quotes.text: Fear to do ill, and you need fear naught else.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin

quotes.text: How few there are who have courage enough to own their Faults, or resolution enough to mend them!
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin

quotes.text: Fear is the main source of superstition, and one of the main sources of cruelty. To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell
quotes.source: Unpopular Essays, An Outline of Intellectual Rubbish (1950).

quotes.text: No man is liberated from fear who dare not see his place in the world as it is; no man can achieve the greatness of which he is capable until he has allowed himself to see his own littleness.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.text: To fear love is to fear life, and those who fear life are already three parts dead.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.text: There are two ways of exerting one's strength: one is pushing down, the other is pulling up.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington
quotes.source: The Great Quotations (1971) edited by George Seldes, p. 366

quotes.text: Avoidance will make you feel less vulnerable in the short run, but it will never make you less afraid.
quotes.author: Brené Brown
quotes.source: Atlas of the Heart: Mapping Meaningful Connection and the Language of Human Experience (2021)

quotes.text: Vulnerability is not weakness; it's our greatest measure of courage.
quotes.author: Brené Brown
quotes.source: Atlas of the Heart: Mapping Meaningful Connection and the Language of Human Experience (2021)

quotes.text: If we can see our difficulties, there is a way of resolving them, or the hope of a way.
quotes.author: Brian Aldiss

quotes.text: Life is never stagnation. It is constant movement, unrhythmic movement, as we as constant change. Things live by moving and gain strength as they go.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee

quotes.text: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XIX. The Just, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Even death is not to be feared by one who has lived wisely.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Wisdom for the Soul: Five Millennia of Prescriptions for Spiritual Healing (2006) edited by Larry Chang, p. 193

quotes.text: If we long for our planet to be important, there is something we can do about it. We make our world significant by the courage of our questions and by the depth of our answers.
quotes.author: Carl Sagan

quotes.text: The contented have no fear of death.
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.text: Remember that good times and bad times will be part of your life equally, and you have to learn to handle both with equanimity. Make the most of life's opportunities and learn from every opportunity, and challenge that life brings along
quotes.author: Chanda Kochhar
quotes.source: "When Chanda Kochhar spoke about importance of honesty in letter to daughter" (Jul 22, 2025) Hindustan Times.

quotes.text: Courage is a moral quality; it is not a chance gift of nature like an aptitude for games. It is a cold choice between two alternatives, the fixed resolve not to quit; an act of renunciation which must be made not once but many times by the power of the will.
quotes.author: Charles Wilson

quotes.text: To be more prompt to go to one’s friends in adversity than in prosperity.
quotes.author: Chilon of Sparta

quotes.text: He has but one great fear that fears to do wrong.
quotes.author: Christian Nestell Bovee
quotes.source: Reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 244.

quotes.text: Patience is only one faculty; earnestness the devotion of all the faculties. Earnestness is the cause of patience; it gives endurance, overcomes pain, strengthens weakness, braves dangers, sustains hope, makes light of difficulties, and lessens the sense of weariness in overcoming them.
quotes.author: Christian Nestell Bovee

quotes.text: The great obstacle to progress is prejudice.
quotes.author: Christian Nestell Bovee

quotes.text: Friendship makes prosperity more shining and lessens adversity by dividing and sharing it.
quotes.author: Cicero

quotes.text: Courage is the ladder on which all the other virtues mount.
quotes.author: Clare Boothe Luce

quotes.text: Few or many, small or great, all is one to a gentleman: he dares not slight any man.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: The Sayings of Confucius — Book XX[184], trans. Leonard A. Lyall

quotes.text: Hold faithfulness and sincerity as first principles. Have no friends not equal to yourself. When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: Love is never troubled; wisdom has no doubts; courage is without fear.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: The Sayings of Confucius — Book XIV, trans. Leonard A. Lyall

quotes.text: Love of daring, without love of learning, sinks into turbulence. Love of strength, without love of learning, sinks into oddity.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: The Sayings of Confucius — Book XVII, trans. Leonard A. Lyall

quotes.text: The superior man has neither anxiety nor fear. When internal examination discovers nothing wrong, what is there to be anxious about, what is there to fear?
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: It is when we all play safe that we create a world of utmost insecurity. It is when we all play safe that fatality will lead us to our doom. It is in the "dark shade of courage" alone that the spell can be broken.
quotes.author: Dag Hammarskjöld
quotes.source: Servant of Peace : A Selection of the Speeches and Statements of Dag Hammarskjöld, Secretary General of the United Nations (1962), p. 107.

quotes.text: Life only demands from you the strength you possess. Only one feat is possible — not to have run away.
quotes.author: Dag Hammarskjöld

quotes.text: To remain indifferent to the challenges we face is indefensible. If the goal is noble, whether or not it is realized within our lifetimes is largely irrelevant. What we must do, therefore, is to strive and persevere and never give up.
quotes.author: Dalai Lama
quotes.source: Beyond Religion: Ethics for a Whole World, Ch. 7 (2011)

quotes.text: 'Tis not in strength of body nor in gold that men find happiness, but in uprightness and in fulness of understanding.
quotes.author: Democritus
quotes.source: Source Book in Ancient Philosophy (1907) / The Golden Sayings of Democritus

quotes.text: It is hard to fight desire; but to control it is the sign of a reasonable man.
quotes.author: Democritus

quotes.text: Strength of body is nobility in beasts of burden, strength of character is nobility in men.
quotes.author: Democritus
quotes.source: Source Book in Ancient Philosophy (1907) / The Golden Sayings of Democritus

quotes.text: It may often be noticed, the less virtuous people are, the more they shrink away from the slightest whiff of the odour of un-sanctity. The good are ever the most charitable, the pure are the most brave.
quotes.author: Dinah Craik
quotes.source: A Woman's Thoughts About Women (1858), Ch. 11.

quotes.text: All negativity is caused by an accumulation of psychological time and denial of the present. Unease, anxiety, tension, stress, worry - all forms of fear - are caused by too much future, and not enough presence.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle
quotes.source: The Power of Now A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997)

quotes.text: The greater part of human pain is unnecessary. It is self created as long as the unobserved mind runs your life.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle
quotes.source: The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment (1997) p. 25

quotes.text: When you complain, you make yourself into a victim. When you speak out, you are in your power.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Courage is doing what you're afraid to do. There can be no courage unless you're scared.
quotes.author: Eddie Rickenbacker
quotes.source: Quote Unquote (1977) compiled by Lloyd Cory, p. 73.

quotes.text: Never does the human soul appear so strong as when it foregoes revenge, and dares to forgive an injury.
quotes.author: Edwin Hubbell Chapin
quotes.source: Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), edited by Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, p. 251

quotes.text: It is the weak man who urges compromise—never the strong man.
quotes.author: Elbert Hubbard

quotes.text: You gain strength, courage, and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face. You are able to say to yourself, "I have lived through this horror. I can take the next thing that comes along."... You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt

quotes.text: It is no use for one to stand in the shade and complain that the sun does not shine upon him. He must come out resolutely on the hot and dusty field where all are compelled to antagonize with stubborn difficulties, and pertinaciously strive until he conquers, if he would deserve to be crowned.
quotes.author: Elias Lyman Magoon
quotes.source: Proverbs for the People (Boston: Gould, Kendall and Lincoln, 1849), pp. 191–192.

quotes.text: It's at the borders of pain and suffering that the men are separated from the boys.
quotes.author: Emil Zátopek
quotes.source: Attributed in "Citius, Altius, Fortius" ("Swifter, Higher, Stronger"), an unsigned article from Khaleej Times, 8 August 2008 (Galadari Printing and Pu…

quotes.text: And if any instance of pain or pleasure, glory or disgrace, be set before you, remember that now is the combat, now the Olympiad comes on, nor can it be put off; and that by one failure and defeat honor may be lost or—won.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — L, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: And if you are accustomed to be exercised in this way, you will see what shoulders, what sinews, what strength you have.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: And if you ever want to practise endurance and toil, do so unto yourself and not unto others—do not embrace statues!
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Clxxvi, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: And if you ever wish to exercise yourself in labor and endurance, do it for yourself, and not for others.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: And what is grief to you? for fear comes from what you expect, but grief from that which is present.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: But if you lay a rotten and ruinous foundation, will not your miserable little building fall down the sooner, the more and the stronger are the materials which you shall lay on it?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Does he then not threaten you at all? If I feel that all these things do not concern me, he does not threaten me at all; but if I fear any of them, it is I whom he threatens.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if it is not right to do it, avoid doing the thing; but if it is right, why are you afraid of those who shall find fault wrongly?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if you are not acting rightly, shun the act itself; if rightly, however, why fear misplaced censure?
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Clxxii, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: For it were better to die of hunger, exempt from grief and fear, than to live in affluence with perturbation; and it is better that your servant should be bad than you unhappy.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xii, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Have you not received manliness? Have you not received endurance?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If labor (pain) be presented to you, you will find that it is endurance.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: It is our attitude toward events, not events themselves, which we can control. Nothing is by its own nature calamitous -- even death is terrible only if we fear it.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Victims and Values : A History and a Theory of Suffering (1990) by Joseph Anthony Amato and David Monge, p. 36

quotes.text: No one then who is in a state of fear or sorrow or perturbation is free; but whoever is delivered from sorrows and fears and perturbations, he is at the same time also delivered from servitude.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: These are the things which make a city strong and impregnable; but nothing else than his opinions makes a man’s soul impregnable.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: What then is the fruit of these opinions? It is that which ought to be the most noble and the most becoming to those who are really educated, release from perturbation, release from fear.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Will you not go back, and you will see clearer when you have laid aside fear?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Will you not make the beginning and lay the foundation in an inquiry whether the determination is sound or not sound, and so then build on it firmness and security?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Yet what faculties and powers you possess for attaining courage and greatness of heart, I can easily show you; what you have for upbraiding and accusation, it is for you to show me!
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Xx, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: You can be invincible, if you enter into no contest in which it is not in your power to conquer.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Fortitude, the virtue which enables us to endure pain, and to banish fear, is of great use in producing tranquility.
quotes.author: Epicurus
quotes.source: Ancient and Modern Celebrated Freethinkers (Half-Hours with the Freethinkers) by Charles Bradlaugh, A. Collins, and J. Watts (1877)

quotes.text: Rudeness is the weak man's imitation of strength.
quotes.author: Eric Hoffer

quotes.text: The fear of becoming a "has been" keeps some people from becoming anything.
quotes.author: Eric Hoffer

quotes.text: Tell me your relation to pain, and I will tell you who you are!
quotes.author: Ernst Jünger

quotes.text: A coward turns away, but a brave man's choice is danger.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.text: How very little can be done under the spirit of fear.
quotes.author: Florence Nightingale
quotes.source: The Book of Positive Quotations (2007) by John Cook, p. 479

quotes.text: I've grown certain that the root of all fear is that we've been forced to deny who we are.
quotes.author: Frances Moore Lappé

quotes.text: It is said that the only fear we cannot correct is the fear of our own mistakes.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: Let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself—nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance.
quotes.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
quotes.source: inaugural address (March 4, 1933); in The Public Papers and Addresses of Franklin D. Roosevelt, 1933 (1938), p. 11.

quotes.text: The only limit to our realization of tomorrow will be our doubts of today. Let us move forward with strong and active faith.
quotes.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Public Papers and Addresses of Franklin D. Roosevelt, 1944–45 (1950), p. 616, which states: "This is the latest draft of the President's proposed…

quotes.text: Even the most courageous among us only rarely has the courage to face what he already knows.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: In the mountains of truth you will never climb in vain: either you will get up higher today or you will exercise your strength so as to be able to get up higher tomorrow.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most.
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.source: Crime and Punishment Part I, Ch. 1 (1866).

quotes.text: Courage is almost a contradiction in terms. It means a strong desire to live taking the form of a readiness to die.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text: Liberty means responsibility. That is why most men dread it.
quotes.author: George Bernard Shaw

quotes.text: Any coward can fight a battle when he's sure of winning; but give me the man who has pluck to fight when he's sure of losing. That's my way, sir; and there are many victories worse than a defeat.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: I think any hardship is better than pretending to do what one is paid for, and never really doing it.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: Our life is determined for us — and it makes the mind very free when we give up wishing and only think of bearing what is laid upon us and doing what is given us to do.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: People glorify all sorts of bravery except the bravery they might show on behalf of their nearest neighbors.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: Tito was experiencing that inexorable law of human souls, that we prepare ourselves for sudden deeds by the reiterated choice of good or evil that gradually determines character.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: If you want to be successful in a particular field of endeavor, I think perseverance is one of the key qualities.
quotes.author: George Lucas
quotes.source: the George Lucas Interview, ‘A Life Making Movies’, for the Academy of Achievement organization, June 19, 1999, Washington, D.C.

quotes.text: The direst foe of courage is the fear itself, not the object of it; and the man who can overcome his own terror is a hero and more.
quotes.author: George MacDonald

quotes.text: To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
quotes.author: George Orwell
quotes.source: "In Front of Your Nose," Tribune (22 March 1946)

quotes.text: Success rests with having the courage and endurance and above all the will to become the person you are, however, peculiar that may be. The you will be able to say, “ I have found my hero and he is me”.
quotes.author: George Sheehan
quotes.source: “Wisdom for the Soul: Five Millennia of Prescriptions for Spiritual Healing”, p. 425

quotes.text: Just remember, you can do anything you set your mind to, but it takes action, perseverance, and facing your fears.
quotes.author: Gillian Anderson
quotes.source: excerpt from the foreword in Girl Boss: Running the Show Like the Big Chicks (1999).

quotes.text: Until I feared I would lose it, I never loved to read. One does not love breathing.
quotes.author: Harper Lee

quotes.text: He who chooses the beginning of a road chooses the place it leads to. It is the means that determine the end.
quotes.author: Harry Emerson Fosdick

quotes.text: Security is mostly a superstition. It does not exist in nature, nor do the children of men as a whole experience it. Avoiding danger is no safer in the long run than outright exposure. Life is either a daring adventure, or nothing.
quotes.author: Helen Keller
quotes.source: The Open Door (1957). This quotation is often contracted into: Security is mostly a superstition... Life is either a daring adventure, or nothing. or…

quotes.text: We differ, blind and seeing, one from another, not in our senses, but in the use we make of them, in the imagination and courage with which we seek wisdom beyond the senses.
quotes.author: Helen Keller

quotes.text: Who shall dare let his incapacity for hope or goodness cast a shadow upon the courage of those who bear their burdens as if they were privileges?
quotes.author: Helen Keller

quotes.text: Fear makes us run away from each other or cling to each other but does not create true intimacy.
quotes.author: Henri Nouwen
quotes.source: Lifesigns: Intimacy, Fecundity, and Ecstasy in Christian Perspective (1986), p. 30

quotes.text: Heroism is the brilliant triumph of the soul over the flesh — that is to say, over fear: fear of poverty, of suffering, of calumny, of sickness, of isolation, and of death. There is no serious piety without heroism. Heroism is the dazzling and glorious concentration of courage.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: It is dangerous to abandon one’s self to the luxury of grief: it deprives one of courage, and even of the wish for recovery.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: Only evil grows of itself, while for goodness we want effort and courage.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: I see these men every day go about their business with more or less courage and content, doing more even than they suspect, and perchance better employed than they could have consciously devised.
