quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: It is never too late to give up our prejudices.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Nothing can rightly compel a simple and brave man to a vulgar sadness. While I enjoy the friendship of the seasons I trust that nothing can make life a burden to me.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Nothing is so much to be feared as fear.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: What a man thinks of himself, that it is which determines, or rather indicates, his fate.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Live daringly, boldly, fearlessly. Taste the relish to be found in competition — in having to put forth the best within you to match the deeds of risk-taking, hard-working competitors.
quotes.author: Henry J. Kaiser
quotes.source: in: DeWitt Wallace, ‎Lila Acheson Wallace (1950), The Reader's Digest, Vol. 56, p. 18

quotes.text: Give what you have. To someone, it may be better than you dare to think.
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

quotes.text: The difference between perseverance and obstinacy is that one comes from a strong will, and the other from a strong won't.
quotes.author: Henry Ward Beecher
quotes.source: Proverbial Wisdom : Proverbs, Maxims and Ethical Sentences, of Interest to All Classes of Men. (1903) by Abram N. Coleman, p. 233.

quotes.text: There are always obstacles and competitors. There is never an open road, except the wide road that leads to failure. Every great success has always been achieved by fight. Every winner has scars. The men who succeed are the efficient few. They are the few who have the ambition and will power to develop themselves.
quotes.author: Herbert N. Casson
quotes.source: in: National Printer Journalist Vol 51 (1933), Nr. 7-12. p. 28

quotes.text: The Fates have given mortals hearts that can endure.
quotes.author: Homer

quotes.text: Human life suffers steep inclines on the way through the world. If you don’t keep “endurance” as your watchword as go along, how will you tolerate the thorny undergrowth and the pits and ditches.
quotes.author: Hong Zicheng
quotes.source: “Wisdom for the Soul: Five Millennia of Prescriptions for Spiritual Healing”, p. 224

quotes.text: He who feared that he would not succeed sat still.
quotes.author: Horace

quotes.text: He who has begun has half done. Dare to be wise; begin!
quotes.author: Horace

quotes.text: So live, my boys, as brave men; and if fortune is adverse, front its blows with brave hearts.
quotes.author: Horace
quotes.source: Book II, Satire II, Line 135-136 (trans. E. C. Wickham)

quotes.text: Resolve to edge in a little reading every day, if it is but a single sentence. If you gain fifteen minutes a day, it will make itself felt at the end of the year.
quotes.author: Horace Mann
quotes.source: The Common School Journal, Vol. V, No. 19 (2 October 1843)

quotes.text: We should face reality and our past mistakes in an honest, adult way. Boasting of glory does not make glory, and singing in the dark does not dispel fear.
quotes.author: Hussein I
quotes.source: king of Jordan, remarks during a conference of Arab chiefs of state, Khartoum, Sudan (August 30, 1967), as reported by The New York Times (August 31…

quotes.text: It takes a great deal of courage to stand up to your enemies; but a great deal more to stand up to your friends.
quotes.author: J. K. Rowling
quotes.source: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (Albus Dumbledore).

quotes.text: When we become conscious of that which determines our life we attain the highest degree of freedom.
quotes.author: Jacques Ellul

quotes.text: The greatest weakness of all weaknesses is to fear too much to appear weak.
quotes.author: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet
quotes.source: Politique Tirée de l'Écriture Sainte (Politics Drawn from the Very Words of Holy Scripture) (1679 - published 1709).

quotes.text: By the aid of self-control, resolution, purity, righteousness, and well-directed thought a man ascends; by the aid of animality, indolence, impurity, corruption, and confusion of thought a man descends.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — The Thought-Factor In Achievement

quotes.text: He who has conquered doubt and fear has conquered failure. His every thought is allied with power, and all difficulties are bravely met and wisely overcome.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Thought And Purpose

quotes.text: In all human affairs there are efforts, and there are results, and the strength of the effort is the measure of the result.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Visions And Ideals

quotes.text: The strong, calm man is always loved and revered. He is like a shade-giving tree in a thirsty land, or a sheltering rock in a storm.
quotes.author: James Allen

quotes.text: The will to do springs from the knowledge that we can do. Doubt and fear are the great enemies of knowledge, and he who encourages them, who does not slay them, thwarts himself at every step.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Thought And Purpose

quotes.text: Man is a real man, and can live and act manfully in this world, not in the strength of opinions, not according to what he thinks, but according to what he is.
quotes.author: James Anthony Froude

quotes.text: Just remember — if you are really and truly determined to work with animals, somehow, either now or later, you will find a way to do it. But you have to want it desperately, work hard, take advantage of an opportunity — and never give up.
quotes.author: Jane Goodall
quotes.source: My Life with the Chimpanzees (1996), p. 113

quotes.text: Everyone believes very easily whatever they fear or desire.
quotes.author: Jean de La Fontaine
quotes.source: Subcontact : Slap the Face of Fear and Wake Up Your Subconscious‎ (2001) by Dian Benson, p. 149

quotes.text: In a world, man must create his own essence: it is in throwing himself into the world, suffering there, struggling there, that he gradually defines himself.
quotes.author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quotes.text: The battles that count aren't the ones for gold medals. The struggles within yourself — the invisible, inevitable battles inside all of us — that's where it's at.
quotes.author: Jesse Owens
quotes.source: Blackthink: My Life as Black Man and White Man (1970)

quotes.text: One is never afraid of the unknown; one is afraid of the known coming to an end.
quotes.author: Jiddu Krishnamurti

quotes.text: What destiny sends, bear! Whoever perseveres will be crowned.
quotes.author: Johann Gottfried Herder
quotes.source: Beautiful Thoughts from German and Spanish Authors (1868) by C.T. Ramage (Craufurd Tait Ramage).

quotes.text: The prudent sees only the difficulties, the bold only the advantages, of a great enterprise; the hero sees both, diminishes those, makes these preponderate, and conquers.
quotes.author: Johann Kaspar Lavater

quotes.text: We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard.
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.source: Address at Rice University on the Nation's Space Effort, Houston, TX (12 September 1962).

quotes.text: What really counts is not the immediate act of courage or of valor, but those who bear the struggle day in and day out — not the sunshine patriots but those who are willing to stand for a long period of time.
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.source: "Remarks at the White House to Members of the American Legion (70)," March 1, 1962, Public Papers of the Presidents: John F. Kennedy, 1962

quotes.text: It is not miserable to be blind; it is miserable to be incapable of enduring blindness.
quotes.author: John Milton
quotes.source: Pro Populo Anglicano Defensio Secunda (1654) p. 32

quotes.text: Nature is always lovely, invincible, glad, whatever is done and suffered by her creatures. All scars she heals, whether in rocks or water or sky or hearts.
quotes.author: John Muir

quotes.text: Endurance is nobler than strength and patience than beauty.
quotes.author: John Ruskin
quotes.source: Bullied Beautiful p. 156 (this link doesn’t work)

quotes.text: In painting as in eloquence, the greater your strength, the quieter your manner.
quotes.author: John Ruskin
quotes.source: Volume V, part VIII, chapter III (1860)

quotes.text: It is not because men's desires are strong that they act ill; it is because their consciences are weak.
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.text: It is as fatal as it is cowardly to blink facts because they are not to our taste.
quotes.author: John Tyndall

quotes.text: To let go means to give up coercing, resisting, or struggling, in exchange for something more powerful and wholesome which comes out of allowing things to be as they are without getting caught up in your attraction to or rejection of them, in the intrinsic stickiness of wanting, of liking and disliking.
quotes.author: Jon Kabat-Zinn
quotes.source: Wherever You Go, There You Are: Mindfulness Meditation in Everyday Life (2005)

quotes.text: Neither wisdom nor good will is now dominant. Hope lies in dreams, in imagination and in the courage of those who dare to make dreams into reality.
quotes.author: Jonas Salk
quotes.source: Address on receiving the Nehru Award (10 January 1977), published in Virginia Woolf Quarterly (1977), Vol. 3, p. 11; also quoted in The Signs of Langu…

quotes.text: Man must not only make himself: the weightiest thing he has to do is to determine what he is going to be. He is causa sui to the second power.
quotes.author: José Ortega y Gasset
quotes.source: Existentialism from Dostoevsky to Sartre, p. 155

quotes.text: Each of us has an inner dream that we can unfold if we will just have the courage to admit what it is. And the faith to trust our own admission. The admitting is often very difficult.
quotes.author: Julia Cameron

quotes.text: And if it is a fear you would dispel, the seat of that fear is in your heart and not in the hand of the feared.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran
quotes.source: The Prophet (1923) — For how can a tyrant rule the free and

quotes.text: We have to continually be jumping off cliffs and developing our wings on the way down.
quotes.author: Kurt Vonnegut
quotes.source: If This Isn't Nice, What Is?: Advice for the Young (2013)

quotes.text: Only those with real strength of character can have real gentleness; those who look gentle are usually merely weak
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: True bravery is shown by performing without witness what one might be capable of doing before all the world.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.
quotes.author: Lao Tzu
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching — 33. 1. He who knows other men is discerning; he who knows himself is, trans. James Legge

quotes.text: The brave only know how to forgive.
quotes.author: Laurence Sterne

quotes.text: Love shows itself more in adversity than in prosperity; as light does, which shines most where the place is darkest.
quotes.author: Leonardo da Vinci

quotes.text: Men out of fear will cling to the thing they most fear.
quotes.author: Leonardo da Vinci
quotes.source: The Notebooks of Leonardo da Vinci (1883) / XX Humorous Writings

quotes.text: Obstacles cannot crush me. Every obstacle yields to stern resolve. He who is fixed to a star does not change his mind.
quotes.author: Leonardo da Vinci
quotes.source: The Notebooks of Leonardo da Vinci (1883) / X Studies and Sketches for Pictures and Decorations

quotes.text: Let me tell you the secret that has led me to my goal. My strength lies solely in my tenacity.
quotes.author: Louis Pasteur
quotes.source: There's a Spiritual Solution to Every Problem (2001) by Wayne W. Dyer

quotes.text: The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: "Interview to the Press" in Karachi about the execution of Bhagat Singh (23 March 1931); published in Young India (2 April 1931), reprinted in Collect…

quotes.text: All things are change, yet we need not fear anything new.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: For all other obstacles either affect the body only, which is a dead thing; or, except through opinion and the yielding of the reason itself, they do not crush nor do any harm of any kind; for if they did, he who felt it would immediately become bad.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is a shame then that ignorance and conceit should be stronger than wisdom.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is in our power to have no opinion about a thing, and not to be disturbed in our soul; for things themselves have no natural power to form our judgments.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live according to nature (xii. 1).
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Let not thy thoughts at once embrace all the various troubles which thou mayest expect to befall thee: but on every occasion ask thyself, What is there in this which is intolerable and past bearing? for thou wilt be ashamed to confess.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Nothing happens to any man that he is not formed by nature to bear. The same things happen to another, and either because he does not see that they have happened, or because he would show a great spirit, he is firm and remains unharmed. It is a shame then that ignorance and conceit should be stronger than wisdom.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Meditations (source), Book V, #18, translated by Gregory Long

quotes.text: Nothing happens to anyone that he can't endure.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Nothing happens to anybody which he is not fitted by nature to bear.

quotes.text: Remember that the ruling faculty is invincible, when self-collected it is satisfied with itself, if it does nothing which it does not choose to do, even if it resist from mere obstinacy.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Remember, however, that thou art formed by nature to bear everything, with respect to which it depends on thy own opinion to make it endurable and tolerable, by thinking that it is either thy interest or thy duty to do this.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: What need is there of suspicious fear, since it is in thy power to inquire what ought to be done?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood. Now is the time to understand more, so that we may fear less.
quotes.author: Marie Curie
quotes.source: Our Precarious Habitat (1973) by Melvin A. Benarde, p. v.

quotes.text: Pain nourishes courage. You can't be brave if you've only had wonderful things happen to you.
quotes.author: Mary Tyler Moore

quotes.text: Nothing, I am sure, calls forth the faculties so much as the being obliged to struggle with the world.
quotes.author: Mary Wollstonecraft

quotes.text: Every day begins with an act of courage and hope: getting out of bed.
quotes.author: Mason Cooley

quotes.text: Unity is strength... when there is teamwork and collaboration, wonderful things can be achieved.
quotes.author: Mattie Stepanek
quotes.source: in: John Chen 50 Digital Team-Building Games:, John Wiley & Sons, 4 April 2012, p.125

quotes.text: Develop enough courage so that you can stand up for yourself and then stand up for somebody else.
quotes.author: Maya Angelou
quotes.source: Rainbow in the Cloud: The Wisdom and Spirit of Maya Angelou (2014), p. 68

quotes.text: If we are bold, love strikes away the chains of fear from our souls.
quotes.author: Maya Angelou

quotes.text: Without courage we cannot practice any other virtue with consistency. We can't be kind, true, merciful, generous, or honest.
quotes.author: Maya Angelou

quotes.text: Courage can't see around corners but goes around them anyway.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: The fear of being laughed at makes cowards of us all.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: The only courage that matters is the kind that gets you from one moment to the next.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: Tough and funny and a little bit kind: that is as near to perfection as a human being can be.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: Fear is sharp-sighted, and can see things underground, and much more in the skies.
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes
quotes.source: Don Quixote de la Mancha (1605-1615), Part III, Book 6.

quotes.text: The brave man carves out his fortune, and every man is the son of his own works.
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.text: The thing I fear most is fear.
quotes.author: Montaigne
quotes.source: Ch. 18. That Men are not to judge of our Happiness till after Death (tr. Donald M. Frame)

quotes.text: Things are not so painful and difficult of themselves, but our weakness or cowardice makes them so.
quotes.author: Montaigne
quotes.source: Ch. 14 (tr. Cotton, rev. W. Carew Hazlitt, 1877)

quotes.text: It is only by struggling with difficult books, books over one's head, that anyone learns to read.
quotes.author: Mortimer Adler

quotes.text: Every adversity has the seed of an equivalent or greater benefit.
quotes.author: Napoleon Hill
quotes.source: A maxim of Hill's, specifically cited as such, in Success Through a Positive Mental Attitude (1960), co-authored with W. Clement Stone, Ch. 14, p. 222…

quotes.text: The person you are the most afraid to contradict is yourself.
quotes.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
quotes.source: The Bed of Procrustes: Philosophical and Practical Aphorisms (2010) Preludes, p.3.

quotes.text: The greatest obstacle to being heroic is the doubt whether one may not be going to prove one's self a fool; the truest heroism is to resist the doubt; and the profoundest wisdom to know when it ought to be resisted, and when to be obeyed.
quotes.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne

quotes.text: Learning how to be strong, to feel her own emotions and not another’s, had been hard; but once you learned the trick of it, you did not forget.
quotes.author: Neil Gaiman

quotes.text: Our march to freedom is irreversible. We must not allow fear to stand in our way.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: The Struggle Is My Life (1990), p. 217

quotes.text: The brave man is not he who does not feel afraid but he who conquers that fear.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

quotes.text: Those who conduct themselves with morality, integrity and consistency need not fear the forces of inhumanity and cruelty.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Nelson Mandela on integrity, At the British Red Cross Humanity Lecture, Queen Elizabeth Conference Centre, London, England (10 July 2003). Source: Fro…

quotes.text: Truth is tough. It will not break, like a bubble, at a touch; nay, you may kick it about all day, like a foot-ball, and it will be round and full at evening.
quotes.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
quotes.source: The Professor at the Breakfast Table (1859), V.

quotes.text: A man who cannot stand erect, who wabbles first one way and then the other, who has no opinion of his own, or courage to think his own thought, is of very little use in this world.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: A man with an iron will, with a determination that nothing shall check his career, is sure, if he has perseverance and grit, to succeed.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: A young man determined and willing will find a way or make one.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVI

quotes.text: All the world loves courage; youth craves it; they want to hear about it, they want to read about it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Always picture yourself as a great, strong, splendid man or woman, clean, true, beautiful—a sublime specimen of humanity.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Begin what you fear to undertake, and half its difficulties will vanish.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Beware of the book which does not make you determined to go and do something and be something in the world.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Brave and honest men do not work for gold. They work for love, for honor, for character.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Conquer your place in the world, for all things serve a brave soul. Combat difficulty manfully; sustain misfortune bravely; endure poverty nobly; encounter disappointment courageously.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVII

quotes.text: Courage and an optimistic outlook upon life are imperative to the winner. Fear is fatal to success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Courage is generosity of the highest order, for the brave are prodigal of the most precious things.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Courage is the great leader in the mental realm.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Determine to do your level best and never to demoralize yourself by doing your second best.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLII

quotes.text: Don't waste time dreaming of obstacles you may never encounter, or in crossing bridges you have not reached.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVII

quotes.text: Even the strongest of us are not beyond the reach of our environment. No matter how independent, strong-willed, and determined our nature, we are constantly being modified by our surroundings.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXV

quotes.text: Every particle of a man's energy, intellect, courage, and enthusiasm is needed to win success in one line.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Everybody knows that determined men are not likely to fail. They carry in their very pluck, grit, and determination the conviction and assurance of success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: Everyone admires a determined, persistent man.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIII

quotes.text: Fear is negative; courage is positive, affirmative.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Fill your mind with courage, hope, and confidence.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: He who would succeed to-day must not only be brave, but must also dare to take chances.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Hope would storm the castle of despair; it gives courage when despondency would give up the battle of life. He is the best doctor who can implant hope and courage in the human soul.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: I should call the strength of will the test of a young man's possibilities.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: If there is anything we ever feel grateful for, it is that we have had courage and pluck enough to push on, to keep going when things looked dark and when seemingly insurmountable obstacles confronted us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: If you have an invitation to speak, no matter how much you may shrink from it, or how timid or shy you may be, resolve that you will not let this opportunity for self-enlargement slip by you.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIII

quotes.text: If you repeat a firm resolve to yourself aloud, vigorously, even vehemently, you are more likely to carry it to reality than if you merely resolve in silence.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: It is astonishing what men who have come to their senses late in life have accomplished by a sudden resolution.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: It is grit, it is perseverance, it is moral stamina and courage that govern the world.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is he who resolves to succeed, and who at every fresh rebuff begins resolutely again, that reaches the goal.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is just such grit that enables men to succeed, for what is called luck is generally the prerogative of valiant souls.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIV

quotes.text: It is only when you doubt your ability to cope with the thing you dread that fear is possible.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: It is the ideal that determines the direction of the life. And what a grand sight, what an inspiration, are those men who sacrifice the dollar to the ideal!
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLV

quotes.text: It makes them stronger, braver, and happier. Such a man makes a little spot of this world a lighter, brighter, warmer place for other people to live in.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It takes faith to look beyond obstacles, to see the way over difficulties, to brave opposition and to allow nothing to swerve us from our course.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Learn to meet hard times with a harder will, and more determined pluck. The nature which is all pine and straw is of no use in times of trial, we must have some oak and iron in us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIV

quotes.text: Men have drawn from adversity the elements of greatness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: Men who leave their mark on the world are men of iron resolution, of grim determination.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Never mind what kind of a man he is, resolve that you will approach your task in the spirit of a master, that whether he is a man of high ideals or not, you will be one.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLII

quotes.text: No matter how many obstacles may block your path, or how dark the way, if you look up, think up, and struggle up, you can't help succeeding.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Our manner and our appearance are determined by our mental outlook.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Since humble birth and handicaps of every sort and degree have not prevented success in the determined man; since want has often spurred to needed action and obstacles but train to higher leaping, why should men fail?
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Strong characters, like the palm-tree, seem to thrive best when most abused. Men who have stood up bravely under great misfortune for years are often unable to bear prosperity.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: Success in life is dependent largely upon the willpower, and whatever weakens or impairs it diminishes success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Success is not measured by what a man accomplishes, but by the opposition he has encountered, and the courage with which he has maintained the struggle against overwhelming odds.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The achievements of will-power are simply beyond computation. Scarcely anything in reason seems impossible to the man who can will strong enough and long enough.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: The boulder which was an obstacle in the path of the weak becomes a stepping-stone in the pathway of the resolute.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIV

quotes.text: The brave, cheerful man will survive his blighted hopes and disappointments, take them for just what they are, lessons and perhaps blessings in disguise, and will march boldly and cheerfully forward in the battle of life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The deed must first live in the thought or it will never be a reality; and a strong, vigorous concept of the thing we want to do is a tremendous initial step.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: The effort or struggle to climb to a higher place in life has strength and dignity in it, and cannot fail to leave us stronger for the struggle, even though we miss the prize.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The great men who have lifted the world to a higher level were not developed in easy circumstances, but were rocked in the cradle of difficulties and pillowed on hardships.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: The habit of vigorous affirmation is the habit of victory. But remember that action must follow on the heels of resolution or you will never go any farther.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The influence of the brave man is contagious and creates an epidemic of noble zeal in all about him.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVII

quotes.text: The man of grit carries in his very presence a power which controls and commands.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: The man who will not execute his resolutions when they are fresh upon him can have no hopes from them afterward.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIV

quotes.text: The man who would do anything worth while in this world must have a vision, and he must have courage to match it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The most successful man is he who has triumphed over obstacles, disadvantages and discouragements.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The reason why so many men fail is because they do not commit themselves with a determination to win at any cost.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: The spirit of courage will transform the whole temper of your life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The storms of adversity, like those of the ocean, rouse the faculties, and excite the invention, prudence, skill, and fortitude of the voyager.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: The strength of a chain lies in its weakest link, however large and strong all the others may be.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLI

quotes.text: The success of those about you who are trying to climb upward will encourage and stimulate you to struggle harder if you have not done quite so well yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXV

quotes.text: The timid, hesitating, vacillating man who listens to his doubts and fears stops to make up his mind, and—the opportunity has passed beyond his reach.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The trend of many a life for good or ill, for success or failure, has been determined by a single book.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The vacillating man, however strong in other respects, is always pushed aside in the race of life by the determined man, the decisive man, who knows what he wants to do and does it; even brains must give way to decision.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: The very resolution to redeem yourself from ignorance at any cost is the first great step toward gaining an education.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LII

quotes.text: The very struggle to get up through the soil has strengthened its fiber and fitted it to cope with the elements above, with the storms it must meet.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The world admires the man who never flinches from unexpected difficulties, who calmly, patiently, and courageously grapples with his fate; who dies, if need be, at his post.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: The world always stands aside for the determined man.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIV

quotes.text: The world in its heart admires the stern, determined doer.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There are a great many people who seem to be courageous enough, but an excessive development of caution holds everything in abeyance to wait for certainty.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is no grander sight than that of a young man or woman in the right place struggling with might and main to make the most of the stuff at command, determined that not a faculty or power shall run to waste.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: There is no strength off the lines of our own individuality.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is something sublime in the youth who possesses the spirit of boldness and fearlessness, who has proper confidence in his ability to do and dare.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is something which everybody admires in an aspiring soul, one whose tendency is upward and onward, in spite of hindrances and in defiance of obstacles.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We all have tender spots, weak spots, and a man can never know his strength who does not study his weaknesses.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We give up too easily under discouragement. We haven't sufficient stamina and grit to push on under disheartening conditions.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We may not find time for what we would like, but what we long for and strive for with all our strength, we usually approximate, if we do not fully reach.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: We only have the right to assume that we can do anything within the limit of our utmost faculty, strength, and endurance.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: We should all be posted upon our weak points, for after all there are many emergencies in life when these weak points, not our strong ones, will measure our manhood and our strength.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What are you afraid of? Failure, even, in an honorable attempt, is preferable to forever postponing the thing that you ought to do.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What can you do with a man who has an invincible purpose in him; who never knows when he is beaten; and who, when his legs are shot off, will fight on the stumps?
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What seems to us disagreeable egotism in others is often but a strong expression of confidence in their ability to attain.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What the age wants is men who have the nerve and the grit to work and wait, whether the world applaud or hiss.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What we fear is invariably something that has not yet happened.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: Whatever our vocation, we should resolve that we will not strangle all that is finest and noblest in us for the sake of the dollar, but that we will put beauty into our life at every opportunity.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LI

quotes.text: Whatever your business, whatever your trials and difficulties, love will ease the jolts of life and smooth your way miraculously.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Without trial you cannot guess at your own strength.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Wondrous is the strength of cheerfulness, altogether past calculation its powers of endurance.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You can not keep a determined man from success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVI

quotes.text: You cannot crush the faith that wrestles with difficulties, that never weakens under trials or afflictions, that pushes on when everybody else turns back, that gets up with greater determination every time it is knocked down.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You cannot keep any one from succeeding who has an unshakable faith in his mission.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You must measure the strength of a man by the power of the feelings he subdues, not by the power of those which subdue him.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You must think in a positive determined way that you are going to succeed in whatever you desire to do or to be before you can expect success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You will be surprised to see how you can increase your courage, your confidence, and your ability, if you will be sincere with yourself and strong and persistent in your affirmations.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Pitiful is the person who is afraid of taking risks.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho
quotes.source: By The River Piedra I Sat Down and Wept (1994)

quotes.text: The only thing standing between you and your dream are your fears...
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: The experience of a sad and tender heart is what gives birth to fearlessness.
quotes.author: Pema Chödrön
quotes.source: How to Meditate: A Practical Guide to Making Friends with Your Mind (2008)

quotes.text: Brave men are brave from the very first.
quotes.author: Pierre Corneille

quotes.text: No man of sense can put himself and his soul under the control of names... You must consider courageously and thoroughly and not accept anything carelessly.
quotes.author: Plato

quotes.text: The expense of a monument is superfluous; my memory will endure if my actions deserve it.
quotes.author: Pliny the Younger

quotes.text: Prosperity is no just scale; adversity is the only balance to weigh friends.
quotes.author: Plutarch
quotes.source: Treasury Of Spiritual Wisdom A Collection Of 10,000 Powerful Quotations For p. 13.

quotes.text: Be not harsh, for gentleness mastereth her more than strength.
quotes.author: Ptahhotep
quotes.source: The Instruction of Ptah-Hotep, trans. Battiscombe Gunn (1906)

quotes.text: Adversity shows whether we have friends, or only the shadows of friends.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: The fear of death is more to be dreaded than death itself.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: Choose rather to be strong in soul than in body.
quotes.author: Pythagoras

quotes.text: We should never believe anything we have not dared to doubt.
quotes.author: Queen Christina of Sweden
quotes.source: Maxims of a Queen, selected and translated by Una Birch (London: John Lane, The Bodley Head, 1907), p. 27.

quotes.text: Let's not play these kids cheap; let's find out what they have that is a strength. What do they have that you can approach and build a bridge upon? Education is all a matter of building bridges, it seems to me.
quotes.author: Ralph Ellison
quotes.source: "What These Children Are Like" (1963), in The Collected Essays, ed. John F. Callahan (New York: Modern Library, 1995), p. 548.

quotes.text: A great part of courage is the courage of having done the thing before. And, in all human action, those faculties will be strong which are used.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Courage charms us, because it indicates that a man loves an idea better than all things in the world, that he is thinking neither of his bed, nor his dinner, nor his money, but will venture all to put in act the invisible thought of his mind.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Do that which is assigned you, and you cannot hope too much or dare too much.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Don't be deceived by a facile exterior. Tender men sometimes have strong wills.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Every brave youth is in training to ride and rule this dragon.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: Every man is actually weak and apparently strong. To himself he seems weak; to others, formidable.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: He who aims high, must dread an easy home and popular manners.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: He who wishes to walk in the most peaceful parts of life with any serenity must screw himself up to resolution. Let him front the object of his worst apprehension, and his stoutness will commonly make his fear groundless.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: I do not wish to treat friendships daintily, but with roughest courage. When they are real, they are not glass threads or frostwork, but the solidest thing we know.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: If a man own land, the land owns him. Now let him leave home, if he dare.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: It is only as a man puts off all foreign support and stands alone that I see him to be strong and to prevail.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: It was a high counsel that I once heard given to a young person, — always do what you are afraid to do.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The height of the pinnacle is determined by the breadth of the base. Every man has this call of the power to do somewhat unique, and no man has any other call.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The mind that is parallel with the laws of nature will be in the current of events, and strong with their strength.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: The sweetest music is not in the oratorio, but in the human voice when it speaks from its instant life tones of tenderness, truth, or courage.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Valor consists in the power of self-recovery, so that a man cannot have his flank turned, cannot be out-generalled, but put him where you will, he stands.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We must set up the strong present tense against all the rumors of wrath, past or to come.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We shun the rugged battle of fate, where strength is born.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: What a man does, that he has. What has he to do with hope or fear?
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Why should we fear to be crushed by savage elements, we who are made up of the same elements?
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: Never give up: There are certain times that you think, “OK, you have beaten me down to my knees. And now the challenge is, I am on my knees and you keep on beating me down. And the question is, are you going to keep beating me all the way to the ground or will I find a way to struggle my way back on to my feet.
quotes.author: Randy Pausch

quotes.text: Go to the edge of the cliff and jump off. Build your wings on the way down.
quotes.author: Ray Bradbury

quotes.text: A brave man is one who admits his fear. Only a fool believes himself invincible.
quotes.author: Robert Asprin

quotes.text: Only those who dare to fail greatly, can ever achieve greatly.
quotes.author: Robert F. Kennedy

quotes.text: We do not go to cowards for tender dealing; there is nothing so cruel as panic; the man who has least fear for his own carcase, has most time to consider others.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.text: A person can meet anxiety to the extent that his values are stronger than the threat.
quotes.author: Rollo May

quotes.text: Courage is not a virtue of value among other personal values like love or fidelity. It is the foundation that underlies and gives reality to all other virtues and personal values. Without courage our love pales into mere dependency. Without courage our fidelity becomes conformism.
quotes.author: Rollo May
quotes.source: The Courage to Create (1975), Ch. 1 : The Courage to Create, p. 12.

quotes.text: Courage is the capacity to meet the anxiety which arises as one achieves freedom. It is the willingness to differentiate, to move from the protecting realms of parental dependence to new levels of freedom and integration.
quotes.author: Rollo May

quotes.text: It is highly significant, and indeed almost a rule, that moral courage has its source in identification through one's own sensitivity with the suffering of one's fellow human beings.
quotes.author: Rollo May
quotes.source: Ch. 1 : The Courage to Create, p. 16

quotes.text: Courage is very important. Like a muscle, it is strengthened by use.
quotes.author: Ruth Gordon

quotes.text: Courage is by no means incompatible with tenderness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Courage is graceful and dignified, whilst fear, in any form, is mean and repulsive.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Difficulties may intimidate the weak, but they act only as a wholesome stimulus to men of resolution and valour.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Duty is not a sentiment, but a principle pervading the life: and it exhibits itself in conduct and in acts, which are mainly determined by man's conscience and freewill.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Even at advanced years men can do much, if they will determine on making a beginning.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Even in yielding, conscience tells us we might resist; and that were we determined to master them, there would not be required for that purpose a stronger resolution than we know ourselves to be capable of exercising.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: For character is itself a fortune; and if the high-principled man will but hold on his way courageously, success will surely come,—nor will the highest reward of all be withheld from him.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Good actions give strength to ourselves, and inspire good actions in others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Duty: With Illustrations of Courage, Patience, and Endurance (1880), Ch. 2, p. 49

quotes.text: He is strong to do good, strong to resist evil, and strong to bear up under difficulty and misfortune.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: He who resolves upon doing a thing, by that very resolution often scales the barriers to it, and secures its achievement.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: If the sense of duty be strong, and the course of action clear, the courageous will, upheld by the conscience, enables a man to proceed on his course bravely, and to accomplish his purposes in the face of all opposition and difficulty.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: If they are stronger than ourselves, we become participators in their strength.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is moral courage that characterises the highest order of manhood and womanhood—the courage to seek and to speak the truth; the courage to be just; the courage to be honest; the courage to resist temptation; the courage to do one's duty.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is only a weak man whom the wind deprives of his cloak: a man of average strength is more in danger of losing it when assailed by the beams of a too genial sun.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is the courageous man who can best afford to be generous; or rather, it is his nature to be so.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is the great lesson of biography to teach what man can be and can do at his best. It may thus give each man renewed strength and confidence.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is the struggle that is the condition of victory.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: It requires strength and courage to swim against the stream, while any dead fish can float with it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Life is a battle to be fought valiantly. Inspired by high and honourable resolve, a man must stand to his post, and die there, if need be.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Many are found capable of bravely bearing up under privations, and cheerfully encountering obstructions, who are afterwards found unable to withstand the more dangerous influences of prosperity.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men may know what is right, and yet fail to exercise the courage to do it; they may understand the duty they have to do, but will not summon up the requisite resolution to perform it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men of sterling character have the courage to speak the truth, even when it is unpopular.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: On the contrary, gentleness and tenderness have been found to characterise the men, not less than the women, who have done the most courageous deeds.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: So do repeated acts, one following another, at length become consolidated in habit, determine the action of the human being for good or for evil, and, in a word, form the character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The battle of life is, in most cases, fought up-hill; and to win it without a struggle were perhaps to win it without honour.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The courage of self-control exhibits itself in many ways, but in none more clearly than in honest living.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The courage of the brave man is contagious, and carries others along with it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The cultivation of this quality is of the greatest importance; resolute determination in the pursuit of worthy objects being the foundation of all true greatness of character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The example of the brave is an inspiration to the timid, their presence thrilling through every fibre.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The first hopes everything, and fears nothing; the last hopes nothing, and fears everything.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The humblest, in sight of even the greatest, may admire, and hope, and take courage.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The lives of some of the greatest men have been a continuous struggle with difficulty and apparent defeat.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The poorest have sometimes taken the highest places; nor have difficulties apparently the most insuperable proved obstacles in their way.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The road into learning is alike free to all who will give the labour and the study requisite to gather it; nor are there any difficulties so great that the student of resolute purpose may not surmount and overcome them.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The sense of duty is a sustaining power even to a courageous man. It holds him upright, and makes him strong.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The very endeavour to gain a firmer position in the world has a certain dignity in it, and tends to make a man stronger and better.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The very sight of a great and good man is often an inspiration to the young, who cannot help admiring and loving the gentle, the brave, the truthful, the magnanimous!
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The work of some of the greatest discoverers has been done in the midst of persecution, difficulty, and suffering.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: There are more good people than bad in the world, and the bad get the upper hand merely because they are bolder.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There is a point which it costs much mental toil and struggling to gain, but which, when once gained, a man can look down from, as a traveller from a lofty mountain, on storms raging below, while he is walking in sunshine.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: They are like bladders tied under the arms of one who has not taught himself to swim. Want of confidence is perhaps a greater obstacle to improvement than is generally imagined.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: This stronger man is he who, by discipline, exercises a constant control over his thoughts, his speech, and his acts.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Though the ordeal of adversity is one from which we naturally shrink, yet, when it comes, we must bravely and manfully encounter it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: To think we are able, is almost to be so—to determine upon attainment is frequently attainment itself.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: True courage and gentleness go hand in hand. The brave man is generous and forbearant, never unforgiving and cruel.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: What ought rather to be rewarded is the endeavour, the struggle, and the obedience; for it is the youth who does his best, though endowed with an inferiority of natural powers, that ought above all others to be encouraged.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: When evil comes, we must deal with it bravely and hopefully.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Where men of high standing have not the courage of their opinions, what is to be expected from men of low standing?
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: A great step towards independence is a good-humoured stomach, one that is willing to endure rough treatment.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 123 (On The Conflict Between Pleasure And Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: All you need to do is to advance; you will thus understand that some things are less to be dreaded, precisely because they inspire us with great fear.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 4 (On The Terrors Of Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Bravery is a scorner of things which inspire fear; it looks down upon, challenges, and crushes the powers of terror and all that would drive our freedom under the yoke.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 88 (On Liberal And Vocational Studies), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Clothe yourself with a hero’s courage, and withdraw for a little space from the opinions of the common man.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 67 (On Ill-Health And Endurance Of Suffering), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Do you, however, always think on death in order that you may never fear it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 30 (On Conquering The Conqueror), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Even the most timid man can deliver a bold speech.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 26 (On Old Age And Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Every honourable act is voluntary. Alloy it with reluctance, complaints, cowardice, or fear, and it loses its best characteristic—self-approval.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 66 (On Various Aspects Of Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Fire is the test of gold; adversity, of strong men.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Floods, or fires, will cause us loss. And we cannot change this order of things; but what we can do is to acquire stout hearts, worthy of good men, thereby courageously enduring chance and placing ourselves in harmony with Nature.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 107 (On Obedience To The Universal Will), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Give me courage to meet hardships; make me calm in the face of the unavoidable.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 49 (On The Shortness Of Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Good luck frees many men from punishment, but no man from fear.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 97 (On The Degeneracy Of The Age), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If we can, let us speak more boldly; if not, let us speak more frankly.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 87 (Some Arguments In Of The Simple Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you ask me, I think that for a man there is no misery unless there be something in the universe which he thinks miserable. I shall not endure myself on that day when I find anything unendurable.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 96 (On Facing Hardships), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you cannot do this, counter one weakness with another, and temper your fear with hope.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 13 (On Groundless Fears), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: It is not the part of a man to fear sweat.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 31 (On Siren Songs), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: It is we ourselves that extend both these limits, lengthening them by our hopes and by our fears.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: It requires the same use of reason, I am fully aware, for a man to endure prosperity well and also to endure misfortune bravely.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 66 (On Various Aspects Of Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Let such a man fight against them with all his might: if he once gives way, he will be vanquished; but if he strives against his sufferings, he will conquer.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 78 (On The Healing Power Of The Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Let us account it worth while to look closely at the matter; then it will be clear how fleeting, how unsure, and how harmless are the things which we fear.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Let us be brave in the face of hazards. Let us not fear wrongs, or wounds, or bonds, or poverty.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 65 (On The First Cause), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Make me more brave now, more just, more restrained!
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 109 (On The Fellowship Of Wise Men), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Many of our blessings bring bane to us; for memory recalls the tortures of fear, while foresight anticipates them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 5 (The Philosopher’S Mean), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: None of us has sifted out the truth; we have passed fear on to one another; none has dared to approach the object which caused his dread, and to understand the nature of his fear—aye, the good behind it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Nothing can subdue him; nothing that must be endured annoys him. For he does not complain that he has been struck by that which can strike any man.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 71 (On The Supreme Good), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Pain, want, disgrace, imprisonment, exile,—these are universally to be feared; but when they encounter the wise man, they are tamed.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 85 (On Some Vain Syllogisms), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Remember that pain has this most excellent quality: if prolonged it cannot be severe, and if severe it cannot be prolonged; and that we should bravely accept whatever commands the inevitable laws of the universe lay upon us.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Remember, however, before all else, to strip things of all that disturbs and confuses, and to see what each is at bottom; you will then comprehend that they contain nothing fearful except the actual fear.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 24 (On Despising Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Take anyone off his guard,—young, old, or middle-aged; you will find that all are equally afraid of death, and equally ignorant of life.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 22 (On The Futility Of Half-Way Measures), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The burden should be suited to your strength, nor should you tackle more than you can adequately handle.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 108 (On The Approaches To Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The conclusion is, not that hardships are desirable, but that virtue is desirable, which enables us patiently to endure hardships.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 67 (On Ill-Health And Endurance Of Suffering), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The love of reason will arm you against the greatest hardships.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 74 (On Virtue As A Refuge From Worldly Distractions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The sun, however, is unimpaired even in the midst of obstacles, and, though an object may intervene and cut off our view thereof, the sun sticks to his work and goes on his course.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 92 (On The Happy Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There are obstacles in our path; so let us fight, and call to our assistance some helpers.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 52 (On Choosing Our Teachers), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is no reason why poverty should call us away from philosophy,—no, nor even actual want. For when hastening after wisdom, we must endure even hunger.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 17 (On Philosophy And Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is nothing so certain among these objects of fear that it is not more certain still that things we dread sink into nothing and that things we hope for mock us.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 13 (On Groundless Fears), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Therefore, encourage and toughen your spirit against the mishaps that afflict even the most powerful.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 4 (On The Terrors Of Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Throw aside all hindrances and give up your time to getting a sound mind; for no man can attain it if he is engrossed in other matters.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 53 (On The Faults Of The Spirit), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We do not fear death; we fear the thought of death.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 30 (On Conquering The Conqueror), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should toughen our minds, and remove them far from the allurements of pleasure.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 51 (On Baiae And Morals), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: What madness it is to be afraid of disrepute in the judgment of the disreputable!
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 91, trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: What then, you ask, is an evil? It is the yielding to those things which are called evils; it is the surrendering of one’s liberty into their control, when really we ought to suffer all things in order to preserve this liberty.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 85 (On Some Vain Syllogisms), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Whatever shall remain to be done virtue can do with courage and readiness.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 74 (On Virtue As A Refuge From Worldly Distractions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Why cast glances toward your strong-box? Liberty cannot be bought.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 80 (On Worldly Deceptions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Why then do you occupy me with the words rather than with the works of wisdom? Make me braver, make me calmer, make me the equal of Fortune, make me her superior.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 117 (On Real Ethics As Superior To Syllogistic Subtleties), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Will you not stop fearing lest that may happen once which really happens every day?
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 58 (On Being), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Wrestle with the duties which you have once undertaken. No man is brave and earnest if he avoids danger, if his spirit does not grow with the very difficulty of his task.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 22 (On The Futility Of Half-Way Measures), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Yes, he has felt pain; for no human virtue can rid itself of feelings. But he has no fear; unconquered he looks down from a lofty height upon his sufferings.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 85 (On Some Vain Syllogisms), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You will thus understand that what you fear is either insignificant or short-lived.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 24 (On Despising Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Our actual enemy is not any force exterior to ourselves, but our own crying weaknesses, our cowardice, our selfishness, our hypocrisy, our purblind sentimentalism.
quotes.author: Sri Aurobindo

quotes.text: Courage is not the absence of fear but the awareness that something else is more important.
quotes.author: Stephen Covey
quotes.source: Foreword to Prisoners of our Thoughts : Viktor Frankl's Principles at Work (2004), by Alex Pattakos, p. x

quotes.text: It is not suffering as such that is most deeply feared but suffering that degrades.
quotes.author: Susan Sontag

quotes.text: Don't look back—forward, infinite energy, infinite enthusiasm, infinite daring, and infinite patience—then alone can great deeds be accomplished.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: Face the brutes.” That is a lesson for all life — face the terrible, face it boldly. Like the monkeys, the hardships of life fall back when we cease to flee before them.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: It is the cheerful mind that is persevering. It is the strong mind that hews its way through a thousand difficulties.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: Our duty is to encourage every one in his struggle to live up to his own highest idea, and strive at the same time to make the ideal as near as possible to the Truth.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength. Teach men of strength that is already within them.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The whole secret of existence is to have no fear. Never fear what will become of you, depend on no one. Only the moment you reject all help are you free.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The world is ready to give up its secrets if we only know how to knock, how to give it the necessary blow. The strength and force of the blow come through concentration.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The world is the great gymnasium where we come to make ourselves strong.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: This life is a hard fact; work your way through it boldly, though it may be adamantine; no matter, the soul is stronger.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The fact is that in order to do any thing in this world worth doing, we must not stand shivering on the bank thinking of the cold and the danger, but jump in and scramble through as well as we can.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith
quotes.source: Lecture IX : On the Conduct of the Understanding

quotes.text: Keep your hands open, and all the sands of the desert can pass through them. Close them, and all you can feel is a bit of grit.
quotes.author: Taisen Deshimaru

quotes.text: But to do this work, keep ever in mind that we must show in a very high degree the qualities of courage, of honesty, and of good judgment.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Strenuous Life

quotes.text: Craft unaccompanied by conscience makes the crafty man a social wild beast who preys on the community and must be hunted out of it. Gentleness and sweetness unbacked by strength and high resolve are almost impotent for good.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: Don't let anyone impose on you. Don't be quarrelsome, but stand up for your rights. If you've got to fight, fight hard and well. To my mind, a coward is the only thing meaner than a liar.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: Talk to schoolchildren in Oyster Bay, Christmastime (1898), as quoted in The Bully Pulpit : A Teddy Roosevelt Book of Quotations (2002) by H. Paul Jef…

quotes.text: Effort along any one line will not suffice. We must not only be good, but strong.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: If the strong man has not in him the lift toward lofty things his strength makes him only a curse to himself and to his neighbor.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Address At The Quarter-Centennial Celebration Of Statehood In Colorado

quotes.text: The men we need are the men of strong, earnest, solid character—the men who possess the homely virtues, and who to these virtues add rugged courage, rugged honesty, and high resolve.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: We can not avoid meeting great issues. All that we can determine for ourselves is whether we shall meet them well or ill.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Strenuous Life

quotes.text: We must not only be good, but strong. We must not only be high-minded, but brave-hearted.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: We must work out our own destiny by our own strength.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: We need men who are far-sighted and resolute; men who combine sincerity with sanity.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Latitude And Longitude Among Reformers

quotes.text: Alas! the fearful Unbelief is unbelief in yourself.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: The work we desire and prize is not the courage to die decently, but to live manfully.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: For if he who resolveth bravely oftentimes falleth short, how shall it be with him who resolveth rarely or feebly?
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: Occasions of adversity best discover how great virtue or strength each one hath. For occasions do not make a man frail, but they show what he is.
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: You can't have thought without emotion, and one emotion is fear, and making an important decision on the basis of fear is not a good idea. So develop your courage.
quotes.author: Ursula Goodenough

quotes.text: Injustice makes the rules, and courage breaks them.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

quotes.text: He who knows how to suffer everything can dare everything.
quotes.author: Vauvenargues

quotes.text: Fear doesn't shut you down; it wakes you up.
quotes.author: Veronica Roth

quotes.text: Look with favor upon a bold beginning.
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: The only lost cause is one we give up on before we enter the struggle.
quotes.author: Václav Havel
quotes.source: Amnesty International's essay "From Prisoner to President – A Tribute"

quotes.text: Give encouragement (the incentive to action) — you will have courage and be encouraged.
quotes.author: W. Clement Stone

quotes.text: Have the courage to say no. Have the courage to face the truth. Do the right thing because it is right. These are the magic keys to living your life with integrity.
quotes.author: W. Clement Stone
quotes.source: Teen Ink : What Matters (2003) by Stephanie H. Meyer, John Meyer, and Peggy Veljkovic, p. 309

quotes.text: There is but one coward on earth, and that is the coward that dare not know.
quotes.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
quotes.source: The Study of the Negro Problems, paragraph 51, in The Annals of the American Academy of Political and Social Science, vol. XI (January 1898)

quotes.text: All our dreams can come true — if we have the courage to pursue them.
quotes.author: Walt Disney
quotes.source: Ch. 3 : Imagination Unlimited, p. 63; Unsourced variant: All your dreams can come true if you have the courage to pursue them.

quotes.text: Nothing endures but personal qualities.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman
quotes.source: Leaves of Grass, Song of the Broad-Axe, Stanza 4.

quotes.text: Life is that which is discontent, which struggles and seeks, which suffers and creates.
quotes.author: Will Durant

quotes.text: A man may be in error and yet live bravely by it; he who is untruthful in his life knows the truth but denies it.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Any one can plant radishes; it takes courage to plant acorns and to wait for the oaks.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: But if this be denied us, then must we bravely walk our weary way alone, toward the sunrise that must come.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: But man never rises to the dignity of true living until he has the courage that dares to face ingratitude calmly, and to pursue his course unchanged when his good works meet with thanklessness or disdain.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Each successive day had its new supply of strength. There is in the leaning tower of Pisa a spiral stairway so steep in its ascent that only one step at a time is revealed to us.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: He does not realize the untiring energy, the unremitting concentration, the heroic courage, the sublime patience that is the secret of some men's success.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If a man honestly seeks to live his best at all times, that determination is visible in every moment of his living, no trifle in his life can be too insignificant to reflect his principle of living.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If man do, day by day, ever the best he can by the light he has, he has no need to fear, no need to regret, no need to worry.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: If you desire the power that some one else possesses, do not envy his strength, and dissipate your energy by weakly wishing his force were yours.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is in the trifles of daily life that truth should be our constant guide and inspiration. Truth is not a dress-suit, consecrated to special occasions, it is the strong, well-woven, durable homespun for daily living.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: It is never easy to meet, and no philosophy can make it so, but the steadfast courage to master conditions, instead of complaining of them, will help him on his way; it will ever enable him to get the best out of what he has.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It ofttimes requires heroic courage to face fruitless effort, to take up the broken strands of a life-work, to look bravely toward the future, and proceed undaunted on our way.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Let us begin to love the truth, to fill our mind and life with the strong white light of sincerity and sterling honesty.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: So it must be that the individual who is most strong in any trial, sorrow or need is he who can live from his inherent strength, who needs no scaffolding of commonplace sympathy to uphold him.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Study the disturbing elements, each by itself, bring all the will power of your nature to bear upon them, and you will find that they will, one by one, melt into nothingness, like vapors fading before the sun.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The man who has a pessimist's doubt of all things; who demands a certified guarantee of his future; who ever fears his work will not be recognized or appreciated; or that after all, it is really not worth while, will never live his best.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The man who longs for some crisis in life, wherein he may show mighty courage, while he is expending no portion of that courage in bearing bravely the petty trials, sorrows and disappointments of daily life, is living in an air-castle.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Then, in some great hour of your life, when you stand face to face with some awful trial, when the structure of your ambition and life-work crumbles in a moment, you will be brave.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
