quotes.text: Be polite and generous, but don't undervalue yourself. You will be useful, at any rate; you may just as well be happy, while you are about it.
quotes.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.

quotes.text: Beware how you take away hope from any human being.
quotes.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
quotes.source: his valedictory address to medical graduates at Harvard University (10 March 1858), published in The Boston Medical and Surgical Journal, Vol. LVIII…

quotes.text: A cheerful man is pre-eminently a useful man.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: A man who is self-reliant, positive, optimistic, and undertakes his work with the assurance of success, magnetizes conditions.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: By cultivating the positive we drive out the negative.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Don't bark against the bad, but chant the beauties of the good. The positive, creative, affirmative elements are our friends.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Don't let these things sap any more of your vitality, waste any more of your time or destroy any more of your happiness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Early form the happy habit, the habit of enjoyment every day, no matter what comes or does not come to you during the day.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: Every one has sufficient positive power to guide and direct his own life if he will only use and develop that power.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every one of us has an inalienable right to be comfortable, prosperous, free from anxiety,—in short to be happy.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every soul is born responsive to the beautiful, but this instinctive love of beauty must be fostered through the eye and the mind must be cultivated, or it will die.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LI

quotes.text: Give your life, your energy, your enthusiasm, all to the highest work of which you are capable.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: Happiness and usefulness were born twins. To separate them is fatal.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: Happiness has very little to do with material things.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: Happiness is incompatible with stagnation. A man must feel his expanding power lifting, tugging away at a lofty purpose, or he will miss the joy of living.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: Happiness is made up of very simple ingredients.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: If you bring to your work the spirit of an artist instead of an artisan, a burning zeal, an absorbing enthusiasm, these will take the drudgery out of it and make it a delight.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLII

quotes.text: If you have a grudge against another, forget it, wipe it out, erase it completely, and substitute a charitable love thought, a kindly, generous thought, before you fall asleep.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LV

quotes.text: If you radiate sweetness and light, people will love to get near you, for we are all looking for the sunlight, trying to get away from the shadows.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: In order to do this you must think confident, cheerful, creative thoughts.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: It is an erring habit of life if we are not first of all cheerful.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is cheerfulness that has the staying quality, like the sunshine changing a world of gloom into a paradise of beauty.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the bright and cheerful spirit that wins the final triumph.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the bright, cheerful, hopeful, contented man who makes his way, who is respected and admired.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the grand secret of a happy home to express the affection you really have.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Joyfulness keeps the heart and face young. A good laugh makes us better friends with ourselves and everybody around us, and puts us into closer touch with what is best and brightest in our lot in life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Let go of everything that is unpleasant; all the mistakes, all the disagreeable past; just rise up in arms against the enemies of your peace and happiness; summon all the force you can muster and drive them out.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Love is serenity, is peace and happiness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVII

quotes.text: Love lightens the burden and cheers the way. Where the heart is, there the burden is light.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Love, like the sun, never sees the dark side of anything.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Make a strenuous effort to radiate joy and gladness to everybody about you.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Never affirm, or think about yourself, your prospects, your career, or your happiness what you do not wish to come true.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: One of the greatest investments one can make is that of attaining a gracious manner, cordiality of bearing, generosity of feeling,—the delightful art of pleasing.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: Paradise is here or nowhere: you must take your joy with you or you will never find it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Resolve that no matter what happens you are going to be happy; that you are going to enjoy yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: So the heart's good cheer and deeds of kindness are always acceptable to children and youth, to busy men and women, to the aged, and to a world of invalids.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Take no chances with your happiness, or the sort of a life that can produce it; whatever else you risk, do not risk this.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: The ability to get on with scolding, irritating people is a great art in doing business. To preserve serenity amid petty trials is a happy gift.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The art of arts is learning how to clear the mind of its enemies—enemies of our comfort, happiness, and success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: The basis of all real personal beauty is a kindly, helpful bearing and a desire to scatter sunshine and good cheer everywhere, and this, shining through the face, makes it beautiful.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LI

quotes.text: The constantly cheerful man, who survives his blighted hopes and disappointments, who takes them just for what they are, lessons, and perhaps blessings in disguise, is the true hero.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The essentials of real happiness are few, simple, and close at hand.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: The fact is that their success represents their expectations of themselves—the sum of their creative, positive, habitual thinking.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: The gladness of service, of having some honorable share in the world's work, what is better than this?
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The habit of directing a firm and steady will upon those things which tend to produce harmony of thought would produce happiness and contentment even in the most lowly occupations.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The habit of happy thought would transform the commonest life into harmony and beauty.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The habit of making the best of everything and of always looking on the bright side is a fortune in itself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXVI

quotes.text: The highest happiness must always come from the exercise of the best thing in us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: The man who has no money is poor, but one who has nothing but money is poorer. He only is rich who can enjoy without owning; he is poor who though he have millions is covetous.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXVI

quotes.text: The man who would succeed must think success, must think upward. He must think progressively, creatively, constructively, inventively, and, above all, optimistically.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: The more generously you give, the more you get in return.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: The more you radiate yourself, the more magnanimous you are, the more generous of yourself, the more you fling yourself out to them without reserve, the more you will get back.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: The most beautiful thing on this earth, that which every human being craves most is love.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The most irresistible charm of youth is its bubbling enthusiasm.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIII

quotes.text: The object for which we strive tells the story of our lives. Men and women should be judged by the happiness they create in those around them.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXVI

quotes.text: The positive man is forceful because he has faith in himself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The positive mind repels all thought enemies that would hinder progress.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The serene optimist is one whose mind has dwelt so long upon the sunny side of life that he has acquired a habit of cheerfulness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The very essence of happiness is honesty, sincerity, truthfulness. He who would have real happiness for his companion must be clean, straightforward, and sincere.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: There is no accomplishment, no trait of character, no quality of mind, which will give greater satisfaction and pleasure or contribute more to one's welfare than an appreciation of the beautiful.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LI

quotes.text: There is no greater foe to the aging processes than joy, hope, good cheer, gladness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is nothing more helpful in building a strong positive character than bracing yourself up by searching, heart to heart talks with yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Think the pleasantest, happiest things possible. Hold the most charitable, loving thoughts toward others.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: To extend to all the cup of joy is indeed angelic business, and there is nothing that makes one more beautiful than to be engaged in it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We admire the beautiful face, the beautiful form, but we love the face illumined by a beautiful soul.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LI

quotes.text: We carry each day nobly, doing the duty or enjoying the privilege of the moment, without thinking whether or not it will make us happy.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We may know enough, but we give ourselves out stingily and we live narrow and reserved lives, when we should be broad, generous, sympathetic, and magnanimous.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: We must give to get, we must be great before we can get great enjoyment; great in our motive, grand in our endeavor, sublime in our ideas.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: We should get ourselves into mental harmony, should become serene and quiet before retiring, and, if possible, lie down smiling, no matter how long it may take to secure this condition.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LV

quotes.text: We were made for happiness, to express joy and gladness, to be prosperous.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: What is needed to round out human happiness is a well-balanced life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What is the happiness of your life made up of? Little courtesies, little kindnesses, pleasant words, genial smiles, a friendly letter, good wishes, and good deeds.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLI

quotes.text: What people need is encouragement, uplift, hope.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIII

quotes.text: What we call happiness is the harvest from our life sowing, our habitual thought-sowing, deed-doing.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: What we do begrudgingly without a purpose becomes a delight with one, and no work is well done nor healthily done which is not enthusiastically done.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: What would have been done at the time with pleasure or even enthusiasm, after it has been delayed for days and weeks, becomes drudgery.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIV

quotes.text: Whatever you do, do not brood over your troubles or dwell upon the things which happen to annoy you at the time. Think the pleasantest, happiest things possible.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: You should not go here and there, making prominent either your bad manners or a gloomy face. Who has a right to rob other people of their happiness?
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You were made to express gladness, to go through life with a victorious attitude, like a conqueror.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Keep love in your heart. A life without it is like a sunless garden when the flowers are dead. The consciousness of loving and being loved brings warmth and richness to life that nothing else can bring.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: as quoted by Alvin Redman in The Epigrams of Oscar Wilde (1952)

quotes.text: Laughter is not at all a bad beginning for a friendship, and it is far the best ending for one.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: The Picture of Dorian Gray (1891), Ch. 1.

quotes.text: To be in love is to surpass one's self.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: The Picture of Dorian Gray, ch. 5

quotes.text: Love is the only thing that will save us, independent of any mistakes we may make. Love is always stronger.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: One is loved because one is loved. No reason is needed for loving.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: Stay close to those who sing, tell stories, enjoy life and whose eyes sparkle with happiness. Because happiness is contagious and will always manage to find a solution whereas logic can find only an explanation for the mistake made.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: The soul of the world is nourished by people's happiness.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho
quotes.source: The Alchemist (1988) The Old King, p. 22.

quotes.text: The wise are wise only because they love.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho
quotes.source: Elders on Love: Dialogues on the Consciousness, Cultivation, and Expression of Love (1999) by Kenneth R. Lakritz and Thomas M. Knoblauch

quotes.text: The secret of joy in work is contained in one word — excellence. To know how to do something well is to enjoy it.
quotes.author: Pearl S. Buck

quotes.text: The more difficult the victory, the greater the happiness in winning.
quotes.author: Pelé

quotes.text: Duty makes us do things well, but love makes us do them beautifully.
quotes.author: Phillips Brooks
quotes.source: Primary Education (1916) by Elizabeth Peabody, p. 190

quotes.text: It is a man's kindly acts that are remembered of him in the years after his life.
quotes.author: Ptahhotep
quotes.source: The Instruction of Ptah-Hotep, trans. Battiscombe Gunn (1906)

quotes.text: No man is happy who does not think himself so.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: Every person is worthy of an infinite wealth of love — the beauty of his soul knows no limit.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Love is the ultimate meaning of everything around us. It is not a mere sentiment; it is truth; it is the joy that is at the root of all creation.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: That side of our existence whose direction is towards the infinite seeks not wealth, but freedom and joy.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: If a child is to keep alive his inborn sense of wonder without any such gift from the fairies, he needs the companionship of at least one adult who can share it, rediscovering with him the joy, excitement and mystery of the world we live in.
quotes.author: Rachel Carson
quotes.source: "Help Your Child to Wonder", Woman's Home Companion (July 1956), p. 46.

quotes.text: In these troubled times it is a wholesome and necessary thing for us to turn again to the earth and in the contemplation of her beauties to know the sense of wonder and humility.
quotes.author: Rachel Carson
quotes.source: "The Exceeding Beauty of the World" (Words to Live by), This Week (1952), quoted in Karen F. Stein, Rachel Carson: Challenging Authors (Rotterdam: Sen…

quotes.text: A man who is sure of his point, carries a broad and contented expression, which everybody reads. And you cannot rightly train one to an air and manner, except by making him the kind of man of whom that manner is the natural expression.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: But power dwells with cheerfulness; hope puts us in a working mood, whilst despair is no muse, and untunes the active powers.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Don't waste yourself in rejection, nor bark against the bad, but chant the beauty of the good.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Every promise of the soul has innumerable fulfilments; each of its joys ripens into a new want.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Happy is the hearing man; unhappy the speaking man.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: He who has acquired the ability, may wait securely the occasion of making it felt and appreciated, and know that it will not loiter.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Life is hardly respectable,—is it? if it has no generous, guaranteeing task, no duties or affections, that constitute a necessity of existing. Every man's task is his life-preserver.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Love is fabled to be blind, but kindness is necessary to perception; love is not a hood, but an eye-water.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Essays: First Series, Circles, last paragraph.

quotes.text: Nothing will supply the want of sunshine to peaches, and, to make knowledge valuable, you must have the cheerfulness of wisdom.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Our first mistake is the belief that the circumstance gives the joy which we give to the circumstance.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Some thoughts always find us young, and keep us so. Such a thought is the love of the universal and eternal beauty.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The happy conditions of life may be had on the same terms. Their attraction for you is the pledge that they are within your reach.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The joy of the spirit indicates its strength.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The life of man is the true romance, which when it is valiantly conducted will yield the imagination a higher joy than any fiction.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Essays: Second Series (1844) — Viii. Nonimalist And Realist

quotes.text: The only way to have a good friend is to be one.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The secret of fortune is joy in our hands.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: There is no beautifier of complexion, or form, or behavior, like the wish to scatter joy and not pain around us.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We have a great deal more kindness than is ever spoken.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We judge of a man’s wisdom by his hope, knowing that the perception of the inexhaustibleness of nature is an immortal youth.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: You can never do a kindness too soon, for you never know how soon it will be too late.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Every minute of every hour of every day you are making the world, just as you are making yourself, and you might as well do it with generosity and kindness and style.
quotes.author: Rebecca Solnit

quotes.text: The highest forms of understanding we can achieve are laughter and human compassion.
quotes.author: Richard Feynman
quotes.source: What Do You Care What Other People Think? (1988).

quotes.text: Life does not always meet our expectations, but that should not prevent us from seeking what happiness we can.
quotes.author: Richard Parks
quotes.source: Moon Viewing at Shijo Bridge (2006), reprinted in Rich Horton (ed.) Fantasy: The Best of the Year 2007, p. 300

quotes.text: Don't ever become a pessimist... a pessimist is correct oftener than an optimist, but an optimist has more fun, and neither can stop the march of events.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: Life is filled with tragedy; if you let it overwhelm you, you cannot enjoy life’s innocent pleasures.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: Love is the condition in which the happiness of another person is essential to your own.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein
quotes.source: "Jubal Harshaw" in the first edition (1961); the later 1991 "Uncut" edition didn't have this line, because it was one Heinlein had added when he went…

quotes.text: People who are busy and happy don’t write diaries; they are too busy living.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: The more you love, the more you can love — and the more intensely you love. Nor is there any limit on how many you can love. If a person had time enough, he could love all of that majority who are decent and just.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein

quotes.text: All who have meant good work with their whole hearts, have done good work, although they may die before they have the time to sign it. Every heart that has beat strong and cheerfully has left a hopeful impulse behind it in the world, and bettered the tradition of mankind.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes.source: Aes Triplex (1878), The Oxford Book of Essays ed. by John Gross (New York: Oxford, 1998) [Title is Latin for "triple brass," used by Horace], p. 316

quotes.text: In every part and corner of our life, to lose oneself is to be a gainer; to forget oneself is to be happy.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.text: One person I have to make good: myself. But my duty to my neighbor is much more nearly expressed by saying that I have to make him happy—if I may.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.text: There is no duty we so much underrate as the duty of being happy.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes.source: "An Apology for Idlers," Virginibus Puerisque and Later Essays, p. 88 (1969). Written between 1874–1879.

quotes.text: I think about grief as a measure of our love, that grief compels us to do something, to love more.
quotes.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer

quotes.text: People can’t understand the world as a gift unless someone shows them how it’s a gift.
quotes.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer

quotes.text: Joy, rather than happiness, is the goal of life, for joy is the emotion which accompanies our fulfilling our natures as human beings. It is based on the experience of one's identity as a being of worth and dignity, who is able to affirm his being, if need be, against all other beings and the whole inorganic world.
quotes.author: Rollo May

quotes.text: To love means to open ourselves to the negative as well as the positive — to grief, sorrow, and disappointment as well as to joy, fulfillment, and an intensity of consciousness we did not know was possible before.
quotes.author: Rollo May

quotes.text: If you are wholly perplexed and in straits, have patience, for patience is the key to joy.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: Let the beauty of what you love be what you do.
quotes.author: Rumi
quotes.source: Path for Greatness : Spiritualty at Work (2000) by Linda J. Ferguson, p. 51

quotes.text: All animals, except man, know that the principal business of life is to enjoy it.
quotes.author: Samuel Butler

quotes.text: Hope is itself a species of happiness, and, perhaps, the chief happiness which this world affords.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson
quotes.source: letter of 8 June 1762, in James Boswell, Life of Samuel Johnson (1791), Vol. 1, p. 103

quotes.text: Hope is necessary in every condition. The miseries of poverty, sickness and captivity would, without this comfort, be insupportable.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: It is seldom that we find either men or places such as we expect them... . Yet it is necessary to hope, though hope should always be deluded, for hope itself is happiness, and its frustrations, however frequent, are yet less dreadful than its extinction.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: Pleasure is very seldom found where it is sought. Our brightest blazes of gladness are commonly kindled by unexpected sparks. The flowers which scatter their odours from time to time in the paths of life, grow up without culture from seeds scattered by chance. Nothing is more hopeless than a scheme of merriment.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: A man may be feeble in organization, but, blessed with a happy temperament, his soul may be great, active, noble, and sovereign.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: All hopeful work is healthful; and to be usefully and hopefully employed is one of the great secrets of happiness. Brain-work, in moderation, is no more wearing than any other kind of work.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: An entirely new direction may be given to the life of a young man by a happy suggestion, a timely hint, or the kindly advice of an honest friend.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Bentham lays it down as a principle, that a man becomes rich in his own stock of pleasures in proportion to the amount he distributes to others. His kindness will evoke kindness, and his happiness be increased by his own benevolence.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: But the man was stout in heart and full of hope.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Cheerfulness also accompanies patience, which is one of the main conditions of happiness and success in life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Cheerfulness is also an excellent wearing quality. It has been called the bright weather of the heart.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Every youth should be made to feel that his happiness and well-doing in life must necessarily rely mainly on himself and the exercise of his own energies, rather than upon the help and patronage of others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: He was ever ready to look on the bright side of things; the darkest cloud had to him its silver lining.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Indeed, the habit of viewing things cheerfully, and of thinking about life hopefully, may be made to grow up in us like any other habit.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is a discerner of good. It turns to the brightest side of things, and its face is ever directed towards happiness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is altogether different from penuriousness: for it is economy that can always best afford to be generous.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is energy—the central element of which is will—that produces the miracles of enthusiasm in all ages.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is the kindly-dispositioned men who are the active men of the world, while the selfish and the sceptical, who have no love but for themselves, are its idlers.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Kindness is indeed a great power in the world.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Let any task be undertaken as a thing not possible to be evaded, and it will soon come to be performed with alacrity and cheerfulness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Life, in such a case, would be like a year in which there was no spring. Without a generous seedtime, there will be an unflowering summer and an unproductive harvest.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Love cherishes hopeful and generous thoughts of others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Man enters a new world of joy, and sympathy, and human interest, through the porch of love.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Manners are the ornament of action; and there is a way of speaking a kind word, or of doing a kind thing, which greatly enhances their value.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men may give their money which comes from the purse, and withhold their kindness which comes from the heart.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: One of the most valuable, and one of the most infectious examples which can be set before the young, is that of cheerful working.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Riches are oftener an impediment than a stimulus to action; and in many cases they are quite as much a misfortune as a blessing.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: 19th C Scottish author and reformer. 'Money: Its Use and Abuse', Self-Help (1856), Chapter 10

quotes.text: Sacrifices must, in short, be ever going on if we would obtain any comfort or happiness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The cheapest of all things is kindness, its exercise requiring the least possible trouble and self-sacrifice.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The cheerful man makes a cheerful world, the gloomy man a gloomy one.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The cheerful mind makes it pleasant, and the discontented mind makes it miserable.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The duty of work is written on the thews and muscles of the limbs, the mechanism of the hand, the nerves and lobes of the brain—the sum of whose healthy action is satisfaction and enjoyment.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The fervent spirit is always a healthy and happy spirit; working cheerfully itself, and stimulating others to work.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The journey may occupy a longer time, but the pleasure of the labour involved by it, and the enjoyment of the results produced, will be more genuine and unalloyed.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The largest and most comprehensive natures are generally also the most cheerful, the most loving, the most hopeful, the most trustful.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The most effective work, also, is usually the full-hearted work—that which passes through the hands or the head of him whose heart is glad.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The possession of a library, or the free use of it, no more constitutes learning, than the possession of wealth constitutes generosity.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The records of the lives of good men are especially useful. They influence our hearts, inspire us with hope, and set before us great examples.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The restless, anxious, dissatisfied temper, that is ever ready to run and meet care half-way, is fatal to all happiness and peace of mind.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The true basis of cheerfulness is love, hope, and patience.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The world will be to each one of us very much what we make it. The cheerful are its real possessors, for the world belongs to those who enjoy it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There needs all the force that enthusiasm can give to enable a man to succeed in any great enterprise of life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: These, at first sight, may appear to be small matters; and yet they are of essential importance to human happiness, well-being, and usefulness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: To wait patiently, however, men must work cheerfully. Cheerfulness is an excellent working quality, imparting great elasticity to the character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Uninterrupted joy, like uninterrupted success, is not good for either man or woman.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We can choose to look at the bright side of things, or at the dark.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We can encourage the disposition of looking at the brightest side of things, instead of the darkest. And while we see the cloud, let us not shut our eyes to the silver lining.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We may make the best of life, or we may make the worst of it; and it depends very much upon ourselves whether we extract joy or misery from it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We must ever stand upright, happen what may, and for this end we must cheerfully resign ourselves to the varied influences of this many-coloured life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The happiness of life... is made up of minute fractions — the little soon-forgotten charities of a kiss, a smile, a kind look, a heartfelt compliment in the disguise of playful raillery, and the countless other infinitesimals of pleasurable thought and genial feeling.
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
quotes.source: "The Improvisatore", in S. C. Hall (ed.) The Amulet, yr. 3 (1828), p. 44

quotes.text: Remember there’s no such thing as a small act of kindness. Every act creates a ripple with no logical end.
quotes.author: Scott Adams

quotes.text: Do you ask what is the foundation of a sound mind? It is, not to find joy in useless things.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 23 (On The True Joy Which Comes From Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Happy is the man who can make others better, not merely when he is in their company, but even when he is in their thoughts!
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 11 (On The Blush Of Modesty), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: He who receives a benefit with gratitude repays the first installment on his debt.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: I hope I may be blessed with that kind of mockery; for one should listen in an unruffled spirit to the railings of the ignorant; when one is marching toward the goal of honour, one should scorn scorn itself.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 76 (On Learning Wisdom In Old Age), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you are willing to think often of these things, you will strive not to seem happy, but to be happy, and, in addition, to seem happy to yourself rather than to others.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you are wise, mingle these two elements: do not hope without despair, or despair without hope.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 104 (On Care Of Health And Peace Of Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If, however, you are wise, measure all things according to the state of man; restrict at the same time both your joys and your fears.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: In order to discover one grateful person, it is worth while to make trial of many ungrateful ones.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 81 (On Benefits.), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Learn to be content with little, and cry out with courage and with greatness of soul: ‘We have water, we have porridge; let us compete in happiness with Jupiter himself.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 110 (On True And False Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Let us greedily enjoy our friends, because we do not know how long this privilege will be ours.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 63 (On Grief For Lost Friends), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Make yourself happy through your own efforts; you can do this, if once you comprehend that whatever is blended with virtue is good, and that whatever is joined to vice is bad.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 31 (On Siren Songs), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The latter, it is true, can by himself develop his own parts; nevertheless, even one who is running well is helped by one who cheers him on.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 109 (On The Fellowship Of Wise Men), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: To have whatsoever he wishes is in no man’s power; it is in his power not to wish for what he has not, but cheerfully to employ what comes to him.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 123 (On The Conflict Between Pleasure And Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We have reached the heights if we know what it is that we find joy in and if we have not placed our happiness in the control of externals.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 23 (On The True Joy Which Comes From Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: What is the happy life? It is peace of mind, and lasting tranquillity.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 92 (On The Happy Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: What resource do we find, then, in the face of these losses? Simply this—to keep in memory the things we have lost, and not to suffer the enjoyment which we have derived from them to pass away along with them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 98 (On The Fickleness Of Fortune), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: When will it be your lot to attain this joy? Thus far, you have indeed not been sluggish, but you must quicken your pace.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 27 (On The Good Which Abides), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Whoever makes up his mind to be happy should conclude that the good consists only in that which is honourable.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 74 (On Virtue As A Refuge From Worldly Distractions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You need never believe that a man can become happy through the unhappiness of another.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You need never believe that anyone who depends upon happiness is happy! It is a fragile support—this delight in adventitious things; the joy which entered from without will some day depart.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 98 (On The Fickleness Of Fortune), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You should rejoice with all in their joys and sympathize with them in their troubles, remembering what you should offer and what you should withhold.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 103 (On The Dangers Of Association With Our Fellow-Men), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You should rather be grateful for the weeds you have in your mind, because eventually they will enrich your practice.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki

quotes.text: Happiness does not depend on the size or content of a goal, but on the strength of the desire to have it.
quotes.author: Simon Soloveychik

quotes.text: One's life has value so long as one attributes value to the life of others, by means of love, friendship, indignation and compassion.
quotes.author: Simone de Beauvoir
quotes.source: Successful Aging : A Conference Report (1974) by Eric Pfeiffer, p. 142

quotes.text: I only wish that wisdom were the kind of thing that flowed... from the vessel that was full to the one that was empty.
quotes.author: Socrates

quotes.text: It is hope which maintains most of mankind.
quotes.author: Sophocles

quotes.text: Shared pain is lessened; shared joy, increased — thus do we refute entropy.
quotes.author: Spider Robinson
quotes.source: "Callahan's Law", as expressed in The Callahan Chronicals (1996) [originally published as Callahan and Company (1988)], Part IV : Earth … and Beyond…

quotes.text: Gratitude fills us with rejoicing, for it so rarely finds frank expression; delicacy of feeling warms our hearts.
quotes.author: Stefan Zweig
quotes.source: Twenty-Four Hours in the Life of a Woman (1927)

quotes.text: I think if you do something and it turns out pretty good, then you should go do something else wonderful, not dwell on it for too long. Just figure out what's next.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs
quotes.source: "Jobs: Iconoclast and salesman" by Brian Williams, at MSNBC (25 May 2006)

quotes.text: Be grateful for the highs — and be grateful for the lows — 'cause it's in the lows where you learn.
quotes.author: Suzanne Somers

quotes.text: Let positive, strong, helpful thoughts enter into your brains from very childhood. Lay yourselves open to these thoughts, and not to weakening and paralysing ones.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: Life is to be fortified by many friendships. To love, and to be loved, is the greatest happiness of existence.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith

quotes.text: Mankind are always happier for having been happy; so that if you make them happy now, you make them happy twenty years hence by the memory of it.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith

quotes.text: We know nothing of tomorrow; our business is to be good and happy today.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith

quotes.text: It’s the hope that’s important. Big part of belief, hope. Give people jam today and they’ll just sit and eat it. Jam tomorrow, now—that’ll keep them going forever.
quotes.author: Terry Pratchett

quotes.text: Do not beautify your appearance, but be beautiful in your way of life.
quotes.author: Thales
quotes.source: Early Greek Philosophy: Beginnings and Ionian Thinkers, LCL-525 (2016), p. 143

quotes.text: Hope is the only good that is common to all men; those who have nothing else possess hope still.
quotes.author: Thales
quotes.source: A Dictionary of Thoughts (1908) by Tryon Edwards, p. 234

quotes.text: Every man of us needs such help at some time or other, and each of us should be glad to stretch out his hand to a brother who stumbles.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: From the greatest to the smallest, happiness and usefulness are largely found in the same soul, and the joy of life is won in its deepest and truest sense only by those who have not shirked life's burdens.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: The best work for our uplifting must be done by ourselves, and yet with brotherly kindness for our neighbor.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: There is not a man of us who does not sometimes slip, who does not sometimes need a helping hand; and woe to him who, when the chance comes, fails to stretch out that helping hand.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: When we come to dealing with our social and industrial needs, remedies, rights and wrongs, a ton of oratory is not worth an ounce of hard-headed, kindly common-sense.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: If in our daily life we can smile, if we can be peaceful and happy, not only we, but everyone will profit from it.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Peace Is Every Step : The Path of Mindfulness in Everyday Life (1992) Bantam reissue

quotes.text: Love is the capacity to take care, to protect, to nourish. If you are not capable of generating that kind of energy toward yourself — if you are not capable of taking care of yourself, of nourishing yourself, of protecting yourself — it is very difficult to take care of another person.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Quoted on his official website (30 December 2008)

quotes.text: The miracle is not to walk on water. The miracle is to walk on the green earth in the present moment, to appreciate the peace and beauty that are available now.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

quotes.text: When you understand the roots of anger in yourself and in the other, your mind will enjoy true peace, joy and lightness
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
quotes.source: Teachings on Love (2005) Full Circle Publishing

quotes.text: It is the first of all problems for a man to find out what kind of work he is to do in this universe.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: It is the very joy of man's heart to admire, where he can; nothing so lifts him from all his mean imprisonments, were it but for moments, as true admiration.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: Love is ever the beginning of Knowledge as fire is of light.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: No man who has once heartily and wholly laughed can be altogether irreclaimably bad.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle
quotes.source: Sartor Resartus (1833–1834), Book I, Chapter IV

quotes.text: The whole idea of compassion is based on a keen awareness of the interdependence of all these living beings, which are all part of one another, and all involved in one another.
quotes.author: Thomas Merton
quotes.source: his final address, during a conference on East-West monastic dialogue, delivered just two hours before his death (10 December 1968), quoted in Religio…

quotes.text: And he who seeketh not to please men, nor feareth to displease, shall enjoy abundant peace.
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: The key to self-generated happiness (the only reliable kind) is the refusal to take oneself too seriously.
quotes.author: Tom Robbins
quotes.source: "The Green Man : Tom Robbins" interviewed by Gregory Daurer, in High Times (12 June 2002).

quotes.text: Love doesn't just sit there, like a stone, it has to be made, like bread; re-made all the time, made new.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

quotes.text: Anyone who takes himself too seriously always runs the risk of looking ridiculous; anyone who can consistently laugh at himself does not.
quotes.author: Vaclav Havel

quotes.text: Laughter is sunshine; it chases winter from the human face.
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.text: Love always brings difficulties, that is true, but the good side of it is that it gives energy.
quotes.author: Vincent van Gogh
quotes.source: Letter to Theo van Gogh from Nuenen, (c. 9 March 1884)

quotes.text: The more I think it over, the more I feel that there is nothing more truly artistic than to love people.
quotes.author: Vincent van Gogh
quotes.source: Van Gogh : The Self-portraits (1969) by Fritz Erpel, p. 17

quotes.text: Hope is definitely not the same thing as optimism. It is not the conviction that something will turn out well, but the certainty that something makes sense, regardless of how it turns out.
quotes.author: Václav Havel
quotes.source: Disturbing the Peace (1986), Chapter 5 : The Politics of Hope

quotes.text: Be generous! Give to those whom you love; give to those who love you; give to the fortunate; give to the unfortunate; yes — give especially to those to whom you don’t want to give.
quotes.author: W. Clement Stone

quotes.text: Hope is brightest when it dawns from fears.
quotes.author: Walter Scott
quotes.source: Lady of the Lake (1810), Canto IV, Stanza 1

quotes.text: In inexhaustible good nature is one of the most precious gifts of heave, spreading itself like oil over the trouble sea of thought, and keeping the mind smooth and equable in the roughest weather.
quotes.author: Washington Irving

quotes.text: There is an eloquence in true enthusiasm that is not to be doubted.
quotes.author: Washington Irving

quotes.text: I think we must be careful about too easily accepting, or being too easily grateful for, sacrifices made by others, especially if we have made none ourselves.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry
quotes.source: Citizenship Papers (2003) / The Failure of War

quotes.text: Laugh. Laughter is immeasurable. Be joyful though you have considered all the facts.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry
quotes.source: "Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front" in Farming: A Hand Book (1970)

quotes.text: We are here just for a spell and then pass on. So get a few laughs and do the best you can. Live your life so that whenever you lose it, you are ahead.
quotes.author: Will Rogers
quotes.source: Inscribed on the Will Rogers Memorial Building in Claremore, Oklahoma.

quotes.text: Only solitary men know the full joys of friendship. Others have their family — but to a solitary and an exile his friends are everything.
quotes.author: Willa Cather
quotes.source: Shadows on the Rock (1931), Book III, Ch. 5

quotes.text: All our greatest joys and our deepest sorrows come to us,—alone.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: An optimist is a man who has succeeded in associating with humanity for some time without becoming a cynic.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Content enables one to warm his hands at the fire of a past joy that exists only in memory.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Every man, by his mere living, is radiating sympathy, or sorrow, or morbidness, or cynicism, or happiness, or hope, or any of a hundred other qualities.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Gratitude is thankfulness expressed in action.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Gratitude is the flowering of a seed of kindness; ingratitude is the dead inactivity of a seed dropped on a stone.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Happiness consists not of having, but of being; not of possessing, but of enjoying. It is the warm glow of a heart at peace with itself.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Happiness has a number of under-studies,—gratification, satisfaction, content, and pleasure,—clever imitators that simulate its appearance rather than emulate its method.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Happiness is paradoxic because it may coexist with trial, sorrow and poverty. It is the gladness of the heart,—rising superior to all conditions.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Happiness is the voice of optimism, of faith, of simple, steadfast love.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Human affection is fed by signs and tokens of that affection. Merely having kindly feelings is not enough, they should be made manifest in action.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: If you would hit the bull's-eye of happiness on the target of life, aim above it.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: In the race for wealth men often sacrifice time, energy, health, home, happiness and honor,—everything that money cannot buy, the very things that money can never bring back.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is one of the incidental by-products of an unselfish life. No man can make his own happiness the one object of his life and attain it, any more than he can jump on the far end of his shadow.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is the heart's recognition of kindness that the lips cannot repay. Gratitude never counts its payments.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let his regret and sorrow be manifest in words of kindness and sympathy, and acts of sweetness and love given to all with whom he comes in contact.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Let the sunlight of our sympathy, tenderness, love, appreciation, influence and kindness ever go out from us as a glow to brighten and hearten others.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us conceive of gratitude in its largest, most beautiful sense, that if we receive any kindness we are debtor, not merely to one man, but to the whole world.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us forget the good deeds we have done by making them seem small in comparison with the greater things we are doing, and the still greater acts we hope to do.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us give the children sunlight, love, companionship, sympathy with their little troubles and worries that seem to them so great, genuine interest in their growing hopes, their vague, unproportioned dreams and yearnings.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us not constantly speak of roses having thorns, let us be thankful that the thorns have roses.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Love should be constantly made evident in little acts of thoughtfulness, words of sweetness and appreciation, smiles and handclasps of esteem.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Mere refraining from wrong-doing is but keeping the weeds out of the garden of one's life. But this must be followed by positive planting of the seeds of right to secure the flowers of true living.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Peace is but the breath, the perfume, the life of love.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Place other things higher than your own happiness and it will surely come to you.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Pleasure is temporary, happiness is continuous; pleasure is a note, happiness is a symphony; pleasure may exist when conscience utters protests; happiness,—never.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The basis of happiness is the love of something outside self.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The expectation of gratitude is the alloy of an otherwise virtuous act. It ever dulls the edge of even our best actions.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The little world around us that does not understand us, does not appreciate our ambition or sympathize with our efforts, that seem to it futile, is not intentionally cruel, calloused, bitter, blind, or heartless.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The man who is selfish with one thousand dollars will not develop angelic wings of generosity when his million comes.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The radiation of kindness need not be expressed in money at all.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: There are men and women whose presence seems to radiate sunshine, cheer and optimism.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: There are more people in this world hungering for kindness, sympathy, comradeship and love, than are hungering for bread.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: True happiness must ever have the tinge of sorrow outlived, the sense of pain softened by the mellowing years, the chastening of loss that in the wondrous mystery of time transmutes our suffering into love and sympathy with others.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Unhappiness is the hunger to get; Happiness is the hunger to give.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: We should ever speak the truth,—but only in love and kindness.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: We then realize that our present happiness or success would have been impossible had it not been for some terrible affliction or loss in the past,—some wondrous potent force in the evolution of our character or our fortune.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Hope is the best possession. None are completely wretched but those who are without hope; and few are reduced so low as that.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt
quotes.source: Characteristics, in the manner of Rochefoucauld's Maxims (1823), No. 34

quotes.text: The greatest happiness you can have is knowing that you do not necessarily require happiness.
quotes.author: William Saroyan

quotes.text: Happiness is a good flow of life.
quotes.author: Zeno of Citium

quotes.text: You can't stay in your corner of the forest waiting for others to come to you. You have to go to them sometimes.
quotes.author: A. A. Milne

quotes.text: Every man is said to have his peculiar ambition. Whether it be true or not, I can say, for one, that I have no other so great as that of being truly esteemed of my fellow-men, by rendering myself worthy of their esteem.
quotes.author: Abraham Lincoln
quotes.source: Address Delivered in Candidacy for the State Legislature (9 March 1832)

quotes.text: One of the goals of education should be to teach that life is precious.
quotes.author: Abraham Maslow

quotes.text: We can chart our future clearly and wisely only when we know the path which has led to the present.
quotes.author: Adlai Stevenson

quotes.text: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
quotes.author: Alan Kay
quotes.source: (1971) at a 1971 meeting of PARC. Archived from the orginal on October 24, 2024.

quotes.text: This is the real secret of life—to be completely engaged with what you are doing in the here and now. And instead of calling it work, realize it is play.
quotes.author: Alan Watts

quotes.text: The aim of art, the aim of a life can only be to increase the sum of freedom and responsibility to be found in every man and in the world. It cannot, under any circumstances, be to reduce or suppress that freedom, even temporarily.
quotes.author: Albert Camus

quotes.text: You will never be happy if you continue to search for what happiness consists of. You will never live if you are looking for the meaning of life.
quotes.author: Albert Camus

quotes.text: A hundred times every day I remind myself that my inner and outer life are based on the labors of other men, living and dead, and that I must exert myself in order to give in the same measure as I have received and am still receiving.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: "The World as I See It", Ideas and Opinions, trans. Sonja Bargmann, p. 8 (1954).

quotes.text: I believe in one thing — that only a life lived for others is a life worth living.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: Nothing truly valuable arises from ambition or from a mere sense of duty; it stems rather from love and devotion towards men and towards objective things.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: Helen Dukas and Banesh Hoffmann, Albert Einstein, The Human Side: New Glimpses From His Archives (1979), p. 46 - 30 July 47 - letter

quotes.text: The secret to success is the willingness to serve without aspiring for rewards.
quotes.author: Alhaji Alieu Ebrima Cham Joof
quotes.source: (the Serer and Gambian historian). From : Joof, Alh. A.E. Cham. "Gambia, Land of our heritage" p IV; and The Point Newspaper : "Tribute to Late Alhagi…

quotes.text: We all know that a good example is more effective than advice. So set a good example, and it won't take long for others to follow.
quotes.author: Anne Frank

quotes.text: Each man must look to himself to teach him the meaning of life. It is not something discovered; it is something molded.
quotes.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

quotes.text: Anyone can become angry, that is easy... but to be angry with the right person, to the right degree, at the right time, for the right purpose, and in the right way... this is not easy.
quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.text: Let us then up and be doing, and doing to the purpose: so by diligence shall we do more with less perplexity.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: The Way to Wealth (Poor Richard's Almanack, 1758)

quotes.text: That passion may not harm us, let us act as if we had only eight hours to live.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: I think I have learned that the best way to lift one's self up is to help someone else.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington
quotes.source: The Story of My Life and Work, vol. I (1900), ch. XV: Cuban Education and the Chicago Peace Jubilee Address

quotes.text: Man is born to live, not to prepare for life.
quotes.author: Boris Pasternak

quotes.text: The meaning of life is that it is to be lived, and it is not to be traded and conceptualized and squeezed into a pattern of systems.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee
quotes.source: (2000) Striking Thoughts. edited by John Little. p. 3

quotes.text: Arouse your energy for the attainment of the as-yet-unattained, for the achievement of the as-yet-unachieved, for the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Saṃyutta Nikāya, Book 2, Sutta 12, Verse 22, as translated by Bhikkhu Bodhi (Wisdom Publications: 2000), p. 553

quotes.text: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter III. Thought, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: As far as we can discern, the sole purpose of human existence is to kindle a light in the darkness of mere being.
quotes.author: Carl Jung

quotes.text: For it all depends on how we look at things, and not on how they are in themselves. The least of things with a meaning is worth more in life than the greatest of things without it.
quotes.author: Carl Jung
quotes.source: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)

quotes.text: The meaning and design of a problem seem not to lie in its solution, but in our working at it incessantly.
quotes.author: Carl Jung

quotes.text: The good life is a process, not a state of being. It is a direction not a destination.
quotes.author: Carl Rogers

quotes.text: If we crave some cosmic purpose, then let us find ourselves a worthy goal.
quotes.author: Carl Sagan
quotes.source: Pale Blue Dot: A Vision of the Human Future in Space (1994)

quotes.text: Life is not a search for experience, but for ourselves. Having discovered our own fundamental level we realize that it conforms to our own destiny and we find peace.
quotes.author: Cesare Pavese

quotes.text: No man can purchase his virtue too dear, for it is the only thing whose value must ever increase with the price it has cost us.
quotes.author: Charles Caleb Colton

quotes.text: I have learned that a man who makes trouble for others makes trouble for himself.
quotes.author: Chinua Achebe

quotes.text: There is only one success... to be able to spend your life in your own way, and not to give others absurd maddening claims upon it.
quotes.author: Christopher Morley

quotes.text: Goodness is something so simple: always to live for others, never to seek one's own advantage.
quotes.author: Dag Hammarskjöld

quotes.text: We are not permitted to choose the frame of our destiny. But what we put into it is ours.
quotes.author: Dag Hammarskjöld

quotes.text: A monotonous life, lived without any purpose or direction, is not worth much. To achieve anything big in life, you should be prepared to risk your all and take a leap of faith for whatever they believed in.
quotes.author: Deendayal Upadhyaya
quotes.source: 'Dao lagaao zindagi pe’ (put a stake on your life) by Deendayal Upadhyaya, and quoted from L.K. Advani, My Country My Life (2008)

quotes.text: Life's meaning has always eluded me and I guess it always will. But I love it just the same.
quotes.author: E. B. White
quotes.source: Letter to Mary Virginia Parrish (29 August 1969)

quotes.text: You don't have to be a fantastic hero to do certain things — to compete. You can be just an ordinary chap, sufficiently motivated to reach challenging goals. The intense effort, the giving of everything you've got, is a very pleasant bonus.
quotes.author: Edmund Hillary
quotes.source: 1000 Brilliant Achievement Quotes (2004) by David Deford, p. 4

quotes.text: The most useless creature that ever yawned at a club, or counted the vermin on his rags under the suns of Calabria, has no excuse for want of intellect. What men want is not talent, it is purpose,—in other words, not the power to achieve, but the will to labour.
quotes.author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton

quotes.text: What men want is not talent, it is purpose—in other words, not the power to achieve, but the will to labour.
quotes.author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton

quotes.text: Happiness is not a goal, it is a by-product. Paradoxically, the one sure way not to be happy is deliberately to map out a way of life in which one would please oneself completely and exclusively.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt

quotes.text: Life was meant to be lived, and curiosity must be kept alive. One must never, for whatever reason, turn his back on life.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
quotes.source: Preface (December 1960) to The Autobiography of Eleanor Roosevelt (1961), p. xix

quotes.text: The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
quotes.source: Leonard C. Schlup and Donald W. Whisenhunt, It Seems to Me: Selected Letters of Eleanor Roosevelt (2001), p. 2.

quotes.text: The purpose of life... is to live it, to taste experience to the utmost, to reach out eagerly and without fear for newer and richer experience.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt

quotes.text: When you cease to make a contribution, you begin to die.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
quotes.source: Eleanor : The Years Alone (1972) by Joseph P. Lash

quotes.text: When we can't dream any longer we die.
quotes.author: Emma Goldman
quotes.source: Quoted by Margaret C. Anderson in "Emma Goldman in Chicago", Mother Earth magazine (December 1914)

quotes.text: But when did you ever undertake a voyage for the purpose of reviewing your own principles and getting rid of any of them that proved unsound?
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Xciii, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: For what purpose? you may say. Why, that you may become an Olympic conqueror; but it is not accomplished without sweat.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If it should ever happen to you to be turned to externals in order to please some person, you must know that you have lost your purpose in life.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If then you desire (aim at) such great things remember that you must not (attempt to) lay hold of them with a small effort; but you must leave alone some things entirely, and postpone others for the present.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Man, you have forgotten your purpose: you were not travelling to this inn, but you were passing through it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Who are you, and for what purpose did you come into the world?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: It is not possible to run a course aright when the goal itself has not been rightly placed.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text: Let the will embrace the highest ideals freely and with infinite strength, but let action first take hold of what lies closest.
quotes.author: Franz Grillparzer

quotes.text: It's our insides that make us who we are, that allow us to dream and wonder and feel for others. That's what's essential. That's what will always make the biggest difference in our world.
quotes.author: Fred Rogers
quotes.source: Commencement Address at Middlebury College May, 2001

quotes.text: Destination and paths. Many people are obstinate about the path once it is taken, few people about the destination.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.source: Section IX, "Man Alone with Himself" / aphorism 494

quotes.text: What is great in man is that he is a bridge and not a goal.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: Nothing you do for children is ever wasted. They seem not to notice us, hovering, averting our eyes, and they seldom offer thanks, but what we do for them is never wasted.
quotes.author: Garrison Keillor

quotes.text: We may affirm absolutely that nothing great in the world has been accomplished without passion.
quotes.author: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
quotes.source: Lectures on the Philosophy of History (1832).

quotes.text: Our deeds are like children that are born to us; they live and act apart from our own will. Nay, children may be strangled, but deeds never: they have an indestructible life both in and out of our consciousness;
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult for each other?
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: What makes life dreary is the want of motive.
quotes.author: George Eliot
quotes.source: Daniel Deronda (1876), Book VIII, Chapter LXV.

quotes.text: One needs something to believe in, something for which one can have whole-hearted enthusiasm. One needs to feel that one's life has meaning, that one is needed in this world.
quotes.author: Hannah Szenes
quotes.source: Hannah Senesh: Her Life and Diary (1938).

quotes.text: You can live in your dreams, but only if you are worthy of them.
quotes.author: Harlan Ellison

quotes.text: Put personal ambition away from you, and then you will find consolation in living or in dying, whatever may happen to you.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: Without passion man is a mere latent force and possibility, like the flint which awaits the shock of the iron before it can give forth its spark.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: Dreams are the touchstones of our characters.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: "A Week on the Concord and Merrimack Rivers" (1849).

quotes.text: Follow your genius closely enough, and it will not fail to show you a fresh prospect every hour.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: I learned this, at least, by my experiment; that if one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: In the long run men hit only what they aim at.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: It is not enough to be busy. So are the ants. The question is: What are we busy about?
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: in: Jeffrey S Cramer The Quotable Thoreau, Princeton University Press, 11 April 2011, p. 466

quotes.text: Every man is working out his destiny in his own way and nobody can be of any help except by being kind, generous, and patient.
quotes.author: Henry Miller

quotes.text: One’s destination is never a place, but rather a new way of looking at things.
quotes.author: Henry Miller

quotes.text: There is not a heart but has its moments of longing,— yearning for something better, nobler, holier than it knows now.
quotes.author: Henry Ward Beecher
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 15.

quotes.text: Each man had only one genuine vocation — to find the way to himself.
quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.source: Demian: The Story of Emil Sinclair's Youth (1919), first published under the pseudonym "Emil Sinclair"

quotes.text: You must find your dream, then the way becomes easy. But there is no dream that lasts forever, each dream is followed by another, and one should not cling to any particular one.
quotes.author: Hermann Hesse

quotes.text: Doing nothing for others is the undoing of ourselves. We must purposely be kind and generous, or we miss the best part of existence. The heart which goes out of itself gets large and full. This is the great secret of the inner life. We do ourselves the most good doing something for others.
quotes.author: Horace Mann
quotes.source: Thoughts (1901) by Jessie K. Freeman and Sarah S. B. Yule, p. 83, and in Collect Writings of Russell H. Conwell (1925), Vol. 1, p. 396

quotes.text: All that we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.
quotes.author: J. R. R. Tolkien
quotes.source: said by Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Rings

quotes.text: Don't loaf and invite inspiration; light out after it with a club, and if you don't get it you will nonetheless get something that looks remarkably like it.
quotes.author: Jack London
quotes.source: (1876 - 1916) 'Getting into Print', first published in 1903 in The Editor magazine.

quotes.text: A man should conceive of a legitimate purpose in his heart, and set out to accomplish it.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Thought And Purpose

quotes.text: All achievements, whether in the business, intellectual, or spiritual world, are the result of definitely directed thought, are governed by the same law and are of the same method; the only difference lies in the object of attainment.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — The Thought-Factor In Achievement

quotes.text: Having conceived of his purpose, a man should mentally mark out a straight pathway to its achievement, looking neither to the right nor the left.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Thought And Purpose

quotes.text: Men do not attract that which they want, but that which they are. Their whims, fancies, and ambitions are thwarted at every step, but their inmost thoughts and desires are fed with their own food, be it foul or clean.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Circumstances

quotes.text: Those who are not prepared for the apprehension of a great purpose should fix the thoughts upon the faultless performance of their duty, no matter how insignificant their task may appear.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Thought And Purpose

quotes.text: I can but entreat you to remember it is only by preserving faith in human dreams that we may, after all, perhaps some day make them come true.
quotes.author: James Branch Cabell
quotes.source: The Cream of the Jest : A Comedy of Evasions (1917) "Richard Fentnor Harroby" in Ch. 1 : Pallation of the Gambit.

quotes.text: Mishaps are like knives, that either serve us or cut us, as we grasp them by the blade or the handle.
quotes.author: James Russell Lowell

quotes.text: Every individual matters. Every individual has a role to play. Every individual makes a difference.
quotes.author: Jane Goodall

quotes.text: Our destiny is frequently met in the very paths we take to avoid it.
quotes.author: Jean de La Fontaine
quotes.source: Fables Book VIII (1678–1679), Fable 16, The Horoscope

quotes.text: Life has no meaning a priori... It is up to you to give it a meaning, and value is nothing but the meaning that you choose.
quotes.author: Jean-Paul Sartre

quotes.text: Aim at the sun, and you may not reach it; but your arrow will fly far higher than if aimed at an object on a level with yourself.
quotes.author: Joel Hawes
quotes.source: You're Born an Original - Don't Die a Copy (1993) by John Mason.

quotes.text: The problems of the world cannot possibly be solved by skeptics or cynics whose horizons are limited by the obvious realities. We need men who can dream of things that never were and ask "why not?".
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.source: Speech delivered to the Dail (Parliament of Ireland) (28 June 1963)

quotes.text: The mountains are calling and I must go.
quotes.author: John Muir
quotes.source: letter to sister Sarah Muir Galloway (3 September 1873); published in William Federic Badè, The Life and Letters of John Muir (1924), chapter 10: Yose…
