quotes.text: All things have been given to us for a purpose, and an artist must feel this more intensely. All that happens to us, including our humiliations, our misfortunes, our embarrassments, all is given to us as raw material, as clay, so that we may shape our art.
quotes.author: Jorge Luis Borges
quotes.source: Twenty Conversations with Borges, Including a Selection of Poems: Interviews by Roberto Alifano, 1981–1983 (1984)

quotes.text: No, men are not born to know, but they are destined for it.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: The aim of argument, or of discussion, should not be victory, but progress.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: Human life, by its very nature, has to be dedicated to something, an enterprise glorious or humble, a destiny illustrious or trivial. We are faced with a condition, strange but inexorable, involved in our very existence.
quotes.author: José Ortega y Gasset
quotes.source: Chapter XIV: Who Rules The World?

quotes.text: What we really want to do is what we are really meant to do. When we do what we are meant to do, money comes to us, doors open for us, we feel useful, and the work we do feels like play to us.
quotes.author: Julia Cameron

quotes.text: To understand the heart and mind of a person, look not at what he has already achieved, but what he aspires to.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran
quotes.source: reported in Become a Conscious Creator: A Return to Self-Empowerment (2007) by Lisa Ford, p. 44.

quotes.text: The highest of distinctions is service to others.
quotes.author: King George VI
quotes.source: a phrase later adopted by his daughter, Elizabeth II.

quotes.text: A purpose of human life, no matter who is controlling it, is to love whoever is around to be loved.
quotes.author: Kurt Vonnegut

quotes.text: It is easier to be wise for others than for oneself.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: The great souls are not those who have fewer passions and more virtues than common souls, but only those who have nobler plans.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: Giving up something that no longer serves a purpose, or protects you, or helps you, isn’t giving up at all, it’s growing up.
quotes.author: Laurell K. Hamilton

quotes.text: We can ask ourselves daily what we have done to make the world a better place, to make someone smile, to help someone to feel more secure, etc. It's the simple things which have the greatest effect. We must never underestimate the strength of a smile or act of kindness.
quotes.author: Leo Buscaglia
quotes.source: A Magazine of People and Possibilities interview (1998)

quotes.text: The purpose of life is not to be happy at all. It is to be useful, to be honorable. It is to be compassionate. It is to matter, to have it make some difference that you lived.
quotes.author: Leo Rosten
quotes.source: "The Myths by Which We Live", in The Rotarian, Vol. 107, No. 3 (September 1965), p. 55

quotes.text: As soon as the higher ideal is put before us, all false ideals will fade away as the stars fade away when they meet the sun.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: A Calendar of Wisdom, P. Sekirin, trans. (1997)

quotes.text: The vocation of every man and woman is to serve other people.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: What Is To Be Done? (1886) Chap. XL, as translated in The Novels and Other Works of Lyof N. Tolstoï (1902) edited by Nathan Haskell Dole, p. 281

quotes.text: There is only one enduring happiness in life—to live for others.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.text: One of the deep secrets of life is that all that is really worth the doing is what we do for others.
quotes.author: Lewis Carroll
quotes.source: This is a paraphrase of statement in a thank you note from Carroll to a childhood friend, the actress Ellen Terry, published in Ellen Terry, Player in…

quotes.text: The greatest ideal that man can aspire to is not to be a show-case of virtue, but just to be a genial, likable and reasonable human being.
quotes.author: Lin Yutang

quotes.text: The indefatigable pursuit of an unattainable perfection, even though it consist in nothing more than the pounding of an old piano, is what alone gives a meaning to our life on this unavailing star.
quotes.author: Logan Pearsall Smith

quotes.text: The test of a vocation is the love of the drudgery it involves.
quotes.author: Logan Pearsall Smith

quotes.text: Whatever is worth doing at all, is worth doing well.
quotes.author: Lord Chesterfield

quotes.text: High ideals make a people strong.... decay comes when ideals wane.
quotes.author: Louis Sullivan
quotes.source: "Education" (1902), in Kindergarten Chats and Other Writings (New York: George Wittenborn Inc., 1947), pp. 225–226

quotes.text: The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: The Power of Purpose: Find Meaning, Live Longer, Better, p. 35.

quotes.text: One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world.
quotes.author: Malala Yousafzai
quotes.source: Inauguration of Library of Birmingham, Jan 2013

quotes.text: An arrow has one motion and the mind another. Even when pausing, even when weighing conclusions, the mind is moving forward, toward its goal.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: He who does not know what the world is, does not know where he is. And he who does not know for what purpose the world exists, does not know who he is, nor what the world is.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: If you don’t have a consistent goal in life, you can’t live it in a consistent way.”
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Let it make no difference to thee whether thou art cold or warm, if thou art doing thy duty; and whether thou art drowsy or satisfied with sleep; and whether ill-spoken of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Let no act be done without a purpose, nor otherwise than according to the perfect principles of art.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: All journeys have secret destinations of which the traveler is unaware.
quotes.author: Martin Buber
quotes.source: The Legend of the Baal-Shem (1955),1995 edition, p. 36

quotes.text: You know I am not born to tread in the beaten track — the peculiar bent of my nature pushes me on.
quotes.author: Mary Wollstonecraft

quotes.text: Every day of our lives we are on the verge of making those changes that would make all the difference.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: Nature forms us for ourselves, not for others; to be, not to seem.
quotes.author: Montaigne
quotes.source: Book II, Ch. 37. Of the Resemblance of Children to their Brothers

quotes.text: There is as much difference between us and ourselves as between us and others.
quotes.author: Montaigne
quotes.source: Ch. 1. Of the Inconstancy of Our Actions (tr. Cotton, rev. W. Carew Hazlitt, 1877)

quotes.text: A fundamental concern for others in our individual and community lives would go a long way in making the world the better place we so passionately dreamt of.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Nelson Mandela on selflessness, Kliptown, Soweto, South Africa (12 July 2008). Source: From Nelson Mandela By Himself: The Authorised Book of Quotatio…

quotes.text: Everyone can rise above their circumstances and achieve success if they are dedicated to and passionate about what they do.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Nelson Mandela on determination, From a letter to Makhaya Ntini on his 100th Cricket Test (17 December 2009). Source: From Nelson Mandela By Himself…

quotes.text: We tried in our simple way to lead our life in a manner that may make a difference to those of others.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Nelson Mandela on freedom fighters, Upon Receiving the Roosevelt Freedom Award (8 June 2002). Source: From Nelson Mandela By Himself: The Authorised B…

quotes.text: What counts in life is not the mere fact that we have lived. It is what difference we have made to the lives of others that will determine the significance of the life we lead.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela
quotes.source: Nelson Mandela on life, 90th Birthday celebration of Walter Sisulu, Walter Sisulu Hall, Randburg, Johannesburg, South Africa (18 May 2002). Source: Fr…

quotes.text: Happiness will never come if it's a goal in itself; happiness is a by-product of a commitment to worthy causes.
quotes.author: Norman Vincent Peale
quotes.source: The Power of Positive Living (1992), p. 63

quotes.text: All at once life takes on a higher and nobler meaning, and we are fired with a desire to do more than we have ever before done, and to be more than we have been in the past.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVI

quotes.text: Bestir yourself; get the cobwebs out of your head; brush off the brain ash. Think, think, think to some purpose!
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Do not let the thorns which appear in every vocation, or temporary despondency or disappointment, shake your purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: Don't let the maxims of a low prudence daily dinned into your ears lower the tone of your high ambition or check your aspirations.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every bit of help, of encouragement, of support you give to this other self will add to the magnificence, the splendor of your destiny.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every man and woman can exercise this virtue of perseverance, can refuse to stop short of the goal of ambition, can decline to turn aside in search of pleasures that do but hinder progress.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIV

quotes.text: Every man must play the part of his ambition.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: Find your purpose and fling your life out to it. Try to be somebody with all your might.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Great tenacity of purpose is the only thing that will carry you over the hard places which appear in every career to ultimate triumph.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: If the aim be right the life in its details cannot be far wrong. Your heart must inspire what your hands execute, or the work will be poorly done.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If you hold to your vision and are honest, earnest and true, there is nothing that can stand in the way of its realization.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If your vocation be only a humble one, elevate it with more manhood than others put into it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter X

quotes.text: In fact it is doubtful whether a man can perform very great service to mankind who is not permeated with a great purpose—with an overmastering idea.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVI

quotes.text: It is a great purpose which gives meaning to life; it unifies all our powers, binds them together in one cable and makes strong and united what was weak, separated, scattered.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: It is continuity of purpose alone that achieves results.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the one-sided man, the sharp-eyed man, the man of single and intense purpose, the man of one idea, who cuts his way through obstacles and forges to the front.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: It is very stimulating to be with people whose aspirations run parallel with your own.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXV

quotes.text: Life is not given for mourning, but for unselfish service.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Most men have ability enough, if they could only focalize it into one grand, central, all-absorbing purpose, to accomplish great things.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Nothing can take the place of an all-absorbing purpose; education can not, genius can not, talent can not, industry can not, will-power can not.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: One could almost say that no life ever failed that was steadfastly devoted to one aim, if that aim were not in itself unworthy.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Our conduct should show that we are on this earth to play a magnificent part in life's drama, to make a splendid contribution to humanity.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Pure grit is that element of character which enables a man to clutch his aim with an iron grip, and keep the needle of his purpose pointing to the star of his hope.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: So man never points steadily in any direction until he has been polarized by a great master purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: The fact that a person believes implicitly that he can do what may seem impossible to others, shows there is something within him that has gotten a glimpse of power sufficient to accomplish his purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The giants of the race have been men of concentration, who have struck sledgehammer blows in one place until they have accomplished their purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: The great danger in our time is not lack of chance or opportunity but of losing our vision, of letting our ambition die.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The great thing is to be a man, to have a high purpose, a noble aim, to be dead in earnest, to yearn for the good and the true.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The highest happiness is the feeling of wellbeing which comes to one who is actively employed doing what he was made to do, carrying out the great life-purpose patterned in his individual bent.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: The ideals must be kept bright and the ambition clean-cut.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIX

quotes.text: The indomitable will, the inflexible purpose, will find a way or make one.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: The man without a purpose never leaves his mark upon the world.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: The more completely we master a vocation the more thoroughly we enjoy it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The only question with him is how to push ahead, to get a little farther along, a little nearer his goal.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The successful men of to-day are men of one overmastering idea, one unwavering aim, men of single and intense purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: The voice, the dress, the look, the very motions of a person, define and alter when he or she begins to live for a reason.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: There is no doubt that every human being comes to this earth with a mission.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is no fate or destiny which puts one man down and another up.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: There is no grander sight in the world than that of a young man fired with a great purpose, dominated by one unwavering aim.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: There is no road to success but through a clear, strong purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There was no turning to the right nor to the left; no dreaming away time, nor building air-castles; but one look and purpose, forward, upward and onward, straight to his goal.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIX

quotes.text: To get the most from your reading you must read with a purpose. To sit down and pick up a book listlessly, with no aim except to pass away time, is demoralizing.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXII

quotes.text: We are our own Fates. We control our own destiny.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: We can do the most possible for ourselves when we are in a position where we can do the most possible for others.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: We need aspiration and great thought-models to lift us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We rise or fall by our ideals, by our pursuit or our disregard of them.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What we admire and aspire to enters into the very texture of our being, becomes a part of us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Whatever you do in life, be greater than your calling.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter X

quotes.text: Whatever your vocation, let quality be your life-slogan.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXII

quotes.text: You cannot long fight successfully against your aspirations.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter X

quotes.text: You like to take things easy. Nobody ever amounts to much who lets his energies flag, his standards droop and his ambition ooze out.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Young men are often told to aim high, but we must aim at what we would hit. A general purpose is not enough.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: The unexamined life is not worth living for a human being.
quotes.author: Plato

quotes.text: Glory ought to be the consequence, not the motive, of our actions; and although it happen not to attend the worthy deed, yet it is by no means the less fair for having missed the applause it deserved.
quotes.author: Pliny

quotes.text: Don't turn back when you are just at the goal.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: A man cannot bury his meanings so deep in his book but time and like-minded men will find them.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: All things ascend, and the royal rule of economy is, that it should ascend also, or, whatever we do must always have a higher aim.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: Each man has his own vocation. The talent is the call.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: If you would serve your brother, because it is fit for you to serve him, do not take back your words when you find that prudent people do not commend you.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: It is easy to live for others; everybody does. I call on you to live for yourselves.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Let not the tie be mercenary, though the service is measured by money. Make yourself necessary to somebody.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: One way is right to go: the hero sees it, and moves on that aim, and has the world under him for root and support.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: Our chief want in life, is, somebody who shall make us do what we can. This is the service of a friend.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The difference between talents and character is adroitness to keep the old and trodden round, and power and courage to make a new road to new and better goals.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The lightning-rod that disarms the cloud of its threat is his body in its duty. A high aim reacts on the means, on the days, on the organs of the body.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The passion rebuilds the world for the youth. It makes all things alive and significant.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We aim above the mark to hit the mark. Every act hath some falsehood of exaggeration in it.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We are all wise. The difference between persons is not in wisdom but in art.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We can lift ourselves out of ignorance, we can find ourselves as creatures of excellence and intelligence and skill.
quotes.author: Richard Bach

quotes.text: The worthwhile problems are the ones you can really solve or help solve, the ones you can really contribute something to... . No problem is too small or too trivial if we can really do something about it.
quotes.author: Richard Feynman

quotes.text: We should employ our passions in the service of life, not spend life in the service of our passions.
quotes.author: Richard Steele
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 442.

quotes.text: Always fall in with what you're asked to accept. Take what is given, and make it over your way. My aim in life has always been to hold my own with whatever's going. Not against: with.
quotes.author: Robert Frost

quotes.text: A man can only achieve strength of purpose by the action of his own freewill.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: And whoever strives to do his duty faithfully is fulfilling the purpose for which he was created, and building up in himself the principles of a manly character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Every one can make his own destiny—every one employ his life nobly.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: For it is not the calling that degrades the man, but the man that degrades the calling.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Hence it is that, inspired by energy of purpose, men of comparatively mediocre powers have often been enabled to accomplish such extraordinary results.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is not then how much a man may know, that is of importance, but the end and purpose for which he knows it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is therefore advisable for young men to seek the fellowship of the good, and always to aim at a higher standard than themselves.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is will,—force of purpose,—that enables a man to do or be whatever he sets his mind on being or doing.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Let a man give the reins to his impulses and passions, and from that moment he yields up his moral freedom.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Let it be your ambition to be foremost in all duty.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Man cannot aspire if he look down; if he will rise, he must look up.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men of genuine excellence, in every station of life—men of industry, of integrity, of high principle, of sterling honesty of purpose—command the spontaneous homage of mankind.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men who have raised themselves from a humble calling, need not be ashamed, but rather ought to be proud of the difficulties they have surmounted.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Practical wisdom, for the purposes of life, must be carried about with us, and be ready for use at call.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Simple honesty of purpose in a man goes a long way in life, if founded on a just estimate of himself and a steady obedience to the rule he knows and feels to be right.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The desire must ripen into purpose and effort; and one energetic attempt is worth a thousand aspirations.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The good purpose once formed must be carried out with alacrity and without swerving.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The most profitable study is that which is conducted with a definite aim and object.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We must be satisfied to work with a purpose, and wait the results with patience.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: What most stands in the way of the performance of duty, is irresolution, weakness of purpose, and indecision.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Nobody grows old merely by a number of years. We grow old by deserting our ideals. Years may wrinkle the skin, but to give up enthusiasm wrinkles the soul.
quotes.author: Samuel Ullman

quotes.text: An expedition will be incomplete if one stops half-way, or anywhere on this side of one’s destination; but life is not incomplete if it is honourable.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 77 (On Taking One’S Own Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: And I am indeed confident that you cannot be warped, that you will stick to your purpose, even though the crowd may surround and seek to distract you.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 32 (On Progress), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: He who has attained wisdom has reached, not the furthermost, but the most important, goal.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 93 (On The Quality, As Contrasted With The Length, Of Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Is it for this purpose that we are strong,—that we may have light burdens to bear?
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 78 (On The Healing Power Of The Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Our plans miscarry because they have no aim. When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 71 (On The Supreme Good), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Our words should aim not to please, but to help.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 75 (On The Diseases Of The Soul), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The same act may be either shameful or honourable: the purpose and the manner make all the difference.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 95 (On The Usefulness Of Basic Principles), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The wise man’s purpose in conducting his life is not to accomplish at all hazards what he tries, but to do all things rightly; the pilot’s purpose, however, is to bring his ship into port at all hazards.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 85 (On Some Vain Syllogisms), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There are only a few who control themselves and their affairs by a guiding purpose; the rest do not proceed; they are merely swept along, like objects afloat in a river.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 23 (On The True Joy Which Comes From Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is, in my opinion, this difference between renown and glory—the latter depends upon the judgments of the many; but renown on the judgments of good men.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 102 (On The Intimations Of Our Immortality), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We must make it our aim already to have lived long enough.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 23 (On The True Joy Which Comes From Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You should look, not to the source from which these things come, but to the goal towards which they tend.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 44 (On Philosophy And Pedigrees), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The great rule of life is to have no schemes but one unalterable purpose.
quotes.author: Sri Aurobindo
quotes.source: Nahar, S., Aurobindo, ., & Institut de recherches évolutives (Paris). India's rebirth: A selection from Sri Aurobindo's writing, talks and speeches. P…

quotes.text: He who studies without passion will never become anything more than a pedant. We must approach knowledge from the inside; inspired by passion.
quotes.author: Stefan Zweig
quotes.source: Confusion of Feelings or Confusion: The Private Papers of Privy Councillor R. Von D (1927)

quotes.text: It is never until one realizes that one means something to others that one feels there is any point or purpose in one's own existence.
quotes.author: Stefan Zweig

quotes.text: Life is futile unless it be directed towards a definite goal.
quotes.author: Stefan Zweig
quotes.source: Twenty-Four Hours in the Life of a Woman (1927)

quotes.text: Take up an idea, devote yourself to it, struggle on in patience, and the sun will rise for you.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: The meaning of life is if something that you did made something better.
quotes.author: Temple Grandin
quotes.source: "Temple Grandin Wants Us to Think Differently About Kids Who Think Differently" Interview, New York Times (January 22, 2022)

quotes.text: Dream and deed are not as different as many think. All the deeds of men are dreams at first, and become dreams in the end.
quotes.author: Theodor Herzl
quotes.source: The Israelis : Founders and Sons (1971) by Amos Elon, p. 57

quotes.text: A man is worthless unless he has in him a lofty devotion to an ideal, and he is worthless also unless he strives to realize this ideal by practical methods.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Promise And Performance

quotes.text: It is far better, for instance, to do well a bit of work which is well worth doing, than to have a large fortune.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: The work may be done in a thousand different ways—with the brain or the hands, in the study, the field, or the workshop—if it is honest work, honestly done and well worth doing, that is all we have a right to ask.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: There is no good reason why we should fear the future, but there is every reason why we should face it seriously, neither hiding from ourselves the gravity of the problems before us nor fearing to approach these problems with the unbending, unflinching purpose to solve them aright.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: In a valiant suffering for others, not in a slothful making others suffer for us, did nobleness ever lie.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: Love is our true destiny. We do not find the meaning of life by ourselves alone — we find it with another.
quotes.author: Thomas Merton
quotes.source: Love and Living (1979) Part One : Love and Living, p. 27

quotes.text: People are meant to go through life two by two. 'Tain't natural to be lonesome.
quotes.author: Thornton Wilder

quotes.text: There is nothing in the world, I venture to say, that would so effectively help one to survive even the worst conditions, as the knowledge that there is a meaning in one’s life.
quotes.author: Viktor Frankl
quotes.source: p. 126 in the 1984 Pocket Books edition

quotes.text: Ultimately, man should not ask what the meaning of his life is, but rather must recognize that it is he who is asked. In a word, each man is questioned by life; and he can only answer to life by answering for his own life; to life he can only respond by being responsible.
quotes.author: Viktor Frankl

quotes.text: What man actually needs is not a tensionless state but rather the striving and struggling for some goal worthy of him. What he needs is not the discharge of tension at any cost, but the call of a potential meaning waiting to be fulfilled by him.
quotes.author: Viktor Frankl

quotes.text: The real test of a man is not how well he plays the role he has invented for himself, but how well he plays the role that destiny assigned to him.
quotes.author: Václav Havel
quotes.source: Ch. 2 : Writing for the Stage, p. 72

quotes.text: The tragedy of modern man is not that he knows less and less about the meaning of his own life, but that it bothers him less and less.
quotes.author: Václav Havel

quotes.text: A person should set his goals as early as he can and devote all his energy and talent to getting there. With enough effort, he may achieve it. Or he may find something that is even more rewarding. But in the end, no matter what the outcome, he will know he has been alive.
quotes.author: Walt Disney
quotes.source: Walt Disney, Magician of the Movies (1966) by Bob Thomas p. 116

quotes.text: The isness of things is well worth studying; but it is their whyness that makes life worth living.
quotes.author: William Beebe

quotes.text: But men of great purpose and noble ideals must know that the path of the reformer is loneliness.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Calmness is singleness of purpose, absolute confidence, and conscious power,—ready to be focused in an instant to meet any crisis.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Consecration is dedicating the individual life to the service of others, to some noble mission, to realizing some unselfish ideal.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Hurry is a counterfeit of haste. Haste has an ideal, a distinct aim to be realized by the quickest, direct methods.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If we are facing some great life ambition let us see if our heroic plans are good, high, noble and exalted enough for the price we must pay for their attainment.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: If you are seeking to accomplish any great serious purpose that your mind and your heart tell you is right, you must have the spirit of the reformer.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: In their hurry to attain some ambition, to gratify the dream of a life, men often throw honor, truth, and generosity to the winds.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Life is worth living if it be lived in a way that is worth living.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: The reformers of the world are its men of mighty purpose.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: There is no honest and true work, carried along with constant and sincere purpose that ever really fails.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Trifles unnoted by us may be links in the chain of some great purpose.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: We never see the target a man aims at in life; we see only the target he hits.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: We should not be merely an influence,—we should be an inspiration. By our very presence we should be a tower of strength to the hungering human souls around us.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: We should realize the right of every human soul to work out its own destiny, with our aid, our sympathy, our inspiration, if we are thus privileged to help him to live his life; but it is intolerance to try to live it for him.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Worry is the traitor in our camp that dampens our powder, weakens our aim.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: Correspondence with Helen Keller, 1908, in The Correspondence of William James: April 1908–August 1910, Vol. 12, Charlottesville: University of Virgin…

quotes.text: This life is worth living, we can say, since it is what we make it, from the moral point of view.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: Destiny is not a matter of chance; it is a matter of choice. It is not a thing to be waited for; it is a thing to be achieved.
quotes.author: William Jennings Bryan
quotes.source: "America's Mission", a speech delivered by the leader of the Democratic Party at the Washington Day banquet given by the Virginia Democratic Associati…

quotes.text: It is a mistake to look too far ahead. Only one link in the chain of destiny can be handled at a time.
quotes.author: Winston Churchill
quotes.source: Speech in the House of Commons, February 27, 1945 "Crimea Conference"; in The Second World War, Volume VI: Triumph and Tragedy (1954), Chapter XXIII –…

quotes.text: Go so far as you can see and when you get there you will always be able to see farther.... as you head toward your goals, be prepared to make some slight adjustments to your course. You don't change your decision to go — you do change your direction to get there.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar
quotes.source: p. 164; Variant: When obstacles arise, you change your direction to reach your goal; you do not change your decision to get there.

quotes.text: Outstanding people have one thing in common: an absolute sense of mission.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar
quotes.source: Created for Excellence : 12 keys to Godly Success (1996) by Kevin Baerg, p. 25

quotes.text: What you get by achieving your goals is not as important as what you become by achieving your goals.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar
quotes.source: Secrets of Superstar Speakers: Wisdom from the Greatest Motivators of Our Time (2000) by Lilly Walters, p. 96

quotes.text: The one thing that is more dangerous than true ignorance is the illusion of understanding.
quotes.author: A. C. Grayling

quotes.text: Life for delays and doubts no time does give, None ever yet made haste enough to live.
quotes.author: Abraham Cowley

quotes.text: Truth is generally the best vindication against slander.
quotes.author: Abraham Lincoln
quotes.source: Letter to Edwin Stanton (14 July 1864); published in Abraham Lincoln: A History (1890) by John Hay

quotes.text: Human nature is not nearly as bad as it has been thought to be... In fact it can be said that the possibilities of human nature have customarily been sold short.
quotes.author: Abraham Maslow
quotes.source: Toward a Psychology of Being (New York: Simon and Schuster, 1962), p. 5

quotes.text: What is necessary to change a person is to change his awareness of himself.
quotes.author: Abraham Maslow
quotes.source: Life in the Open Sea‎ (1972) by William M. Stephens, p. 21

quotes.text: Life, too, is like that. You live it forward, but understand it backward.
quotes.author: Abraham Verghese

quotes.text: It is thrifty to prepare today for the wants of tomorrow.
quotes.author: Aesop

quotes.text: Although I am a typical loner in my daily life, my awareness of belonging to the invisible community of those who strive for truth, beauty, and justice has prevented me from feelings of isolation.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: Whoever is careless with truth in small matters cannot be trusted in important affairs.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: Albert Einstein: Historical and Cultural Perspectives by Gerald James Holton, Yehuda Elkana p. 388

quotes.text: We think in generalities, but we live in detail.
quotes.author: Alfred North Whitehead
quotes.source: "The Education of an Englishman", in The Atlantic Monthly, Vol. 138 (1926), p. 192

quotes.text: Perhaps it is possible to discover more in silence than in speech. Or perhaps it is only that those who are silent among us learn to listen.
quotes.author: Alice Hoffman

quotes.text: Mindfulness is not chasing the moment but beautifying the moment.
quotes.author: Amit Ray
quotes.source: Mindfulness Living in the Moment - Living in the Breath (2015)

quotes.text: If fifty million people say a foolish thing, it is still a foolish thing.
quotes.author: Anatole France
quotes.source: Listening and Speaking: A Guide to Effective Oral Communication (1954) by Ralph G. Nichols and Thomas R. Lewis, p. 74

quotes.text: It is well for the heart to be naive and for the mind not to be.
quotes.author: Anatole France

quotes.text: Introspection is a devouring monster. You have to feed it with much material, much experience, many people, many places, many loves, many creations, and then it ceases feeding on you.
quotes.author: Anaïs Nin
quotes.source: (April 1936), in The Diary of Anais Nin: 1934–1939, edited by Gunther Stuhlmann (San Diego: Harcourt Brace & Company, 1967), p. 81

quotes.text: People can tell you to keep your mouth shut, but it doesn't stop you having your own opinions. Even if people are still very young, they shouldn't be prevented from saying what they think.
quotes.author: Anne Frank

quotes.text: There are no events but thoughts and the heart's hard turning, the heart's slow learning where to love and whom. The rest is merely gossip, and tales for other times.
quotes.author: Annie Dillard

quotes.text: A rock pile ceases to be a rock pile the moment a single man contemplates it, bearing within him the image of a cathedral.
quotes.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
quotes.source: Pilote de Guerre (1942) (translated into English as Flight to Arras)

quotes.text: Here is my secret. It is very simple: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.
quotes.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

quotes.text: Only during hard times do people come to understand how difficult it is to be master of their feelings and thoughts.
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.text: There should be more sincerity and heart in human relations, more silence and simplicity in our interactions. Be rude when you’re angry, laugh when something is funny, and answer when you’re asked.
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.source: Letter to his brother, A.P. Chekhov (October 13, 1888)

quotes.text: We never think entirely alone; we think in company, in a vast collaboration; we work with the workers of the past and of the present.
quotes.author: Antonin Sertillanges
quotes.source: The Intellectual Life (1920), translated by Mary Ryan. Cork: The Mercier Press, 1948, p. 106

quotes.text: Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom.
quotes.author: Aristotle

quotes.text: All I urge is that a life in which conduct does not fairly well accord with principles is a silly life; and that conduct can only be made to accord with principles by means of daily examination, reflection, and resolution.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — The Reflective Mood

quotes.text: But not reading of books will take the place of a daily, candid, honest examination of what one has recently done, and what one is about to do—of a steady looking at one's self in the face (disconcerting though the sight may be).
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — The Reflective Mood

quotes.text: I am entirely convinced that what is more than anything else lacking in the life of the average well-intentioned man of to-day is the reflective mood.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — The Reflective Mood

quotes.text: If my typical man wishes to live fully and completely he must, in his mind, arrange a day within a day.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — The Cause Of The Troubles

quotes.text: The wise should adapt themselves to the present, even when the past seems more attractive
quotes.author: Baltasar Gracián

quotes.text: No man can teach another self-knowledge. He can only lead him or her up to self-discovery - the source of truth.
quotes.author: Barry Long
quotes.source: Knowing Yourself: The True in the False (Barry Long Books, 1996).

quotes.text: Truth cannot be taught but it is quickly recognized by the person ready to discover it.
quotes.author: Barry Long
quotes.source: Knowing Yourself: The True in the False (Barry Long Books, 1996).

quotes.text: A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.
quotes.author: Baruch Spinoza

quotes.text: Observe all men; thy self most.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin

quotes.text: Perfect solitude is when, for a whole day, no human eye has beheld your face.
quotes.author: Berthold Auerbach
quotes.source: On the Heights (1865), trans. Simon Adler Stern. New York: Henry Holt and Company, 1907, p. 622

quotes.text: To understand the actual world as it is, not as we should wish it to be, is the beginning of wisdom.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.text: The first thought is often the best.
quotes.author: Bishop Butler
quotes.source: Sermon on the Character of Balaam, Seventh Sermon; Reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 787-90

quotes.text: Man is but a reed, the weakest in nature, but he is a thinking reed.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal
quotes.source: Thoughts, Chapter II. 10; Reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 787-90

quotes.text: One must know oneself. If this does not serve to discover truth, it at least serves as a rule of life, and there is nothing better.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: We know the truth, not only by the reason, but also by the heart.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: The change is from inner to outer. — We start by dissolving our attitude not by altering outer conditions.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee

quotes.text: It is the integrity of each individual human that is in final examination.
quotes.author: Buckminster Fuller

quotes.text: People should think things out fresh and not just accept conventional terms and the conventional way of doing things.
quotes.author: Buckminster Fuller
quotes.source: The Peter Plan: A Proposal for Survival (1977) by Laurence J. Peter

quotes.text: Thinking is a momentary dismissal of irrelevancies.
quotes.author: Buckminster Fuller
quotes.source: Utopia or Oblivion : The Prospects of Humanity (1969)

quotes.text: And he who lives a hundred years, ignorant and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is wise and reflecting.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter VIII. The Thousands, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought, which is difficult to guard, difficult to hold back.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter III. Thought, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Earnest among the thoughtless, awake among the sleepers, the wise man advances like a racer, leaving behind the hack.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter II. On Earnestness, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: If a man would hasten towards the good, he should keep his thought away from evil; if a man does what is good slothfully, his mind delights in evil.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter IX. Evil, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Let a wise man blow off the impurities of his self, as a smith blows off the impurities of silver one by one, little by little, and from time to time.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XVIII. Impurity, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Let him not despise what he has received, nor ever envy others: a mendicant who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XXV. The Bhikshu (Mendicant), trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter III. Thought, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Make an island of yourself, make yourself your refuge; there is no other refuge. Make truth your island, make truth your refuge; there is no other refuge.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter V. The Fool, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: The wise who control their body, who control their tongue, the wise who control their mind, are indeed well controlled.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XVII. Anger, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: There is no fear for one whose mind is not filled with desires.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter VI. The Wise Man (Pandita), trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: You shouldn't chase after the past or place expectations on the future. What is past is left behind. The future is as yet unreached. Whatever quality is present you clearly see right there, right there.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Bhaddekaratta Sutta: An Auspicious Day, MN 131, (1997) translated from the Pali by Thanissaro Bhikkhu

quotes.text: All mortals tend to turn into the thing they are pretending to be.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis

quotes.text: Love may forgive all infirmities and love still in spite of them: but Love cannot cease to will their removal.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis

quotes.text: We live, in fact, in a world starved for solitude, silence, and privacy: and therefore starved for meditation and true friendship.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis

quotes.text: Don't judge the future of a person based on his present conditions, because time has the power to change black coal to shiny diamond.
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.text: A problem thoroughly understood is always fairly simple. Found your opinions on facts, not prejudices. We know too many things that are not true.
quotes.author: Charles Kettering
quotes.source: Dynamic Work Simplification (1971) by W. Clements Zinck, p. 122

quotes.text: If you wish to be like a little child, study what a little child could understand — nature; and do what a little child could do — love.
quotes.author: Charles Kingsley
quotes.source: notes of August 1842, published in Charles Kingsley : His Letters and Memories of His Life (1883) edited by Frances Eliza Grenfell Kingsley, p. 65.

quotes.text: What I would say is the single most important thing, if you want to avoid all the stupid errors, is knowing where you're competent and where you aren't. And that's very hard to do because the human mind naturally tries to make you think you're way smarter than you are.
quotes.author: Charlie Munger

quotes.text: Don't disparage the day that still has an hour of light in its hand.
quotes.author: Chinua Achebe

quotes.text: But still anger ought be far from us, for nothing is able to be done rightly nor judiciously with anger.
quotes.author: Cicero
quotes.source: Variant: In anger nothing right nor judicious can be done.

quotes.text: Peace is liberty in tranquillity.
quotes.author: Cicero
quotes.source: Living by the Fruit of the Spirit, p. 39

quotes.text: The pursuit, even of the best things, ought to be calm and tranquil.
quotes.author: Cicero
quotes.source: Living Like Benjamin: Making Dreams Come True, (1 November 2007), p. 143

quotes.text: We think a happy life consists in tranquility of mind.
quotes.author: Cicero

quotes.text: Man has three ways of acting wisely. First, on meditation; that is the noblest. Secondly, on imitation; that is the easiest. Thirdly, on experience; that is the bitterest.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: The Analects, as reported in Chambers Dictionary of Quotations (1997), p. 279

quotes.text: The more man meditates upon good thoughts, the better will be his world and the world at large.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Attributed to Confucius in Out of the Blue: Delight Comes Into Our Lives (1996) by Mark Victor Hansen, Barbara Nichols, and Patty Hansen, p. 93

quotes.text: The superior man examines his heart, that there may be nothing wrong there, and that he may have no cause for dissatisfaction with himself. That wherein the superior man cannot be equaled is simply this — his work which other men cannot see.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Analects / The Doctrine of the Mean

quotes.text: To know that we know what we know, and that we do not know what we do not know, that is true knowledge.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Walden (1854) by Henry David Thoreau, Ch. 1

quotes.text: When we see men of worth, we should think of equaling them; when we see men of a contrary character, we should turn inwards and examine ourselves.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: Only the development of compassion and understanding for others can bring us the tranquility and happiness we all seek.
quotes.author: Dalai Lama
quotes.source: Be Happy Now: Simple Steps for Enjoying Life, (27 March 2012), p. 96

quotes.text: Time is always moving on; nothing can stop it. We can’t change the past, but we can shape the future. The more compassionate you are, the more you will find inner peace.
quotes.author: Dalai Lama
quotes.source: Official twitter page of the Office of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. Tweet from 8. April 2019 11:30 am. Archived from the original on March 10, 20…

quotes.text: You must never run away from the truth, Jake, however unpleasant. Because once you begin running, you can never stop.
quotes.author: Dale Bailey
quotes.source: The Resurrection Man's Legacy, originally published in Fantasy & Science Fiction (July 1995); reprinted in Nebula Awards 31, p. 161

quotes.text: In a very real sense we have two minds, one that thinks and one that feels. These two fundamentally different ways of knowing interact to construct our mental life.
quotes.author: Daniel Goleman

quotes.text: The great secret that all old people share is that you really haven't changed in seventy or eighty years. Your body changes, but you don't change at all. And that, of course, causes great confusion.
quotes.author: Doris Lessing

quotes.text: A moment of danger can bring about a temporary cessation of the stream of thinking and thus give you a taste of what it means to be present, alert, aware.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: All that you ever have to deal with, cope with, in real life—as opposed to imaginary mind projections—is this moment. Ask yourself what “problem” you have right now, not next year, tomorrow, or five minutes from now. What is wrong with this moment?
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Be present as the watcher of your mind.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Do not give all your attention away to the mind and the external world. By all means focus on what you are doing, but feel the inner body at the same time whenever possible.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Even a brief illness or an accident can show you what is real and unreal in your life, what ultimately matters and what doesn't.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Happiness depends on conditions being perceived as positive; inner peace does not.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: It is easy to stay present as the observer of your mind when you are deeply rooted within your body. No matter what happens on the outside, nothing can shake you anymore.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Make it your practice to withdraw attention from past and future whenever they are not needed. Step out of the time dimension as much as possible in everyday life.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Most people don't know how to listen because the major part of their attention is taken up by thinking. They pay more attention to that than to what the other person is saying
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: The primary cause of unhappiness is never the situation but your thoughts about it. Be aware of the thoughts you are thinking. Separate them from the situation, which is always neutral. There is the situation or the fact, and here are my thoughts about it. Life isn't as serious as the mind makes it out to be.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle
quotes.source: Oneness With All Life: Inspirational Selections from A New Earth (2008)

quotes.text: To bring your attention to a stone, a tree, or an animal does not mean to think about it, but simply to perceive it, to hold it in your awareness.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: When you know you are not at peace, your knowing creates a still space that surrounds your nonpeace in a loving and tender embrace and then transmutes your nonpeace into peace.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: When you lose touch with inner stillness, you lose touch with yourself.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Whenever you are able to observe your mind, you are no longer trapped in it. Another factor has come in, something that is not of the mind: the witnessing presence.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: You cannot pay attention to silence without simultaneously becoming still within.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.
quotes.author: Edsger W. Dijkstra
quotes.source: How do we tell truths that might hurt? (1975).

quotes.text: The heart loves repose and the soul contemplation, but the mind needs action.
quotes.author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton

quotes.text: Thought is valuable in proportion as it is generative.
quotes.author: Edward Bulwer-Lytton
quotes.source: Caxtoniana, Essay XIV; Reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 787-90

quotes.text: Love is so exquisitely elusive. It cannot be bought, cannot be badgered, cannot be hijacked. It is available only in one rare form: as the natural response of a healthy mind and healthy heart.
quotes.author: Eknath Easwaran

quotes.text: I think if I worked for a man, I would work for him. I would not work for him a part of his time, but all of his time.
quotes.author: Elbert Hubbard

quotes.text: Your friend is that man who knows all about you, and still likes you.
quotes.author: Elbert Hubbard

quotes.text: It isn't enough to talk about peace. One must believe in it. And it isn't enough to believe in it. One must work at it.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt

quotes.text: Just as man cannot live without dreams, he cannot live without hope. If dreams reflect the past, hope summons the future.
quotes.author: Elie Wiesel

quotes.text: And it is good for you to know your own preparation and power, that in those matters where you have not been prepared, you may keep quiet, and not be vexed, if others have the advantage over you.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Count the cost—and then, if your desire still holds, try the wrestler’s life.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Civ, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: Examine a little at last, look around, stir yourself up, that you may know who you are.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Having these things (or thoughts) always in hand, and exercising them by yourself, and keeping them in readiness, you will never be in want of one to comfort you and strengthen you.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If then you attempt to avoid only the things contrary to nature which are within your power you will not be involved in any of the things which you would avoid.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If these things are true; and if we are not stupid or insincere when we say that the good or ill of man lies within his own will, and that all beside is nothing to us, why are we still troubled? Why do we still fear?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: In our power are our thinking, our intentions, our desires, our decisions.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Let death and exile and every other thing which appears dreadful be daily before your eyes; but most of all death: and you will never think of anything mean nor will you desire anything extravagantly.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Let silence be your general rule; or say only what is necessary and in few words.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Clxiv, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: Now the things within our power are by nature free, unrestricted, unhindered; but those beyond our power are weak, dependent, restricted, alien.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — I, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Reflect that the chief source of all evils to Man, and of baseness and cowardice, is not death, but the fear of death.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Cxxxv, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: The beginning of philosophy is to know the condition of one’s own mind. If a man recognises that this is in a weakly state, he will not then want to apply it to questions of the greatest moment.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Xlvi, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: This is why the ancients taught the maxim, Know thyself. Therefore we ought to exercise ourselves in small things, and beginning with them to proceed to the greater.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Whereas Socrates used to say that we should never lead a life not subjected to examination.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Xlvii, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: With some people solitariness is an escape not from others but from themselves. For they see in the eyes of others only a reflection of themselves.
quotes.author: Eric Hoffer

quotes.text: There is one thing alone that stands the brunt of life throughout its course: a quiet conscience.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.text: The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function.
quotes.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

quotes.text: The one self-knowledge worth having is to know one’s own mind.
quotes.author: Francis Herbert Bradley

quotes.text: When a wise man does not understand, he says: "I do not understand." The fool and the uncultured are ashamed of their ignorance. They remain silent when a question could bring them wisdom.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: Be sincere, be brief, be seated.
quotes.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
quotes.source: Advice to his son James on how to make a public speech, as quoted in Basic Public Speaking (1963) by Paul L. Soper, p. 12

quotes.text: We shall strive for perfection. We shall not achieve it immediately — but we still shall strive. We may make mistakes — but they must never be mistakes which result from faintness of heart or abandonment of moral principle.
quotes.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt

quotes.text: I tell you: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: My formula for the greatness of a human being is amor fati: that one wants nothing to be different—not forward, not backward, not in all eternity. Not merely to bear what is necessary, still less conceal it... but love it.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.source: "Why I Am So Clever," § 2.10, cited in Kauffman, Nietzsche, p. 283

quotes.text: What destroys a man more quickly than to work, think, and feel without inner necessity, without any deep personal desire, without pleasure — as a mere automaton of “duty.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: Silence is always beautiful, and a silent person is always more beautiful than one who talks.
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.text: Some luck lies in not getting what you thought you wanted but getting what you have, which once you have got it you may be smart enough to see is what you would have wanted had you known.
quotes.author: Garrison Keillor

quotes.text: Life is not measured by the time we live.
quotes.author: George Crabbe

quotes.text: More helpful than all wisdom is one draught of simple human pity that will not forsake us.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: A tragic situation exists precisely when virtue does not triumph but when it is still felt that man is nobler than the forces which destroy him.
quotes.author: George Orwell

quotes.text: A thinking man's greatest happiness is to have fathomed what can be fathomed and to revere in silence what cannot be fathomed.
quotes.author: Goethe

quotes.text: Art is long, life short; judgment difficult, opportunity transient.
quotes.author: Goethe

quotes.text: Talent develops in tranquility, character in the full current of human life.
quotes.author: Goethe
quotes.source: Quote Unquote (A Handbook of Quotations), p. 74

quotes.text: Toleration is the greatest gift of the mind; it requires the same effort of the brain that it takes to balance oneself on a bicycle.
quotes.author: Helen Keller

quotes.text: Order means light and peace, inward liberty and free command over one’s self; order is power.
quotes.author: Henri-Frédéric Amiel

quotes.text: A man thinking or working is always alone, let him be where he will. Solitude is not measured by the miles of space that intervene between a man and his fellows.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: All change is a miracle to contemplate; but it is a miracle which is taking place every instant.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: In accumulating property for ourselves or our posterity, in founding a family or a state, or acquiring fame even, we are mortal; but in dealing with truth we are immortal, and need fear no change nor accident.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: It takes two to speak the truth — one to speak, and another to hear.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: A Week on the Concord and Merrimack Rivers.

quotes.text: Nay, be a Columbus to whole new continents and worlds within you, opening new channels, not of trade, but of thought.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Our life is frittered away by detail.... Simplicity, simplicity, simplicity! I say, let your affairs be as two or three, and not a hundred or a thousand; instead of a million count half a dozen, and keep your accounts on your thumb-nail.... Simplify, simplify.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: Walden (1854), Ch. 2 : Where I Lived, and What I Lived For.

quotes.text: So our human life but dies down to its root, and still puts forth its green blade to eternity.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: The man who goes alone can start today; but he who travels with another must wait till that other is ready, and it may be a long time before they get off.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: The only obligation which I have a right to assume, is to do at any time what I think right.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: Walden (1854) — On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience

quotes.text: We may not arrive at our port within a calculable period, but we would preserve the true course.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: When we are unhurried and wise, we perceive that only great and worthy things have any permanent and absolute existence,—that petty fears and petty pleasures are but the shadow of the reality.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Who looks in the sun will see no light else; but also he will see no shadow. Our life revolves unceasingly, but the centre is ever the same, and the wise will regard only the seasons of the soul.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: With thinking we may be beside ourselves in a sane sense. By a conscious effort of the mind we can stand aloof from actions and their consequences; and all things, good and bad, go by us like a torrent.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Every artist dips his brush in his own soul and paints his own nature into his picture.
quotes.author: Henry Ward Beecher

quotes.text: Self is the only prison that can ever bind the soul.
quotes.author: Henry van Dyke

quotes.text: For why do you hasten to remove things that hurt your eyes, but if anything gnaws your mind, defer the time of curing it from year to year?
quotes.author: Horace
quotes.source: Book I, epistle ii, lines 37–39; translation by C. Smart

quotes.text: If any man seeks for greatness, let him forget greatness and ask for truth, and he will find both.
quotes.author: Horace Mann

quotes.text: Truth is ever to be found in simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things.
quotes.author: Isaac Newton
quotes.source: Cited in Rules for methodizing the Apocalypse, Rule 9, from a manuscript published in The Religion of Isaac Newton (1974) by Frank E. Manuel, p. 120…

quotes.text: A man does not come to the almshouse or the jail by the tyranny of fate or circumstance, but by the pathway of grovelling thoughts and base desires.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Circumstances

quotes.text: Change of diet will not help a man who will not change his thoughts.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Health And The Body

quotes.text: Every thought-seed sown or allowed to fall into the mind, and to take root there, produces its own, blossoming sooner or later into act, and bearing its own fruitage of opportunity and circumstance.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Circumstances

quotes.text: If you would renew your body, beautify your mind. Thoughts of malice, envy, disappointment, despondency, rob the body of its health and grace.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Health And The Body

quotes.text: The outer world of circumstance shapes itself to the inner world of thought, and both pleasant and unpleasant external conditions are factors, which make for the ultimate good of the individual.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Effect Of Thought On Circumstances

quotes.text: You cannot travel within and stand still without.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — Visions And Ideals

quotes.text: The search for the truth is the most important work in the whole world — and the most dangerous.
quotes.author: James Clavell
quotes.source: his screenplay The Fly (1958), based on the short story by George Langelaan.

quotes.text: Let's not look back in anger or forward in fear, but around in awareness.
quotes.author: James Thurber

quotes.text: So, a man who is really earnest must begin with himself, he must be passively aware of all his thoughts, feelings and actions. Again, this is not a matter of time. There is no end to self-knowledge. Self-knowledge is only from moment to moment, and therefore there is a creative happiness from moment to moment.
quotes.author: Jiddu Krishnamurti
quotes.source: New Delhi India 1st Public Talk (14 November 1948)

quotes.text: You can look only when the mind is completely quiet.
quotes.author: Jiddu Krishnamurti
quotes.source: 2nd Public Talk, Amsterdam, The Netherlands (12 May 1968)

quotes.text: The discovery of truth by slow progressive meditation is wisdom. Intuition of truth, not preceded by perceptible meditation, is genius.
quotes.author: Johann Kaspar Lavater

quotes.text: Peace is a daily, a weekly, a monthly process, gradually changing opinions, slowly eroding old barriers, quietly building new structures. And however undramatic the pursuit of peace, that pursuit must go on.
quotes.author: John F. Kennedy
quotes.source: his Address to the United Nations General Assembly (20 September 1963)

quotes.text: If you wish to know someone, you need only observe that on which he bestows his care, and what sides of his own nature he cultivates.
quotes.author: John Kessel
quotes.source: Events Preceding the Helvetican Renaissance (2009) in Gardner Dozois & Jonathan Strahan (eds.) The New Space Opera 2 (mass market paperback edition, )…

quotes.text: We may avoid much disappointment and bitterness of soul by learning to understand how little necessary to our joy and peace are the things the multitude most desire and seek.
quotes.author: John Lancaster Spalding

quotes.text: We may not have chosen the time, but the time has chosen us.
quotes.author: John Lewis
quotes.source: on the (March 2010), quoted by Speaker Nancy Pelosi in her closing remarks. See: Christopher Beam (March 21, 2010): It’s Been Real: Scenes from the Ca…

quotes.text: Truth is as impossible to be soiled by any outward touch as the sunbeam.
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.text: Keep close to Nature's heart... and break clear away, once in a while, and climb a mountain or spend a week in the woods. Wash your spirit clean.
quotes.author: John Muir
quotes.source: statement by Muir as remembered by Samuel Hall Young in Alaska Days with John Muir (1915), chapter 7

quotes.text: Only by going alone in silence, without baggage, can one truly get into the heart of the wilderness. All other travel is mere dust and hotels and baggage and chatter.
quotes.author: John Muir
quotes.source: letter to wife Louie (Louisa Wanda Strentzel) (July 1888); published in William Federic Badè, The Life and Letters of John Muir (1924), chapter 15: Wi…

quotes.text: Take a course of good water and air, and in the eternal youth of Nature you may renew your own. Go quietly, alone; no harm will befall you.
quotes.author: John Muir
quotes.source: "Mount Shasta" in Picturesque California (1888-1890) page 165; reprinted in Steep Trails (1918), chapter 5

quotes.text: He who has the truth at his heart need never fear the want of persuasion on his tongue.
quotes.author: John Ruskin

quotes.text: Success is peace of mind attained only through self-satisfaction and knowing you’ve made the effort, do the best of what you’re capable.
quotes.author: John Wooden

quotes.text: The best way to capture moments is to pay attention. This is how we cultivate mindfulness. Mindfulness means being awake. It means knowing what you are doing.
quotes.author: Jon Kabat-Zinn
quotes.source: Wherever You Go, There You Are: Mindfulness Meditation in Everyday Life (2005)

quotes.text: My attitude was always to keep open, to keep scanning. I think that's how things work in nature. Many people are close-minded, rigid, and that's not my inclination.
quotes.author: Jonas Salk

quotes.text: A wise man is never less alone than when he is alone.
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift
quotes.source: Essay on the Faculties of the Mind

quotes.text: It is better to be concerned with being than with nothingness. Dream therefore of what you still have rather than what you have lost.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: The breath of the mind is attention.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: The mind can only create errors. Truths are not created, they exist; one can only see them, disentangle them, discover them, and expose them.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: To seek wisdom rather than truth. It is more within our grasp.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: We are afraid of having and showing a small mind and we are not afraid of having and showing a small heart.
quotes.author: Joseph Joubert

quotes.text: The excellent man is he who condemns what he finds in his mind without previous effort, and only accepts as worthy of him what is still far above him and what requires a further effort in order to be reached.
quotes.author: José Ortega y Gasset
quotes.source: The Revolt of the Masses (1929), p. 63

quotes.text: Man struggles to find life outside himself, unaware that the life he is seeking is within him.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Reason is like an open secret that can become known to anyone at any time; it is the quiet space into which everyone can enter through his own thought.
quotes.author: Karl Jaspers
quotes.source: Philosophy for a Time of Crisis : An Interpretation, with Key Writings by Fifteen Great Modern Thinkers (1959) by Adrienne Koch, Ch. 18, "Karl Jaspers…

quotes.text: Everyone speaks well of his heart; no one dares speak well of his mind.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: The finest achievement for a man of thought is to have fathomed what may be fathomed, and quietly to revere the unfathomable.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: Wisdom is to the soul what health is to the body.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: Silence is a source of great strength.
quotes.author: Lao Tzu

quotes.text: Solitude is the best nurse of wisdom.
quotes.author: Laurence Sterne

quotes.text: The first rule of achieving goodness is this: think only about self-perfection.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: A Calendar of Wisdom, P. Sekirin, trans. (1997).

quotes.text: The water you touch in a river is the last of that which has passed, and the first of that which is coming. Thus it is with time present.
quotes.author: Leonardo da Vinci
quotes.source: The Notebooks of Leonardo Da Vinci (1938), XIX Philosophical Maxims. Morals. Polemics and Speculations., as translated by Edward MacCurdy

quotes.text: He who knows himself properly can very soon learn to know all other men. It is all reflection.
quotes.author: Lichtenberg

quotes.text: A man may own a thousand acres of land, and yet he still sleeps upon a bed of five feet.
quotes.author: Lin Yutang

quotes.text: Be a master everywhere and wherever you stand is your true place.
quotes.author: Linji Yixuan

quotes.text: All things will be clear and distinct to the man who does not hurry; haste is blind and improvident.
quotes.author: Livy

quotes.text: But if one should guide his life by true principles, man's greatest riches is to live on a little with contented mind; for a little is never lacking.
quotes.author: Lucretius

quotes.text: A man of truth must also be a man of care.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi

quotes.text: The only tyrant I accept in this world is the "still small voice" within me. And even though I have to face the prospect of being a minority of one, I humbly believe I have the courage to be in such a hopeless minority.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Young India (2 March 1922). Quoted in The Essential Gandhi: An Anthology of His Writings on His Life, Work, and Ideas edited by Louis Fischer (2002)…

quotes.text: We but mirror the world. All the tendencies present in the outer world are to be found in the world of our body. If we could change ourselves, the tendencies in the world would also change.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
