quotes.source: an article on dealing with snake bites, published in Indian Opinion dated August 9th, 1913, in the Gujarti language edition, English translation avail…

quotes.text: Accept the truth from whatever source it comes.
quotes.author: Maimonides
quotes.source: Introduction to the Shemonah Peraqim, as quoted in Truth and Compassion: Essays on Judaism and Religion in Memory of Rabbi Dr. Solomon Frank (1983) Ed…

quotes.text: Silence is a fence around wisdom.
quotes.author: Maimonides

quotes.text: Anyway, you think for yourself. And if a man can’t do that, he isn’t really thinking.
quotes.author: Manly Wade Wellman

quotes.text: About pain: the pain which is intolerable carries us off; but that which lasts a long time is tolerable; and the mind maintains its own tranquillity by retiring into itself, and the ruling faculty is not made worse.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Adapt yourself to the environment in which your lot has been cast, and show true love to the fellow-mortals with whom destiny has surrounded you.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Consider in what condition both in body and soul a man should be when he is overtaken by death; and consider the shortness of life, the boundless abyss of time past and future, the feebleness of all matter.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Do not think that what is hard for you to master is humanly impossible; but if a thing is humanly possible, consider it to be within your reach.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Everywhere and at all times it is in thy power piously to acquiesce in thy present condition, and to behave, justly to those who are about thee, and to exert thy skill upon thy present thoughts, that nothing shall steal into them without being well examined.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: For the present is the only thing of which a man can be deprived, if it is true that this is the only thing which he has, and that a man cannot lose a thing if he has it not.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: It is in your power to withdraw yourself whenever you desire. Perfect tranquility within consists in the good ordering of the mind, the realm of your own.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Treasures of love & inspiration Galahad Books, 1993, p. 278

quotes.text: Nothing has such power to broaden the mind as the ability to investigate systematically and truly all that comes under thy observation in life.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Pain is either an evil to the body—then let the body say what it thinks of it—or to the soul; but it is in the power of the soul to maintain its own serenity and tranquillity, and not to think that pain is an evil.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Remember that man lives only in the present, in this fleeting instant; all the rest of his life is either past and gone, or not yet revealed. Short, therefore, is man's life, and narrow is the corner of the earth wherein he dwells.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The rational principle which rules has this nature, that it is content with itself when it does what is just, and so secures tranquillity.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The safety of life is this, to examine everything all through, what it is itself, that is its material, what the formal part; with all thy soul to do justice and to say the truth.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The things you think about determine the quality of your mind. Your soul takes on the color of your thoughts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts.

quotes.text: Those who do not observe the movements of their own minds must of necessity be unhappy.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Through not observing what is in the mind of another a man has seldom been seen to be unhappy; but those who do not observe the movements of their own minds must of necessity be unhappy.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Throwing away then all things, hold to these only which are few; and besides, bear in mind that every man lives only this present time, which is an indivisible point, and that all the rest of his life is either past or it is uncertain.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: To change your mind and to follow him who sets you right is to be nonetheless the free agent that you were before.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Remember that to change thy opinion and to follow him who corrects thy error is as consistent with freedom as it is to persist in thy error. (Long tra…

quotes.text: To live your brief life rightly, isn't that enough?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: To understand the true quality of people, you must look into their minds, and examine their pursuits and aversions.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Meditations, book 4, section 38 (trans. by Jeremy Collier).

quotes.text: What then will it be when it forms a judgment about anything aided by reason and deliberately? Therefore the mind which is free from passions is a citadel, for man has nothing more secure to which he can fly for refuge and for the future be inexpugnable.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: When thou art offended at any man's fault, forthwith turn to thyself and reflect in what like manner thou dost err thyself; for example, in thinking that money is a good thing, or pleasure, or a bit of reputation, and the like.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The very secret of life for me, I believed, was to maintain in the midst of rushing events an inner tranquility.
quotes.author: Margaret Bourke-White
quotes.source: Written by Herself: Autobiographies of American women, (1992)

quotes.text: Truth is the most valuable thing we have. Let us economize it.
quotes.author: Mark Twain

quotes.text: Whenever you find yourself on the side of the majority, it is time to pause and reflect.
quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.source: Mark Twain (2016). “The Wit and Wisdom of Mark Twain”, p.97, Chartwell

quotes.text: Solitude is the place of purification.
quotes.author: Martin Buber
quotes.source: I and Thou (1923), trans. Ronald Gregor Smith. London: Bloomsbury, 2013, p. 72

quotes.text: In the end, we will remember not the words of our enemies but the silence of our friends.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.source: The Trumpet of Conscience, Steeler Lecture, November 1967.

quotes.text: One day we must come to see that peace is not merely a distant goal that we seek, but that it is a means by which we arrive at that goal. We must pursue peaceful ends through peaceful means.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.source: Beverly Hills California, (February 25, 1967); as quoted in “Martin Luther King Jr. On the Vietnam War", The Atlantic.

quotes.text: The time is always right to do what’s right.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.source: at a speech delivered in Finney Chapel at Oberlin College (October. 22, 1964), as reported in "When MLK came to Oberlin" by Cindy Leise (The Chronicle…

quotes.text: Go placidly amid the noise and haste, and remember what peace there may be in silence.
quotes.author: Max Ehrmann

quotes.text: Loneliness is the poverty of the self; solitude is the richness of the self.
quotes.author: May Sarton
quotes.source: Mrs. Stevens Hears the Mermaids Singing (New York: W. W. Norton & Company, 1965), p. 183

quotes.text: Learn to know thyself, it shall profit thee more than any craft.
quotes.author: Meister Eckhart

quotes.text: Nothing is more useful than silence.
quotes.author: Menander

quotes.text: The envious man is an enemy to himself, for his mind is always spontaneously occupied with its own unhappy thoughts.
quotes.author: Menander

quotes.text: He who exerts his mind to the utmost knows his nature.
quotes.author: Mencius
quotes.source: 7A:1, as translated by Wing-tsit Chan in A Source Book in Chinese Philosophy (1963), p. 62

quotes.text: When you are angry, it means you, yourself are unhappy. Even if you are wronged, you are still making yourself unhappy if you feel anger.
quotes.author: Michio Kushi

quotes.text: How strange that the young should always think the world is against them when in fact that is the only time it is for them.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: Make it thy business to know thyself, which is the most difficult lesson in the world.
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.text: Time ripens all things. No man is born wise.
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes
quotes.source: Don Quixote de la Mancha (1605–1615), chapter 33. Note: "Time ripens all things" is the translator's interpolation and does not appear in the original…

quotes.text: Only in solitude do we find ourselves, and in finding ourselves, we find in ourselves all our brothers in solitude.
quotes.author: Miguel de Unamuno
quotes.source: "Solitude", Essays and Soliloquies (1924), tr. J. E. Crawford Flitch

quotes.text: When you learn how to die, you learn how to live.
quotes.author: Mitch Albom

quotes.text: Walk around feeling like a leaf. Know you could tumble any second. Then decide what to do with your time.
quotes.author: Naomi Shihab Nye
quotes.source: Everything Comes Next: Collected and New Poems (2020)

quotes.text: If you want to make peace with your enemy, you have to work with your enemy. Then he becomes your partner.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

quotes.text: The mind is sharper and keener in seclusion and uninterrupted solitude. No big laboratory is needed in which to think. Originality thrives in seclusion free of outside influences beating upon us to cripple the creative mind. Be alone, that is the secret of invention; be alone, that is when ideas are born.
quotes.author: Nikola Tesla
quotes.source: Nikola Tesla's Life & Work by István G. Kocsis, (2015).

quotes.text: All that is required to feel that here and now is happiness is a simple, frugal heart.
quotes.author: Nikos Kazantzakis

quotes.text: Change your thoughts and you can change the world.
quotes.author: Norman Vincent Peale
quotes.source: Back on Track : How to Straighten Out Your Life When It Throws You a Curve (1997) by Deborah Norville, p. 201

quotes.text: I never think about what I want. It's about what you want to give to other people.
quotes.author: Oprah Winfrey
quotes.source: The Money Adventure (1998) by Egbert Sukop, p. 128

quotes.text: All the forces in nature that are the most powerful are the quietest.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every lesson in school or college is an opportunity. Every examination is a chance in life.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter I

quotes.text: How many a man can trace his downfall in life to the failure to seize his opportunity at the favorable moment, when it was within easy grasp, the nick of time, which often does not present itself but once!
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVIII

quotes.text: It is the mind that makes the body rich. No man is rich, however much money or land he may possess, who has a poor heart.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXVI

quotes.text: Love is the great mind opener, the great heart opener and life-enricher, the great developer.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Nothing in the universe is static. None of us stands still.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The attitude of mind which your thoughts and convictions produce is a real force which builds or tears down.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The days come to us like friends in disguise, bringing priceless gifts from an unseen hand; but, if we do not use them, they are borne silently away, never to return.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter VI

quotes.text: The heart must be educated to be tender, sympathetic, and true.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter X

quotes.text: The majority of people do not see things; they just look at them. The power of keen observation is indicative of a superior mentality; for it is the mind, not the optic nerve, that really sees.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIX

quotes.text: The power that makes our desire, our vision, a reality is not in our environment or in any condition outside of us; it is within us.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The present time is the raw material out of which we make whatever we will.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter VI

quotes.text: The sense of fatigue is one of Nature's many signals of danger. All we accomplish by stimulating or crowding the body or mind when tired is worse than lost.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLVI

quotes.text: The simple truth is that a will strong enough to keep a man continually striving for things not wholly beyond his powers will carry him in time very far toward his chosen goal.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The unattained still beckons us toward the summit of life's mountains, into the atmosphere where great souls live and breathe and have their being.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The whole secret of a richly stored mind is alertness, sharp, keen attention, and thoughtfulness.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIX

quotes.text: Thinking, contemplating what we have read, is what digestion and assimilation are to the food.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXII

quotes.text: We are too impatient to listen. Instead of being attentive and eager to drink in the story or the information, we have not enough respect for the talker to keep quiet.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVII

quotes.text: We must change our thought before we can change our conditions.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We ought to think upward, then we would reach the heights where superiority dwells. The man whose mind is set firmly toward achievement does not appropriate success, he is success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: We should early form the habit of erasing from the mind all disagreeable, unhealthy, death-dealing thoughts.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: We think so much about what others have and spend so much time wondering why we cannot have similar things that we do not see the beauty, loveliness and sweetness in our own environment.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We try to grasp too much of life at once; since we think of it as a whole, instead of living one day at a time.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What the world wants is young men who will amass golden thoughts, golden wisdom, golden deeds, not mere golden dollars; young men who prefer to have thought-capital, character-capital, to cash-capital.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Whatever we hold in our minds, dwell upon, contemplate, whatever is dominant in our motives, will stand out in our flesh so that the world can read it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You cannot use any ability until you think, until you believe, you can. Your reserve power will stand in the background until your self-faith calls it into action.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is through introspection that we obtain the self-knowledge allowing us to bring positive change to our lives. By engaging in it, you will be able to see when it is not the world that needs to reform but yourself.
quotes.author: P. M. Forni
quotes.source: The Thinking Life: How to Thrive in the Age of Distraction, Macmillan, 13 September 2011, p. 48.

quotes.text: Our language has wisely sensed the two sides of being alone. It has created the word loneliness to express the pain of being alone. And it has created the word solitude to express the glory of being alone.
quotes.author: Paul Tillich
quotes.source: The Eternal Now (New York: Scribner, 1963), p. 11

quotes.text: The person who tries to live alone will not succeed as a human being. His heart withers if it does not answer another heart. His mind shrinks away if he hears only the echoes of his own thoughts and finds no other inspiration.
quotes.author: Pearl S. Buck

quotes.text: Meditation is an invitation to notice when we reach our limit and to not get carried away by hope and fear.
quotes.author: Pema Chödrön
quotes.source: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

quotes.text: Through meditation, we’re able to see clearly what’s going on with our thoughts and emotions, and we can also let them go.
quotes.author: Pema Chödrön
quotes.source: When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times (1997)

quotes.text: Be ruled by time, the wisest counsellor of all.
quotes.author: Pericles

quotes.text: You, therefore, if you seek ever to have quiet minds before the last day, follow the few and not the crowd.
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.text: Remember what Simonides said,—that he never repented that he had held his tongue, but often that he had spoken.
quotes.author: Plutarch
quotes.source: Morals, Volume I. Rules for the Preservation of Health.

quotes.text: The truth is so lovable that it has only to be known to be embraced.
quotes.author: Plutarch
quotes.source: as quoted by ** David Allyn Gorton, The History of Medicine, Philosophical and Critical (1910) Vol. 1

quotes.text: If thou wouldest be a wise man, and one sitting in council with his overlord, apply thine heart unto perfection. Silence is more profitable unto thee than abundance of speech.
quotes.author: Ptahhotep
quotes.source: The Instruction of Ptah-Hotep, trans. Battiscombe Gunn (1906)

quotes.text: He who lives in solitude may make his own laws.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus
quotes.source: Moral Sayings (1st century B.C.), tr. Darius Lyman (1856), #432

quotes.text: Let your life lightly dance on the edges of Time like dew on the tip of a leaf.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: The truth comes as conqueror only because we have lost the art of receiving it as guest.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore
quotes.source: The Fourfold Way of India (1924); this has become paraphrased as "Truth comes as conqueror only to those who have lost the art of receiving it as frie…

quotes.text: Make your ego porous. Will is of little importance, complaining is nothing, fame is nothing. Openness, patience, receptivity, solitude is everything.
quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.source: Sunbeams : A Book of Quotations (1990) by Sy Safransky, p. 42

quotes.text: A thrill passes through all men at the reception of new truth, or at the performance of a great action, which comes out of the heart of nature.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Be a gift and a benediction. Shine with real light and not with the borrowed reflection of gifts.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Each mind has its own method. A true man never acquires after college rules.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: How a man's truth comes to mind, long after we have forgotten all his words! How it comes to us in silent hours, that truth is our only armor in all passages of life and death!
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: If you act you show character; if you sit still, if you sleep, you show it.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: In these hours the mind seems so great that nothing can be taken from us that seems much. All loss, all pain, is particular; the universe remains to the heart unhurt.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Let us be poised, and wise, and our own, today.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nature transcends all our moods of thought, and its secret we do not yet find.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself. Nothing can bring you peace but the triumph of principles.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nothing is more simple than greatness; indeed, to be simple is to be great.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Other men are lenses, through which we read our own minds.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: “Uses of Great Men,” Representative Men (London: George Routledge & Co., 1850), p. 3.

quotes.text: Silence is a solvent that destroys personality, and gives us leave to be great and universal.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The core will come to the surface. Strong will and keen perception overpower old manners, and create new; and the thought of the present moment has a greater value than all the past.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The nobler the truth or sentiment, the less imports the question of authorship.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Letters and Social Aims (1876), Quotation and Originality.

quotes.text: The revelation of thought takes men out of servitude into freedom.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Conduct of Life, Fate; Reported in Hoyt's New Cyclopedia Of Practical Quotations (1922), p. 787-90

quotes.text: The rich mind lies in the sun and sleeps, and is Nature. To think is to act.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The soul is the perceiver and revealer of truth.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The soul is the perceiver and revealer of truth. We know truth when we see it, let skeptic and scoffer say what they choose.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The wise workman will not regret the poverty or the solitude which brought out his working talents.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Thoughts come into our minds by avenues which we never left open, and thoughts go out of our minds through avenues which we never voluntarily opened.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: What your heart thinks great is great. The soul’s emphasis is always right.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: When the act of reflection takes place in the mind, when we look at ourselves in the light of thought, we discover that our life is embosomed in beauty.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The best gift an educator can give is to get someone to become self-reflective.
quotes.author: Randy Pausch

quotes.text: Time is all you have and you may find one day that you have less than you think.
quotes.author: Randy Pausch
quotes.source: The Last Lecture (2008), expanded and revised publication version of his last lecture

quotes.text: If you would be a real seeker after truth, you must at least once in your life doubt, as far as possible, all things.
quotes.author: René Descartes

quotes.text: If your happiness depends on what somebody else does, I guess you do have a problem.
quotes.author: Richard Bach
quotes.source: Illusions : The Adventures of a Reluctant Messiah (1977)

quotes.text: I have often had occasion to observe, that a warm blundering man does more for the world than a frigid wise man.
quotes.author: Richard Cecil
quotes.source: reported in Josiah Hotchkiss Gilbert, Dictionary of Burning Words of Brilliant Writers (1895), p. 394

quotes.text: If you cannot examine your thoughts, you have no choice but to think them, however silly they may be.
quotes.author: Richard Mitchell
quotes.source: Less Than Words Can Say (1979), Ch. 15

quotes.text: Life is short, but the years are long.
quotes.author: Robert A. Heinlein
quotes.source: Part of the secret "call and response" codewords by which members of the long-lived Howard Families can identify others

quotes.text: Be aware of wonder. Live a balanced life - learn some and think some and draw and paint and sing and dance and play and work every day some.
quotes.author: Robert Fulghum
quotes.source: quoted by Jan Swanson, Alan Cooper in A Physician's Guide to Coping with Death and Dying p. 221.

quotes.text: The present is the child, and the necessary child, of all the past, and the mother of all the future.
quotes.author: Robert G. Ingersoll
quotes.source: How To Reform Mankind (1896), chapter I

quotes.text: The land is the real teacher. All we need as students is mindfulness.
quotes.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer

quotes.text: Many of the faults you see in others, dear reader, are your own nature reflected in them.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: When you see anyone complaining of such and such a person's ill-nature and bad temper, know that the complainant is bad-tempered, forasmuch as he speaks ill of that bad-tempered person, because he alone is good-tempered who is quietly forbearing towards the bad-tempered and ill-natured.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: You'll never get mixed up if you simply tell the truth. Then you don't have to remember what you have said, and you never forget what you have said.
quotes.author: Sam Rayburn
quotes.source: private conversation; in W. B. Ragsdale, "An Old Friend Writes of Rayburn", U.S. News & World Report (October 23, 1961), p. 72.

quotes.text: A desire for knowledge is the natural feeling of mankind; and every human being, whose mind is not debauched, will be willing to give all he has to get knowledge.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: A fly, Sir, may sting a stately horse and make him wince; but one is but an insect, and the other is a horse still.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: Learn that the present hour alone is man's.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: To let friendship die away by negligence and silence, is certainly not wise. It is voluntarily to throw away one of the greatest comforts of this weary pilgrimage.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: A man's manner, to a certain extent, indicates his character. It is the external exponent of his inner nature.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: And such usually is human life to each of us; it is, for the most part, but the reflection of ourselves.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: At the same time, life will always be to a large extent what we ourselves make it. Each mind makes its own little world.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Childhood is like a mirror, which reflects in after-life the images first presented to it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Contact with others is also requisite to enable a man to know himself.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Every action, every thought, every feeling, contributes to the education of the temper, the habits, and understanding; and exercises an inevitable influence upon all the acts of our future life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: For it is mind, soul, and heart—not taste or art—that make men great.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Frugality is not only the basis of quiet, but of beneficence.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: I believe that with simple industry and careful exactness in the utilization of our energies, we never had a fairer chance nor a brighter prospect than the present.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It still oftener happens, that the worry we subject ourselves to, has its source in our own imagination.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Nor will the wise man expect too much from those about him. If he would live at peace with others, he will bear and forbear.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The book is a living voice. It is an intellect to which one still listens.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The golden words that good men have uttered, the examples they have set, live through all time: they pass into the thoughts and hearts of their successors, help them on the road of life, and often console them in the hour of death.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The truest politeness comes of sincerity. It must be the outcome of the heart, or it will make no lasting impression; for no amount of polish can dispense with truthfulness.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Time was the estate out of which these great workers, and all other workers, formed that rich treasury of thoughts and deeds which they have left to their successors.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: While, in a large-natured man, solitude will make the pure heart purer, in the small-natured man it will only serve to make the hard heart still harder: for though solitude may be the nurse of great spirits, it is the torment of small ones.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: And yet time is the one loan which even a grateful recipient cannot repay.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 1 (On Saving Time), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Believe me, a great part of those we have loved, though chance has removed their persons, still abides with us.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 99 (On Consolation To The Bereaved), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Believe me, those who seem to be busied with nothing are busied with the greater tasks; they are dealing at the same time with things mortal and things immortal.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 8 (On The Philosopher’S Seclusion), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Besides, an event which in its entirety is of brief compass cannot contain long intervals. The time which we spend in living is but a point, nay, even less than a point.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 49 (On The Shortness Of Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Cast away everything of that sort, if you are wise; nay, rather that you may be wise; strive toward a sound mind at top speed and with your whole strength.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 17 (On Philosophy And Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Countless cases occur to my mind of men who think that what they themselves are unable to do is impossible, who maintain that we utter words which are too big for man’s nature to carry out.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 104 (On Care Of Health And Peace Of Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Examine yourself; scrutinize and observe yourself in divers ways; but mark, before all else, whether it is in philosophy or merely in life itself that you have made progress.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 16 (On Philosophy, The Guide Of Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Hence, the wise man accustoms himself to coming trouble, lightening by long reflection the evils which others lighten by long endurance.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 76 (On Learning Wisdom In Old Age), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: How long I am to exist is not mine to decide, but how long I shall go on existing in my present way is in my own control.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 93 (On The Quality, As Contrasted With The Length, Of Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: In the first place, you cannot lack them; because nature demands but little, and the wise man suits his needs to nature.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 17 (On Philosophy And Riches), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: In this sense the wise man is self-sufficient, that he can do without friends, not that he desires to do without them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 9 (On Philosophy And Friendship), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: It is one thing to understand the merits and the values of facts, another thing to know the precise moment for action, and still another to curb impulses and to proceed, instead of rushing, toward what is to be done.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 89 (On The Parts Of Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: It is peace of mind, and lasting tranquillity. This will be yours if you possess greatness of soul; it will be yours if you possess the steadfastness that resolutely clings to a good judgment just reached.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 92 (On The Happy Life), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Let us therefore so set our minds in order that we may desire whatever is demanded of us by circumstances, and above all that we may reflect upon our end without sadness.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 61 (On Meeting Death Cheerfully), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Lies are thin stuff; they are transparent, if you examine them with care.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 79 (On The Rewards Of Scientific Discovery), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Now is it not madness, Lucilius, for none of us to reflect that he is mortal?
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 114 (On Style As A Mirror Of Character), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Now is the time for you to reflect, not only that all things are mortal, but also that their mortality is subject to no fixed law.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 63 (On Grief For Lost Friends), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: One who daily puts the finishing touches to his life is never in want of time. And yet, from this want arise fear and a craving for the future which eats away the mind.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 101 (On The Futility Of Planning Ahead), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Ponder for a long time whether you shall admit a given person to your friendship; but when you have decided to admit him, welcome him with all your heart and soul.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 3 (On True And False Friendship), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Press on, therefore, as you have begun; perhaps you will be led to perfection, or to a point which you alone understand is still short of perfection.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium (Moral Letters to Lucilius) / Letter XX: On practicing what you preach

quotes.text: Rather let the soul be roused from its sleep and be prodded, and let it be reminded that nature has prescribed very little for us.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 20 (On Practising What You Preach), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Spite of all do you still chafe and complain, not understanding that, in all the evils to which you refer, there is really only one—the fact that you do chafe and complain?
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 96 (On Facing Hardships), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The deep flood of time will roll over us; some few great men will raise their heads above it, and, though destined at the last to depart into the same realms of silence, will battle against oblivion and maintain their ground for long.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 21 (On The Renown Which My Writings Will Bring You), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The mind of the wise man is like the ultra-lunar firmament; eternal calm pervades that region.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 59 (On Pleasure And Joy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The place where one lives, however, can contribute little towards tranquillity; it is the mind which must make everything agreeable to itself.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 55 (On Vatia’S Villa), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The primary indication, to my thinking, of a well-ordered mind is a man’s ability to remain in one place and linger in his own company.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 2 (On Discursiveness In Reading), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There are many external things which compass us about, to deceive us or to weigh upon us; there are many things within which, even amid solitude, fret and ferment.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 82 (On The Natural Fear Of Death), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Virtue is divided into two parts—into contemplation of truth, and conduct.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We are indeed uplifted merely by meeting wise men; and one can be helped by a great man even when he is silent.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We mortals have been endowed with sufficient strength by nature, if only we use this strength, if only we concentrate our powers and rouse them all to help us or at least not to hinder us.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 116 (On Self-Control), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We must see to it that nothing shall come upon us unforeseen. And since things are all the more serious when they are unfamiliar, continual reflection will give you the power, no matter what the evil may be, not to play the unschooled boy.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 107 (On Obedience To The Universal Will), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should be living within too narrow limits if anything were barred to our thoughts.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 55 (On Vatia’S Villa), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should be sensible, and our wants more reasonable, if each of us were to take stock of himself, and to measure his bodily needs also, and understand how little he can consume, and for how short a time!
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 114 (On Style As A Mirror Of Character), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should therefore reflect upon all contingencies, and should fortify our minds against the evils which may possibly come.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 91, trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: What man can you show me who places any value on his time, who reckons the worth of each day, who understands that he is dying daily?
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 1 (On Saving Time), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Whatever can happen at any time can happen today.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium (Moral Letters to Lucilius) / Letter LXIII

quotes.text: Wisdom is the perfect good of the human mind; philosophy is the love of wisdom, and the endeavour to attain it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 89 (On The Parts Of Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You must be not only present in the body, but watchful in mind, if you would avail yourself of the fleeting opportunity.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 22 (On The Futility Of Half-Way Measures), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You must drink quickly as from a rapid stream that will not always flow.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: You must linger among a limited number of master-thinkers, and digest their works, if you would derive ideas which shall win firm hold in your mind.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 2 (On Discursiveness In Reading), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 28 (On Travel As A Cure For Discontent), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You need not look about for the reward of a just deed; a just deed in itself offers a still greater return.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 113 (On The Vitality Of The Soul And Its Attributes), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You see where the true happiness lies, but you have not the courage to attain it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 21 (On The Renown Which My Writings Will Bring You), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Your good fortune is not to need good fortune.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: We must have beginner's mind, free from possessing anything, a mind that knows everything is in flowing change. Nothing exists but momentarily in its present form and color. One thing flows into another and cannot be grasped.
quotes.author: Shunryu Suzuki
quotes.source: Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970) / Zen Mind

quotes.text: The capacity to give one's attention to a sufferer is a very rare and difficult thing; it is almost a miracle; it is a miracle. Nearly all those who think they have this capacity do not possess it. Warmth of heart, impulsiveness, pity are not enough.
quotes.author: Simone Weil
quotes.source: Waiting on God (1950) / Reflections on the Right Use of School Studies with a View to the Love of God

quotes.text: Anyone who holds a true opinion without understanding is like a blind man on the right road.
quotes.author: Socrates

quotes.text: Prepare your mind and heart before you prepare your speech. What we say may be less important than how we say it.
quotes.author: Stephen Covey

quotes.text: Truth never yet fell dead in the streets; it has such affinity with the soul of man, the seed however broadcast will catch somewhere and produce its hundredfold.
quotes.author: Theodore Parker
quotes.source: A Discourse of Matters Pertaining to Religion (1842).

quotes.text: Finally, and most important of all, it should ever be kept in mind that the man who does a great work must almost invariably owe the possibility of doing it to the faithful work of other men, either at the time or long before.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: He was a plain, quiet man, not seeking for glory; but a man who, when aroused, was always in deadly earnest, and who never shrank from duty.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: Breath is the bridge which connects life to consciousness, which unites your body to your thoughts. Whenever your mind becomes scattered, use your breath as the means to take hold of your mind again.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

quotes.text: The present moment contains past and future. The secret of transformation, is in the way we handle this very moment.
quotes.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

quotes.text: A man protesting against error is on the way to uniting himself with all men who believe in truth.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle
quotes.source: Heroes and Hero-Worship (1840), Lecture IV; in Collected Works, Vol. XII (London: Chapman and Hall, 1869), p. 148

quotes.text: Silence is more eloquent than words.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle
quotes.source: Heroes and Hero Worship (1840), Lecture II.

quotes.text: Silence is the element in which great things fashion themselves together; that at length they may emerge, full-formed and majestic, into the daylight of Life, which they are thenceforth to rule.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: Speech is of time, silence is of eternity.
quotes.author: Thomas Carlyle

quotes.text: First keep the peace within yourself, then you can also bring peace to others.
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: Peace is ever with the humble man, but in the heart of the proud there is envy and continual wrath.
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: To account nothing of one’s self, and to think always kindly and highly of others, this is great and perfect wisdom.
quotes.author: Thomas à Kempis

quotes.text: Those who are silent, self-effacing and attentive become the recipients of confidences.
quotes.author: Thornton Wilder

quotes.text: The word must be heard in silence; there must be darkness to see the stars.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
quotes.source: Chapter 8, "The Children of the Open Sea" (Ged)

quotes.text: The world’s vast and strange, Hara, but no vaster and no stranger than our minds are. Think of that sometimes.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

quotes.text: To hear, one must be silent.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

quotes.text: It is good to be firm by temperament and pliant by reflection.
quotes.author: Vauvenargues

quotes.text: Time bears away all things, even our minds.
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: The worker must work for the glory of his handiwork, not simply for pay; the thinker must think for truth, not for fame.
quotes.author: W. E. B. Du Bois
quotes.source: Ch. V: Of the Wings of Atalanta

quotes.text: Nothing in the world is permanent, and we're foolish when we ask anything to last, but surely we're still more foolish not to take delight in it while we have it. If change is of the essence of existence one would have thought it only sensible to make it the premise of our philosophy.
quotes.author: W. Somerset Maugham

quotes.text: The beauty of the morning and the radiance of noon are good, but it would be a very silly person who drew the curtains and turned on the light in order to shut out the tranquility of the evening.
quotes.author: W. Somerset Maugham

quotes.text: Where all think alike, no one thinks very much.
quotes.author: Walter Lippmann
quotes.source: The Stakes of Diplomacy (New York: Henry Holt and Company, 1915), p. 51

quotes.text: To have peace you must make peace with your enemy. To make peace only with your friends is to avoid the issue, and to permit a great principle to become absurd.
quotes.author: Wendell Berry
quotes.source: "A Statement against the War in Vietnam", The Long-Legged House (1969)

quotes.text: We can make our minds so like still water that beings gather about us that they may see, it may be, their own images, and so live for a moment with a clearer, perhaps even with a fiercer life because of our quiet.
quotes.author: William Butler Yeats

quotes.text: Wisdom and goodness are twin-born, one heart Must hold both sisters, never seen apart.
quotes.author: William Cowper

quotes.text: A cynic is a man who is morally near-sighted,—and brags about it. He sees the evil in his own heart, and thinks he sees the world.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Calmness comes ever from within. It is the peace and restfulness of the depths of our nature.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Every man has an atmosphere which is affecting every other. So silent and unconsciously is this influence working, that man may forget that it exists.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If we desire to do good in the world, let us begin to love humanity, to realize more truly the great dominant note that sounds in every mortal, despite all the discords of life, the great natural bond of unity that makes all men brothers.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Into the hands of every individual is given a marvellous power for good or for evil,—the silent, unconscious, unseen influence of his life. This is simply the constant radiation of what a man really is, not what he pretends to be.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is a time for action, not worry, because worry paralyzes thought and action, too. If you set down a column of figures in addition, no amount of worry can change the sum total of those figures.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: It is the compass of the soul, the guardian of conscience, the final touchstone of right. Truth is the revelation of the ideal; but it is also an inspiration to realize that ideal, a constant impulse to live it.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us love the truth so strongly that there will develop within us, without our conscious effort, an ever-present horror of a lie.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Let us make the best we can of to-day in the best preparation for to-morrow; then even the things that come too late will be new revelations of wisdom to use in the present now before us, and in the future we are forming.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Make simplicity the keynote of your life and you will be great, no matter though your life be humble and your influence seem but little.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Man might possess everything tangible in the world and yet not be happy, for happiness is the satisfying of the soul, not of the mind or the body.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Nature, in all her revelations, seeks to teach man the greatness of simplicity.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Simplicity is the pure white light of a life lived from within.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Simplicity is the sun of a self-centred and pure life,—the secret of any specific greatness in the life of the individual.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: The bitter words of anger and reproach that rise so easily to our lips and give us a moment's fleeting satisfaction in thus venting our feelings, may change the current of the whole life of some one near to us.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The fury of storm and of wind agitate only the surface of the sea; they can penetrate only two or three hundred feet,—below that is the calm, unruffled deep.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The love of Truth is the cultivated hunger for it in itself and for itself, without any thought of what it may cost, what sacrifices it may entail, what theories or beliefs of a lifetime may be laid desolate.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The man who is self-reliant seeks ever to discover and conquer the weakness within him that keeps him from the attainment of what he holds dearest; he seeks within himself the power to battle against all outside influences.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The man whose character is simple looks truth and honesty so straight in the face that he has no consciousness of intrigue and corruption around him.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: The secret of all true greatness is simplicity.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Time is the only really valuable possession of man, for without it every power within him would cease to exist.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: To cure one’s self of worry is not an easy task; it is not to be removed in two or three applications of the quack medicine of any cheap philosophy, but it requires only clear, simple commonsense applied to the business of life.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: To the man who is calm, revenge is so far beneath him that he cannot reach it,—even by stooping. When injured, he does not retaliate; he wraps around him the royal robes of Calmness, and he goes quietly on his way.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: To think of this water of past time with such regret that it shuts our eyes to the mighty river of the present is sheer folly.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: To true simplicity, to perceive a truth is to begin to live it, to see a duty is to begin to do it. Nothing great can ever enter into the consciousness of a man of simplicity and remain but a theory.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Tolerance is silent justice, blended with sympathy.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Truth is the oldest of all the virtues; it antedated man, it lived before there was man to perceive it or to accept it.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Under the guise of helping us to bear the present, and to be ready for the future, worry multiplies enemies within our own mind to sap our strength.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: When a man discovers a great truth in Nature he has the key to the understanding of a million phenomena; when he grasps a great truth in morals he has in it the key to his spiritual re-creation.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: When the chance to win fame, wealth, success or the attainment of your heart's desire, by sacrifice of honor or principle, comes to you and it does not affect you long enough even to seem a temptation, you have been the victor.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: One truth discovered is immortal, and entitles its author to be so: for, like a new substance in nature, it cannot be destroyed.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt
quotes.source: The Spirit of the Age, Jeremy Bentham.

quotes.text: We do not see nature with our eyes, but with our understandings and our hearts.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt
quotes.source: "Thoughts on Taste," Edinburgh Magazine, (October 1818), reprinted in The Collected Works of William Hazlitt (1902-1904)

quotes.text: It is only by risking our persons from one hour to another that we live at all. And often enough our faith beforehand in an uncertified result is the only thing that makes the result come true.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: "Is Life Worth Living?" The Will to Believe and Other Essays in Popular Philosophy (1897).

quotes.text: Let any one try, I will not say to arrest, but to notice or attend to, the present moment of time. One of the most baffling experiences occurs. Where is it, this present? It has melted in our grasp, fled ere we could touch it, gone in the instant of becoming.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: The art of being wise is the art of knowing what to overlook.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: Of this I am quite sure, that if we open a quarrel between the past and the present, we shall find that we have lost the future.
quotes.author: Winston Churchill
quotes.source: Speech in the House of Commons, June 18, 1940 "War Situation"

quotes.text: Whatever kind of ambition it took to do what you did around here, this world could use a lot more of it.
quotes.author: Carol Boone

quotes.text: I don't care if you like each other right now, but you will respect each other.
quotes.author: Coach Boone

quotes.text: I don't scratch my head 'til it itches, and I don't dance until I hear some music. I will not be intimidated.
quotes.author: Coach Boone

quotes.text: The best player will play, color won't matter.
quotes.author: Coach Boone

quotes.text: We will be perfect every day in every aspect of the game.
quotes.author: Coach Boone

quotes.text: Win or lose, we gonna walk out of this stadium tonight with our heads held high. Do your best. That's all anybody can ask for.
quotes.author: Coach Boone

quotes.text: You wanna act like a star, you'd better give me a star effort.
quotes.author: Coach Yoast

quotes.text: Coach, I'm hurt. I ain't dead.
quotes.author: Gerry Bertier

quotes.text: I was afraid of you, Julius. I only saw what I was afraid of, and now I know I was only hating my brother.
quotes.author: Gerry Bertier

quotes.text: Attitude reflects leadership, captain.
quotes.author: Julius Campbell

quotes.text: People say that it can't work, black and white. Here, we make it work every day. We still have our disagreements, of course, but before we reach for hate, always, always, we remember the Titans.
quotes.author: Sheryl Yoast

quotes.text: Man needs his difficulties because they are necessary to enjoy success.
quotes.author: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

quotes.text: Truth is strong enough to overcome all human sophistries.
quotes.author: Aeschines

quotes.text: The important thing in my view is not to pin the blame for a mistake on somebody, but rather to find out what caused the mistake.
quotes.author: Akio Morita

quotes.text: Mistakes are a part of being human. Appreciate your mistakes for what they are: precious life lessons that can only be learned the hard way. Unless it's a fatal mistake, which, at least, others can learn from.
quotes.author: Al Franken

quotes.text: The tragedy is not that things are broken. The tragedy is that things are not mended again.
quotes.author: Alan Paton

quotes.text: Life is like riding a bicycle. To keep your balance you must keep moving.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.source: Letter to his son Eduard (5 February 1930), as quoted in Walter Isaacson, Einstein: His Life and Universe (2007), p. 367

quotes.text: Our life consists not in the pursuit of material success but in the quest for worthy spiritual growth. Our entire earthly existence is but a transitional stage in the movement toward something higher, and we must not stumble and fall, nor must we linger fruitlessly on one rung of the ladder.
quotes.author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn

quotes.text: Please know that I am aware of the hazards. I want to do it because I want to do it. Women must try to do things as men have tried. When they fail, their failure must be a challenge to others.
quotes.author: Amelia Earhart
quotes.source: Letter to her husband George P. Putnam, on the eve of her last flight

quotes.text: Art begins with resistance — at the point where resistance is overcome. No human masterpiece has ever been created without great labor.
quotes.author: André Gide

quotes.text: Most often people seek in life occasions for persisting in their opinions rather than for educating themselves.
quotes.author: André Gide

quotes.text: No theory is good unless it permits, not rest, but the greatest work. No theory is good except on condition that one use it to go on beyond.
quotes.author: André Gide

quotes.text: Those who make no mistakes are making the biggest mistakes of all — they are attempting nothing new.
quotes.author: Anthony de Mello

quotes.text: You cannot by any chance fail if you persevere.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — Controlling The Mind

quotes.text: We do not have to live the same mistakes over again if we can look at them, learn from them, and build upon them.
quotes.author: Audre Lorde

quotes.text: Don’t persist in folly. Some people commit themselves to their errors. They act mistakenly and consider it constancy to go on that way.
quotes.author: Baltasar Gracián

quotes.text: The greatest of sages can commit one mistake, but not two; he may fall into error, but he doesn’t lie down and make his home there.
quotes.author: Baltasar Gracián

quotes.text: Time heals griefs and quarrels, for we change and are no longer the same persons.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: Running water never grows stale. So you just have to 'keep on flowing.
quotes.author: Bruce Lee

quotes.text: Realistic thinking accrues only after mistake making, which is the cosmic wisdom's most cogent way of teaching each of us how to carry on.
quotes.author: Buckminster Fuller
quotes.source: Buckminster Fuller and Answar Dil, Humans in Universe (1983), 218.

quotes.text: If a man find a prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, he may walk with him, overcoming all dangers, happy, but considerate.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XXIII. The Elephant, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Let a man leave anger, let him forsake pride, let him overcome all bondage!
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter XVII. Anger, trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Man needs difficulties; they are necessary for health.
quotes.author: Carl Jung

quotes.text: You fix what can be fixed, and what can't be fixed you endure.
quotes.author: Charlie Munger

quotes.text: Patience is not only a virtue, but an acquired trait.
quotes.author: Christian Calhoun

quotes.text: What I do is based on powers we all have inside us; the ability to endure; the ability to love, to carry on, to make the best of what we have — and you don’t have to be a "Superman" to do it.
quotes.author: Christopher Reeve

quotes.text: Men do not stumble over mountains, but over molehills
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Reported in United States Congress House Committee on Agriculture (1973) Hearings Before the Committee on Agriculture, House of Representatives, Ninet…

quotes.text: The man of virtue makes the difficulty to be overcome his first business, and success only a subsequent consideration: this may be called perfect virtue.
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.text: Patience is a nobler motion than any deed.
quotes.author: Cyrus Augustus Bartol

quotes.text: Most of the important things in the world have been accomplished by people who have kept on trying when there seemed to be no hope at all.
quotes.author: Dale Carnegie
quotes.source: The Ring of Truth (2004) by Joseph O'Day

quotes.text: Humanity will ever seek but never attain perfection. Let us at least survive and go on trying.
quotes.author: Dora Russell

quotes.text: Neither failure nor success has the power to change your inner state of Being. You have found the life underneath your life situation.
quotes.author: Eckhart Tolle

quotes.text: The man who makes no mistakes does not usually make anything.
quotes.author: Edward John Phelps
quotes.source: speech at Mansion House, London (Jan. 24, 1889), quoting Bishop W. C. Magee of Peterborough, in 1868.

quotes.text: Patience can't be acquired overnight. It's just like building up a muscle. Every day you need to work on it.
quotes.author: Eknath Easwaran

quotes.text: A failure is a man who has blundered, but is not able to cash in the experience.
quotes.author: Elbert Hubbard
quotes.source: The Roycraft Dictionary and Book of Epigrams (1923)

quotes.text: The greatest mistake you can make in life is to be continually fearing you will make one.
quotes.author: Elbert Hubbard
quotes.source: The Note Book of Elbert Hubbard (1927)

quotes.text: For remember that, if you are persistent, those very persons who at first ridiculed will afterwards admire you.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxii, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: For when this faculty of the will is set right, a man who is not good becomes good: but when it fails, a man becomes bad.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: But man is not made for defeat. A man can be destroyed but not defeated.
quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.source: The Old Man and the Sea (1952), p. 113.

quotes.text: Difficulties are just things to overcome after all.
quotes.author: Ernest Shackleton

quotes.text: This is certain, that a man that studieth revenge, keeps his own wounds green, which otherwise would heal, and do well.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text: Endurance. Belief. Patience. Hope. These are the key words of our existence.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: Select your battles carefully. Ultimately, victory and defeat are a matter of your own careful — or reckless — choices.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: There is a certain momentum to victory... and to defeat.
quotes.author: Frank Herbert

quotes.text: Study nature, love nature, stay close to nature. It will never fail you.
quotes.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
quotes.source: The Wright Style (1992) by Carla Lind, p. 3

quotes.text: The reasonable man adapts himself to the world: the unreasonable one persists in trying to adapt the world to himself. Therefore all progress depends on the unreasonable man.
quotes.author: George Bernard Shaw

quotes.text: I'm proof against that word failure. I've seen behind it. The only failure a man ought to fear is failure of cleaving to the purpose he sees to be best.
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.text: Let a man once overcome his selfish terror at his own finitude, and his finitude is, in one sense, overcome.
quotes.author: George Santayana
quotes.source: Introduction to The Ethics of Spinoza (1910)

quotes.text: A man's life is interesting primarily when he has failed—I well know. For it's a sign that he tried to surpass himself.
quotes.author: Georges Clemenceau
quotes.source: conversation with Jean Martet, June 1, 1928—Clemenceau, The Events of His Life as Told by Himself to His Former Secretary, Jean Martet, trans. Milton…

quotes.text: He who travels the hazardous road of misfortune courageously, leaves it strewn with sweet flowers of consolation for others.
quotes.author: Helen Keller

quotes.text: When one door of happiness closes, another opens; but often we look so long at the closed door that we do not see the one which has been opened for us.
quotes.author: Helen Keller

quotes.text: Goodness is the only investment that never fails. In the music of the harp which trembles round the world it is the insisting on this which thrills us.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: The faintest assured objection which one healthy man feels will at length prevail over the arguments and customs of mankind.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Through our own recovered innocence we discern the innocence of our neighbors.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Failure is only the opportunity to more intelligently begin again. There is no disgrace in honest failure; there is disgrace in fearing to fail.
quotes.author: Henry Ford
quotes.source: pp. 19–20. Quoted in Samuel Crowther, "Henry Ford's Problem," The Magazine of Business, vol. 52 (1927), p. 182

quotes.text: All things come round to him who will but wait.
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
quotes.source: Tales of a Wayside Inn, The Student's Tale, Part I.

quotes.text: Perseverance is a great element of success. If you only knock long enough and loud enough at the gate, you are sure to wake up somebody.
quotes.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
quotes.source: Samuel Longfellow (ed.) Final Memorials (Boston: Ticknor and Co., 1887) Ch. 19: Table-Talk

quotes.text: Ten men have failed from defect in morals, where one has failed from defect in intellect.
quotes.author: Horace Mann

quotes.text: Only while sleeping one makes no mistakes. Making mistakes is the privilege of the active—of those who can correct their mistakes and put them right.
quotes.author: Ingvar Kamprad

quotes.text: It is better to go to defeat with free will than to live in a meaningless security as a cog in a machine.
quotes.author: Isaac Asimov

quotes.text: To me the greatest moment in an experiment is always just before I learn whether the particular idea is a good or a bad one. Thus even a failure is exciting, and most of my ideas have of course been wrong.
quotes.author: Ivar Giaever
quotes.source: Electron Tunneling and Superconductivity, Nobel Lecture [http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/1973/giaever-lecture.pdf ] (December 12…

quotes.text: It is impossible to live without failing at something, unless you live so cautiously that you might as well not have lived at all — in which case, you fail by default.
quotes.author: J. K. Rowling

quotes.text: The world is full of wonderful things you haven’t seen yet. Don’t ever give up on the chance of seeing them.
quotes.author: J. K. Rowling
quotes.source: Online tweet, in response to an extremely depressed person contemplating suicide, as quoted in Alex Ungerman "J.K. Rowling Sends Beautiful Message to…

quotes.text: I am sorry: sorry you have come in for this burden; sorry about everything. Don't adventures ever have an end? I suppose not. Someone else always has to carry on the story.
quotes.author: J. R. R. Tolkien

quotes.text: ALL that a man achieves and all that he fails to achieve is the direct result of his own thoughts.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — The Thought-Factor In Achievement

quotes.text: Our triumphs seem hollow unless we have friends to share them, and our failures are made bearable by their understanding.
quotes.author: James Rachels
quotes.source: The Elements of Moral Philosophy (1999), p. 183.

quotes.text: An appeal to the reason of the people has never been known to fail in the long run.
quotes.author: James Russell Lowell

quotes.text: Let us be of good cheer, however, remembering that the misfortunes hardest to bear are those which never come.
quotes.author: James Russell Lowell

quotes.text: Hope is what enables us to keep going in the face of adversity. It is what we desire to happen, but we must be prepared to work hard to make it so.
quotes.author: Jane Goodall
quotes.source: The Book of Hope: A Survival Guide for Trying Times (2021), p. 8.

quotes.text: Failure concentrates the mind wonderfully. If you don’t make mistakes, you’re not trying hard enough.
quotes.author: Jasper Fforde
quotes.source: The Well of Lost Plots (2003), , p. 255

quotes.text: All great achievers are given multiple reasons to believe they are failures. But in spite of that they persevere.
quotes.author: John C. Maxwell

quotes.text: Pain makes man think. Thought makes man wise. Wisdom makes life endurable.
quotes.author: John Patrick
quotes.source: The Teahouse of the August Moon, act I, scene i, p. 6 (1957). These words are spoken by Sakini, an Okinawan, to the audience. They are repeated in act…

quotes.text: The only real mistake is the one from which we learn nothing.
quotes.author: John Powell
quotes.source: The Secret of Staying in Love (1990), p. 85.

quotes.text: Truth gains more even by the errors of one who, with due study and preparation, thinks for himself, than by the true opinions of those who only hold them because they do not suffer themselves to think.
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill
quotes.source: Ch. II: Of the Liberty of Thought and Discussion

quotes.text: Adversity is the state in which man most easily becomes acquainted with himself, being especially free of admirers then.
quotes.author: John Wooden
quotes.source: Wooden: A Lifetime of Observations and Reflections on and Off the Court (1997)

quotes.text: Don’t beat yourself. That’s the worst kind of defeat you’ll ever suffer.
quotes.author: John Wooden

quotes.text: A good conscience is to the soul what health is to the body; it preserves a constant ease and serenity within us, and more than countervails all the calamities and afflictions which can possibly befall us.
quotes.author: Joseph Addison

quotes.text: Our life evokes our character and you find out more about yourself as you go on.
quotes.author: Joseph Campbell

quotes.text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding. Even as the stone of the fruit must break, that its heart may stand in the sun, so must you know pain.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: Our minds are better employed in bearing the misfortunes that do befall us than is foreseeing those that may.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: Everything comes in time to him who knows how to wait.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.source: War and Peace (1865–1867; 1869), Book X, Chapter 16

quotes.text: One is ashamed to say how little is needed for all men to be delivered from those calamities which now oppress them; it is only needful not to lie.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.text: It is not necessary to succeed in order to persevere. As long as there is a margin of hope, however narrow, we have no choice but to base all our action on that margin.
quotes.author: Leó Szilárd

quotes.text: Tests are a gift. And great tests are a great gift. To fail the test is a misfortune. But to refuse the test is to refuse the gift, and something worse, more irrevocable, than misfortune.
quotes.author: Lois McMaster Bujold

quotes.text: Maybe you have to know darkness before you can appreciate the light.
quotes.author: Madeleine L'Engle

quotes.text: It is unwise to be too sure of one's own wisdom. It is healthy to be reminded that the strongest might weaken and the wisest might err.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi

quotes.text: You may never be able to come back to the place you have left, nor can you undo the wrongs that you have done. But you can always begin again. You can cleanse the heart, you can remake your life, you can rebuild character.
quotes.author: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.source: Harijan, 7 January 1939, in The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, Vol. 68, p. 6.

quotes.text: Victory is sweetest when you've known defeat.
quotes.author: Malcolm S. Forbes
quotes.source: Wisdom Through the Ages (2003) by Helen Granat, p. 69.

quotes.text: We are healed of a suffering only by experiencing it to the full.
quotes.author: Marcel Proust

quotes.text: But now the more of these things a man deprives himself of, or of other things like them, or even when he is deprived of any of them, the more patiently he endures the loss, just in the same degree he is a better man.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Is any man afraid of change? Why, what can take place without change?
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Not to feel exasperated or defeated or despondent because your days aren't packed with wise and moral actions. But to get back up when you fail, to celebrate behaving like a human—however imperfectly—and fully embrace the pursuit you've embarked on.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Remember too on every occasion which leads thee to vexation to apply this principle; not that this is a misfortune, but that to bear it nobly is good fortune.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: So remember this principle when something threatens to cause you pain: the thing itself was no misfortune at all; to endure it and prevail is great good fortune.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: These it is thy duty to observe, and without being disturbed or showing anger towards those who are angry with thee, to go on thy way and finish that which is set before thee.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Life is not easy for any of us. But what of that? We must have perseverance and above all confidence in ourselves. We must believe that we are gifted for something, and that this thing, at whatever cost, must be attained.
quotes.author: Marie Curie
quotes.source: 'La vie n’est facile pour aucun de nous. Mais quoi, il faut avoir de la persévérance, et surtout de la confiance en soi. Il faut croire que l’on est d…

quotes.text: Patience is the art of hoping.
quotes.author: Marquis De Vauvenargues

quotes.text: Keep moving. Let nothing slow you up. Move on with dignity and honor and respectability.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.

quotes.text: We must keep moving. If you can't fly, run; if you can't run, walk; if you can't walk, crawl; but by all means keep moving.
quotes.author: Martin Luther King Jr.

quotes.text: Take chances, make mistakes. That's how you grow. Pain nourishes your courage. You have to fail in order to practice being brave.
quotes.author: Mary Tyler Moore

quotes.text: We may encounter many defeats, but we must not be defeated.
quotes.author: Maya Angelou

quotes.text: I can accept failure. Everyone fails at something. But I can't accept not trying (no hard work).
quotes.author: Michael Jordan
quotes.source: Jordan, Michael. I Can't Accept Not Trying : Michael Jordan on the Pursuit of Excellence. San Francisco, CA: HarperSanFrancisco, 1994. p. 129.

quotes.text: Grasp your opportunities, no matter how poor your health; nothing is worse for your health than boredom.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: In retrospect, our triumphs could as easily have happened to someone else; but our defeats are uniquely our own.
quotes.author: Mignon McLaughlin

quotes.text: There are some defeats more triumphant than victories.
quotes.author: Montaigne
quotes.source: Ch. 30. Of Cannibals (tr. Cotton, rev. W. Hazlitt, 1842)

quotes.text: Aiki is not a technique to fight with or defeat an enemy. It is the way to reconcile the world and make human beings one family.
quotes.author: Morihei Ueshiba
quotes.source: It's A Lot Like Dancing… : An Aikido Journey (1993 by Terry Dobson Riki Moss, and Jan E. Watson -

quotes.text: I never thought of losing, but now that it's happened, the only thing is to do it right. That's my obligation to all the people who believe in me. We all have to take defeats in life.
quotes.author: Muhammad Ali
quotes.source: Statement after losing to Ken Norton despite 5-1 odds in his favor (31 March 1973), as quoted by Jeff Johnson in "Muhammad Ali In His Own Words: Six o…

quotes.text: Most of us are good "starters" but poor "finishers" of everything we begin. Moreover, people are prone to give up at the first signs of defeat. There is no substitute for persistence. Failure cannot cope with Persistance.
quotes.author: Napoleon Hill

quotes.text: Prison itself is a tremendous education in the need for patience and perseverance. It is above all a test of one's commitment.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

quotes.text: The time for the healing of the wounds has come. The moment to bridge the chasms that divide us has come. The time to build is upon us.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

quotes.text: Believe that problems do have answers. Believe that they can be overcome. Believe that they can be handled. And finally, believe that you can solve them.
quotes.author: Norman Vincent Peale
quotes.source: ‪You Can If You Think You Can‬ (1987), p. 36

quotes.text: Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
quotes.author: Oliver Goldsmith
