quotes.source: The Citizen of the World (1760–1761), Letter VI

quotes.text: A man may make millions and be a failure still.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: A multitude of men fail to get on because they take themselves too seriously.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: All the light you need is for the next step. Faith in your vision and persistent endeavor will do the rest.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Don't expect to have health for nothing. Nothing in this world worth anything can be had for nothing.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLVI

quotes.text: Endurance is a much better test of character than any one act of heroism, however noble.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XL

quotes.text: Erase all the shadows, all the doubts and fears, and the suggestions of poverty and failure from your mind.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: Even the man with small ability will often succeed if he has the quality of persistence, where a genius without persistence would fail.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every defeat is a Waterloo to him who has no reserves.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every obstacle overcome lends him strength for the next conflict. If he falls, he rises with more determination than before.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: Every one who slips from the right path, no matter what he has done, should be given another chance, a fresh opportunity to make good, to rebuild his character.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Every time you think you are a failure, it helps you to become one, for your thought is your life pattern and you can not get away from it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Everybody believes in the man who persists. He may meet misfortunes, sorrows and reverses, but everybody believes that he will ultimately triumph because they know there is no keeping him down.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Failure often leads a man to success by arousing his latent energy, by firing a dormant purpose, by awakening powers which were sleeping.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: He who will pay the price for victory need never fear final defeat.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: Hold the victorious attitude toward life and you will overcome all unfavorable conditions.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If your wealth has made others poorer, your life is a failure.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: In the game of life most of us start out by putting the odds on our failure.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the man of action, of continued and repeated action, the man who never acknowledges defeat who ultimately wins out.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It is the positive, forceful man that overcomes. Obstacles do not frighten, or turn him from his purpose.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Look where you will, ask of whom you will, and you will find that not circumstances, but personal qualities, defects and deficiencies, cause failures.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Love is a healer, a life-giver, a balm for our hurts.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVII

quotes.text: Love is healing the hurts made by hate and discord.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Many a man has never found himself until he has lost his all. Adversity stripped him only to discover him.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: Many people fail because they lose their grit after they fail, or when they get down, they don't know how to get up.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: Never even think of the possibility of going through life a failure or a partial failure.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Never mind what discouragements, misfortunes or failures come to you, let nobody, no combination of unfortunate circumstances, destroy your faith in your dream of what you believe you were made to do.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: No one can pursue a worthy object steadily and persistently with all the powers of his mind, and yet make his life a failure.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: Not the distance we have run, but the obstacles we have overcome, the disadvantages under which we have made the race, will decide the prizes.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: One of the worst forms of worry is the brooding over failure. It blights the ambition, deadens the purpose and defeats the very object the worrier has in view.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: Our occupations, difficulties, obstacles, disappointments, if used aright, are the great schoolmasters which help us to possess ourselves.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Persistency always gives confidence. Everybody believes in the man who persists.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Persistency is characteristic of all men who have accomplished anything great.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Resolve that you will close the door on everything in the past that pains and can not help you.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIV

quotes.text: Some men are rich in health, in constant cheerfulness, in a mercurial temperament which floats them over troubles and trials enough to sink a shipload of ordinary men.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXVI

quotes.text: Success is a great tonic, and failure a great depressant.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIII

quotes.text: The great difference between those who succeed and those who fail does not consist in the amount of work done by each, but in the amount of intelligent work.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XII

quotes.text: The man who always acts promptly, even if he makes occasional mistakes, will succeed when a procrastinator, even if he have the better judgment, will fail.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIV

quotes.text: The persistent man never stops to consider whether he is succeeding or not.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The persistent tortoise outruns the swift but fickle hare.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIII

quotes.text: The slow trotter will out-travel the fleet racer. Genius darts, flutters, and tires; but perseverance wears and wins.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIII

quotes.text: The strong-willed, intelligent, persistent man will find or make a way where, in the nature of things, a way can be found or made.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXVIII

quotes.text: The trouble with most of us is that we do not keep our eyes on the model; we lose our earlier vision.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter VIII

quotes.text: The victorious, triumphant attitude will put you in command of resources which a timid, self-depreciating, failure attitude will drive from you.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The world has little use for whiners, or long-faced failures.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: There is no philosophy which will help a man to succeed when he is always doubting his ability to do so, and thus attracting failure.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LVI

quotes.text: There is nothing which will multiply one's ability like self-faith. It can make a one-talent man a success, while a ten-talent man without it would fail.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: There is plenty in this world, if we keep it moving and keep moving after it.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXI

quotes.text: To overcome one barrier gives us greater ability to overcome the next.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXIII

quotes.text: We are the victors of our opponents. They have developed in us the very power by which we overcome them.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXVII

quotes.text: We can all be our own healers if we will.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We can often find out by hard knocks and repeated failures what we can not do before what we can do.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XI

quotes.text: We fail to see that we can control our own destiny: make ourselves do whatever is possible; make ourselves become whatever we long to be.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: We have to learn to turn away from the heart-breaks of life and to face toward the light.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Whatever we long for, yearn for, struggle for, and hold persistently in the mind, we tend to become just in exact proportion to the intensity and persistence of the thought.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Whatever you do for a living, whatever fortune or misfortune may come to you, hold the victorious attitude and push ahead.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Wherever doubt can get a foothold it introduces its brother fear, and fear brings with it all of its relatives, worry, anxiety, discouragement—the whole failure family.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You can not keep a man down who has these qualities. He will make stepping-stones out of his stumbling-blocks, and lift himself to success.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXV

quotes.text: In my experience, each failure contains the seeds of your next success — if you are willing to learn from it.
quotes.author: Paul Allen

quotes.text: Some day you will know for yourself that it is almost as true to say that one recovers from all things as that there is nothing which does not leave its scar.
quotes.author: Paul Bourget

quotes.text: I ask myself: are defeats necessary? Well, necessary or not, they happen. When we first begin fighting for a dream, we have no experience and make mistakes. The secret of life, though, is to fall seven times and to get up eight times.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: Life is one long training session in preparation for what will come. Life and death lose their meaning; there are only challenges to be met with joy and overcome with tranquility.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: There is suffering in life, and there are defeats. No one can avoid them. But it's better to lose some of the battles in the struggles for your dreams than to be defeated without ever knowing what you're fighting for.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho
quotes.source: Honor Your Gifts (2007) by Dona M. Deane, p. 199.

quotes.text: What hurts us is what heals us.
quotes.author: Paulo Coelho

quotes.text: They who overcome their desires once can overcome them always.
quotes.author: Pierre Corneille

quotes.text: Prosperity proves men to be fortunate, while it is adversity which makes them great.
quotes.author: Pliny the Younger

quotes.text: Perseverance is more prevailing than violence; and many things which cannot be overcome when they are together, yield themselves up when taken little by little.
quotes.author: Plutarch

quotes.text: Socrates thought that if all our misfortunes were laid in one common heap, whence every one must take an equal portion, most persons would be contented to take their own and depart.
quotes.author: Plutarch

quotes.text: Every one excels in something in which another fails.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: Never find your delight in another's misfortune.
quotes.author: Publilius Syrus

quotes.text: Friends are as companions on a journey, who ought to aid each other to persevere in the road to a happier life.
quotes.author: Pythagoras
quotes.source: Gems of Thought: Being a Collection of More Than a Thousand Choice Selections, Or Aphorisms, from Nearly Four Hundred and Fifty Different Authors, and…

quotes.text: Rejoice not in another man's misfortune!
quotes.author: Pythagoras

quotes.text: A man who stands united with his thought conceives magnificently of himself. He is conscious of a universal success, even though bought by uniform particular failures.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: All loss, all pain, is particular; the universe remains to the heart unhurt. Neither vexations nor calamities abate our trust.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: By persisting in your path, though you forfeit the little you gain the great.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Every man is a consumer, and ought to be a producer. He fails to make his place good in the world, unless he not only pays his debt, but also adds something to the common wealth.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: The Conduct of Life (1860) — I. Fate

quotes.text: I have failed, and you have failed, but perhaps together we shall not fail.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Essays: Second Series (1844) — Viii. Nonimalist And Realist

quotes.text: Let me never fall into the vulgar mistake of dreaming that I am persecuted whenever I am contradicted.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Never was a sincere word utterly lost. Never a magnanimity fell to the ground, but there is some heart to greet and accept it unexpectedly.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Our strength grows out of our weakness. The indignation which arms itself with secret forces does not awaken until we are pricked and stung and sorely assailed.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The characteristic of heroism is its persistency. All men have wandering impulses, fits and starts of generosity.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The imagination is not a talent of some men but is the health of every man.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We acquire the strength we have overcome.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: We must know our friends under ugly masks. The calamities are our friends.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Wherever there is failure, there is some giddiness, some superstition about luck, some step omitted, which Nature never pardons.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Remember brick walls let us show our dedication. They are there to separate us from the people who don't really want to achieve their childhood dreams.
quotes.author: Randy Pausch

quotes.text: Most people can bear adversity; but if you wish to know what a man really is give him power. This is the supreme test. It is the glory of Lincoln that, having almost absolute power, he never used it except on the side of mercy.
quotes.author: Robert G. Ingersoll
quotes.source: (1883), Unity: Freedom, Fellowship and Character in Religion, Volume 11, Number 3, The Exchange Table, True Greatness Exemplified in Abraham Lincoln…

quotes.text: Our business in this world is not to succeed, but to continue to fail, in good spirits.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes.source: Complete Works, vol. 26, Reflections and Remarks on Human Life, section 4.

quotes.text: We must go on, because we can't turn back.
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.text: The relationship between commitment and doubt is by no means an antagonistic one. Commitment is healthiest when it is not without doubt but in spite of doubt.
quotes.author: Rollo May
quotes.source: Ch. 1 : The Courage to Create, p. 21

quotes.text: The lion who breaks the enemy's ranks is a minor hero compared to the lion who overcomes himself.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: Nothing... will ever be attempted, if all possible objections must be first overcome.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson
quotes.source: The History of Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia (1759) / Ch. IV

quotes.text: Adversity is the touchstone of character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Ask the diplomatist, and he will tell you that he has learned his art through being baffled, defeated, thwarted, and circumvented, far more than from having succeeded.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: But while prosperity is apt to harden the heart to pride, adversity in a man of resolution will serve to ripen it into fortitude.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: By far the best experience of men is made up of their remembered failures in dealing with others in the affairs of life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Courage, combined with energy and perseverance, will overcome difficulties apparently insurmountable.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Even if a man fail in his efforts, it will be a satisfaction to him to enjoy the consciousness of having done his best.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Failures in one direction have sometimes had the effect of forcing the farseeing student to apply himself in another.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: He who allows his application to falter, or shirks his work on frivolous pretexts, is on the sure road to ultimate failure.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: He who has lost all, but retains his courage, cheerfulness, hope, virtue, and self-respect, is still rich.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: In humble life nothing can be more cheering and beautiful than to see a man combating suffering by patience, triumphing in his integrity, and who, when his feet are bleeding and his limbs failing him, still walks upon his courage.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is a mistake to suppose that men succeed through success; they much oftener succeed through failure.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: It is in misfortune that the character of the upright man shines forth with the greatest lustre; and when all else fails, he takes stand upon his integrity and his courage.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: It is indolence that exhausts, not action, in which there is life, health, and pleasure.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Life, all sunshine without shade, all happiness without sorrow, all pleasure without pain, were not life at all—at least not human life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Meeting evils by anticipation is not the way to overcome them. If we perpetually carry our burdens about with us, they will soon bear us down under their load.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: One must give and take, refrain and restrain, endure and be patient. One may not be blind to another's failings, but they may be borne with good-natured forbearance.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The apprenticeship of difficulty is one which the greatest of men have had to serve.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The best of causes have had to fight their way to triumph through a long succession of failures, and many of the assailants have died in the breach before the fortress has been won.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The brave man will not be baffled, but tries and tries again until he succeeds.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The character of a man does not depend on whether his efforts are immediately followed by failure or by success.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The persistent man will not be baffled or repulsed by opposition.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The tree does not fall at the first stroke, but only by repeated strokes and after great labour. We may see the visible success at which a man has arrived, but forget the toil and suffering and peril through which it has been achieved.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: The very greatest things—great thoughts, discoveries, inventions—have usually been nurtured in hardship, often pondered over in sorrow, and at length established with difficulty.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There are many tests by which a gentleman may be known; but there is one that never fails—How does he exercise power over those subordinate to him?
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There is, perhaps, no station in life, in which difficulties have not to be encountered and overcome before any decided measure of success can be achieved.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There may be much faltering, stumbling, and temporary defeat; difficulties and temptations manifold to be battled with and overcome; but if the spirit be strong and the heart be upright, no one need despair of ultimate success.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There was no worry, nor fever, nor fret about him; but instead, cheerfulness, patience, and unfailing perseverance.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: They have to do battle with these conditions, and if possible overcome them. Such men have in all ages represented the moral force of the world.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: We learn wisdom from failure much more than from success. We often discover what will do by finding out what will not do; and probably he who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: 19th century Scottish author and reformer, 'Self-Culture: facilities and Difficulties', Self-Help (1856), Chapter 11.

quotes.text: We must sow before we can reap, and often have to wait long, content meanwhile to look patiently forward in hope; the fruit best worth waiting for often ripening the slowest.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Again, if a man’s cataract is cured, he cannot, immediately after his recovery, give back their eyesight to other men also; but when we are freed from evil we can free others also.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: How many things are superfluous we fail to realize until they begin to be wanting; we merely used them not because we needed them but because we had them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 123 (On The Conflict Between Pleasure And Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Look about you and note the things that drive us mad, which we lose with a flood of tears; you will perceive that it is not the loss that troubles us with reference to these things, but a notion of loss.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 42 (On Values), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Men complain about their plans and the outcome of their plans; they always prefer what they have failed to win.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 115 (On The Superficial Blessings), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Night brings our troubles to the light, rather than banishes them; it merely changes the form of our worries.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 56 (On Quiet And Study), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: No one can resume his progress at the point where he left off. Therefore let us press on and persevere.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 71 (On The Supreme Good), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: The mind, however, once healed, is healed for good and all.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 72 (On Business As The Enemy Of Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is nothing that will not surrender to persistent treatment, to concentrated and careful attention; however much the timber may be bent, you can make it straight again.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 50 (On Our Blindness And Its Cure), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is this difference between ourselves and the other school: our ideal wise man feels his troubles, but overcomes them; their wise man does not even feel them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 9 (On Philosophy And Friendship), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: We should fortify ourselves against such calamities. But no wall can be erected against Fortune which she cannot take by storm; let us strengthen our inner defences.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 74 (On Virtue As A Refuge From Worldly Distractions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You cannot escape necessities, but you can overcome them.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 37 (On Allegiance To Virtue), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is only one solution if old age is not to be an absurd parody of our former life, and that is to go on pursuing ends that give our existence a meaning.
quotes.author: Simone De Beauvoir

quotes.text: We must overcome difficulty by constant practice. We must learn that nothing can happen to us unless we make ourselves susceptible to it.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: Any man at times will stumble, and it is then our duty to lift him up and set him on his feet again; but no man can be permanently carried, for if he expects to be carried he shows that he is not worth carrying.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: It is hard to fail, but it is worse never to have tried to succeed.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: speech at the Hamilton Club, Chicago (10 April 1899) The Strenuous Life (vol. 13 of The Works of Theodore Roosevelt, national ed.), chapter 1, p. 320…

quotes.text: No worse wrong can be done by a man to his children than to teach them to go through life endeavoring to shirk difficulties instead of meeting them and overcoming them.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: Of course the all-important thing to keep in mind is that if we have not both strength and virtue we shall fail.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: On the one hand, he must not be volatile and irresolute, and, on the other hand, he must not fear to try a new line because he has failed in another.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Character And Success

quotes.text: The boy who is going to make a great man, or is going to count in any way in after life, must make up his mind not merely to overcome a thousand obstacles, but to win in spite of a thousand repulses or defeats.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — Character And Success

quotes.text: We can do a great deal when we undertake, soberly, to do the possible. When we undertake the impossible, we too often fail to do anything at all.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Strenuous Life (1900) — The Labor Question

quotes.text: Restlessness is discontent — and discontent is the first necessity of progress. Show me a thoroughly satisfied man — and I will show you a failure.
quotes.author: Thomas Edison
quotes.source: The Diary and Sundry Observations of Thomas Alva Edison (1948), p. 110.

quotes.text: There is the greatest practical benefit in making a few failures early in life.
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley
quotes.source: "On Medical Education (An Address to the Students of the Faculty of Medicine in University College, London, 1870)", in Critiques and Addresses (London…

quotes.text: It is light that defeats the dark.
quotes.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

quotes.text: Every misfortune is to be subdued by patience.
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: Love truth, but pardon error.
quotes.author: Voltaire
quotes.source: "Deuxième discours: de la liberté," Sept Discours en Vers sur l'Homme (1738)

quotes.text: It's not hard to stand behind one's successes. But to accept responsibility for one's failures... that is devishly hard!
quotes.author: Václav Havel
quotes.source: "Václav Havel: Heir to a Spiritual Legacy" by Richard L. Stanger in Christian Century (11 April 1990).

quotes.text: There are times when we must sink to the bottom of our misery to understand truth, just as we must descend to the bottom of a well to see the stars in broad daylight.
quotes.author: Václav Havel
quotes.source: Living in Truth (1986) / The Power of the Powerless

quotes.text: All the adversity I've had in my life, all my troubles and obstacles, have strengthened me... You may not realize it when it happens, but a kick in the teeth may be the best thing in the world for you.
quotes.author: Walt Disney

quotes.text: Perseverance is not a long race; it is many short races one after another.
quotes.author: Walter Elliott
quotes.source: The Spiritual Life : Doctrine and Practice of Christian Perfection (1918).

quotes.text: What people see as fearlessness is really persistence.
quotes.author: Wangari Maathai

quotes.text: Mistake, error, is the discipline through which we advance.
quotes.author: William Ellery Channing

quotes.text: All of us failed to match our dreams of perfection. So I rate us on the basis of our splendid failure to do the impossible.
quotes.author: William Faulkner

quotes.text: But what, to our eyes, may seem hopeless failure is often but the dawning of a greater success.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Failure is often the rock-bottom foundation of real success.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Failure is often the turning-point, the pivot of circumstance that swings us to higher levels.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: High ideals, noble efforts will make seeming failures but trifles, they need not dishearten us; they should prove sources of new strength.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If man were sincere in his longing to live life over he would get more help from his failures.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: If we look back upon our past life we will see how, in the marvellous working of events, the cities of our greatest happiness and of our fullest success have been built along the rivers of our deepest sorrows, our most abject failures.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Learn to look not merely at the clouds, but through them to the sun shining behind them.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: Let us not be impatient, chafing at delay, fretting over failure, wearying over results, and weakening under opposition.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Life is a successive unfolding of success from failure.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Man may fail in a dozen different lines of activity and then succeed brilliantly in a phase wherein he was unconscious of any ability.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: Many of our failures sweep us to greater heights of success, than we ever hoped for in our wildest dreams.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Many of the rivers of our greatest prosperity and growth have had their source and their trickling increase into volume among the dark, gloomy recesses of our failure.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Our highest hopes, are often destroyed to prepare us for better things.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The best men in the world, those who have made the greatest real successes look back with serene happiness on their failures.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The honest, faithful struggler should always realize that failure is but an episode in a true man's life,—never the whole story.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The rocky way may prove safer than the slippery path of smoothness. Birds cannot fly best with the wind but against it; ships do not progress in calm, when the sails flap idly against the unstrained masts.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: There is always more progress than you can perceive, and it is really only the outcome of the battle that counts.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: This was the success of failure, a wondrous process of Nature for the highest growth,—a mighty lesson of comfort, strength, and encouragement if man would only realize and accept it.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: We must let the consciousness of doing right, of living up to our ideals, be our reward and stimulus, or life will become to us but a series of failures, sorrows and disappointments.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: How poor are they that have not patience! What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Sure I am of this, that you have only to endure to conquer. You have only to persevere to save yourselves, and to save all those who rely upon you. You have only to go right on, and at the end of the road, be it short or long, victory and honor will be found.
quotes.author: Winston Churchill
quotes.source: Remarks at the Guildhall, 4 September 1914, after the first British naval victory of World War I, the sinking of three German cruisers in the Battle o…

quotes.text: Trying to define yourself is like trying to bite your own teeth.
quotes.author: Alan Watts

quotes.text: The only way to escape the corruptible effect of praise is to go on working.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: Nonconformity is the highest evolutionary attainment of social animals.
quotes.author: Aldo Leopold
quotes.source: "A Man's Leisure Time," 1920; Published in Round River, Luna B. Leopold (ed.), Oxford University Press, 1966, p. 8.

quotes.text: The gain in self-confidence of having accomplished a tiresome labour is immense.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — Dangers To Avoid

quotes.text: You must safeguard your self-respect. Self-respect is at the root of all purposefulness, and a failure in an enterprise deliberately planned deals a desperate wound at one's self-respect.
quotes.author: Arnold Bennett
quotes.source: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day (1908) — Remember Human Nature

quotes.text: Do not fear to be eccentric in opinion, for every opinion now accepted was once eccentric.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell
quotes.source: "A Liberal Decalogue", New York Times Magazine (16 December, 1951).

quotes.text: Self-respect will keep a man from being abject when he is in the power of enemies, and will enable him to feel that he may be in the right when the world is against him.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
quotes.author: Buddha
quotes.source: Dhammapada — Chapter VI. The Wise Man (Pandita), trans. F. Max Müller

quotes.text: Develop the mind of equilibrium. You will always be getting praise and blame, but do not let either affect the poise of the mind: follow the calmness, the absence of pride.
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.text: People need self-respect, but self-respect must be earned -- it cannot be self-respect if it's not earned -- and the only way to earn anything is to achieve it in the face of the possibility of failing.
quotes.author: Charles Murray
quotes.source: Coming Apart: The State of White America, 1960-2010. Crown Forum (2012); ISBN10: 0307453421; ISBN13: 9780307453426

quotes.text: Confidence is that feeling by which the mind embarks in great and honourable courses with a sure hope and trust in itself.
quotes.author: Cicero

quotes.text: Where is there dignity unless there is also honesty?
quotes.author: Cicero

quotes.text: In archery we have something like the way of the superior man. When the archer misses the center of the target, he turns round and seeks for the cause of his failure in himself.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Analects / The Doctrine of the Mean

quotes.text: There is nothing more visible than what is secret, and nothing more manifest than what is minute. Therefore the superior man is watchful over himself, when he is alone.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Analects / The Doctrine of the Mean

quotes.text: The only kind of dignity which is genuine is that which is not diminished by the indifference of others.
quotes.author: Dag Hammarskjöld

quotes.text: With realization of one's own potential and self-confidence in one's ability, one can build a better world.
quotes.author: Dalai Lama
quotes.source: in: Jennifer E. Rhule Find the Leader in You: A Guide to Discovering Your Unlimited Potential, AuthorHouse, 25 July 2013, p. 86.

quotes.text: I grant the man is vain who writes for praise. Praise no man e'er deserved who sought no more.
quotes.author: Edward Young

quotes.text: Before we can make friends with anyone else, we must first make friends with ourselves.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
quotes.source: The Life You Were Born to Live : A Guide to Finding Your Life Purpose (1995) by Dan Millman, p. 38.

quotes.text: But if things independent of the will and not in our power are nothing to us, with respect to these we must employ confidence; and thus we shall both be cautious and confident, and indeed confident because of our caution.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Consider not what he does, but what you are to do to keep your own will in a state conformable to nature, for another cannot hurt you unless you please.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxx, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Fidelity (integrity) is your own, virtuous shame is your own; who then can take these things from you? who else than yourself will hinder you from using them?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: For if you suppose any other things to be either good or evil, it is inevitable that, when you are disappointed of what you wish or incur what you would avoid, you should reproach and blame their authors.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxxi, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: If I can get them with the preservation of my own honor and fidelity and self-respect, show me the way and I will get them; but if you require me to lose my own proper good, that you may gain what is no good, consider how unreasonable and foolish you are.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxiv, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: If then we shall not also put in practice right opinions, we shall be nothing more than the expositors of the opinions of others.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: If you choose, you are free; if you choose, you need blame no man—accuse no man.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Xxii, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: If you have assumed a character beyond your strength, you have both played a poor figure in that, and neglected one that is within your powers.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Golden Sayings of Epictetus — Lxxix, trans. Hastings Crossley

quotes.text: It is the action of an uninstructed person to reproach others for his own misfortunes; of one entering upon instruction, to reproach himself; and one perfectly instructed, to reproach neither others nor himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — V, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Show yourself superior in these, that you may be superior as a man.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: When then we are impeded, or disturbed, or grieved, let us never blame others, but ourselves—that is, our opinions.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: When you do anything from a clear judgment that it ought to be done, never shrink from being seen to do it, even though the world should misunderstand it; for if you are not acting rightly, shun the action itself; if you are, why fear those who wrongly censure you?
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxxv, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: When you would listen to a philosopher, do not say to him, You tell me nothing; but only show yourself worthy of hearing or fit for hearing; and you will see how you will move the speaker.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Whether then have you nothing which is in your own power, which depends on yourself only and cannot be taken from you, or have you anything of the kind?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: You must cultivate either your own reason or else externals; apply yourself either to things within or without you—that is, be either a philosopher or one of the mob.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: The Enchiridion — Xxviii, trans. T. W. Higginson

quotes.text: Some people have no original ideas because they do not think well enough of themselves to consider their ideas worth noticing and developing.
quotes.author: Eric Hoffer

quotes.text: That which is unique and worthwhile in us makes itself felt only in flashes. If we do not know how to catch and savor the flashes we are without growth and exhilaration.
quotes.author: Eric Hoffer
quotes.source: Also quoted in Between the Devil and the Dragon : The Best Essays and Aphorisms of Eric Hoffer (1982)

quotes.text: No one can construct for you the bridge upon which precisely you must cross the stream of life, no one but you yourself alone.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.source: Untimely Meditations, “Schopenhauer as educator,” § 3.1, R. Hollingdale, trans. (1983), p. 129

quotes.text: There exists in the world a single path along which no one can go except you: whither does it lead? Do not ask, go along it.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.source: Untimely Meditations, “Schopenhauer as educator,” § 3.1, R. Hollingdale, trans. (1983), p. 129

quotes.text: We are responsible to ourselves for our own existence; consequently we want to be the true helmsman of this existence and refuse to allow our existence to resemble a mindless act of chance.
quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.source: Untimely Meditations, “Schopenhauer as educator,” § 3.1, R. Hollingdale, trans. (1983), p. 128

quotes.text: Live with your century; but do not be its creature. Work for your contemporaries; but create what they need, not what they praise.
quotes.author: Friedrich Schiller

quotes.text: If you want to be respected by others the great thing is to respect yourself. Only by that, only by self-respect will you compel others to respect you.
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.text: No man who is occupied in doing a very difficult thing, and doing it well, ever loses his self-respect.
quotes.author: George Bernard Shaw

quotes.text: You don't learn to hold your own in the world by standing on guard, but by attacking, and getting well hammered yourself.
quotes.author: George Bernard Shaw

quotes.text: Our dignity is not in what we do, but in what we understand.
quotes.author: George Santayana

quotes.text: Just trust yourself, then you will know how to live.
quotes.author: Goethe

quotes.text: Self-pity gets you nowhere. One must have the adventurous daring to accept oneself as a bundle of possibilities and undertake the most interesting game in the world — making the most of one's best.
quotes.author: Harry Emerson Fosdick

quotes.text: But one cannot be too much on his guard in such a case, lest his actions be biassed by obstinacy, or an undue regard for the opinions of men.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: Walden (1854) — On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience

quotes.text: Every path but your own is the path of fate. Keep on your own track, then.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: On the death of a friend, we should consider that the fates through confidence have devolved on us the task of a double living, that we have henceforth to fulfill the promise of our friend's life also, in our own, to the world.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: It is better to fail in originality, than to succeed in imitation.
quotes.author: Herman Melville

quotes.text: Sapere aude! Have the courage to use your own understanding.
quotes.author: Immanuel Kant

quotes.text: A man's weakness and strength, purity and impurity, are his own, and not another man's; they are brought about by himself, and not by another; and they can only be altered by himself, never by another.
quotes.author: James Allen
quotes.source: As a Man Thinketh (1903) — The Thought-Factor In Achievement

quotes.text: Originality consists in thinking for yourself, not in thinking differently from other people.
quotes.author: James Fitzjames Stephen
quotes.source: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity (1873), Ch. 2. Second edition (London: Smith, Elder, and Co., 1874), p. 52.

quotes.text: Sincerity is impossible, unless it pervade the whole being, and the pretence of it saps the very foundation of character.
quotes.author: James Russell Lowell

quotes.text: The willingness to accept responsibility for one's own life is the source from which self-respect springs.
quotes.author: Joan Didion

quotes.text: It is not by wearing down into uniformity all that is individual in themselves, but by cultivating it and calling it forth, within the limits imposed by the rights and interests of others, that human beings become a noble and beautiful object of contemplation.
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.text: A good place to start is with yourself. See if you can give yourself gifts that may be true blessings, such as self-acceptance, or some time each day with no purpose. Practice feeling deserving enough to accept these gifts without obligation—to simply receive from yourself, and from the universe.
quotes.author: Jon Kabat-Zinn
quotes.source: Wherever You Go, There You Are: Mindfulness Meditation in Everyday Life (2005)

quotes.text: Be genuine and strenuous; earn for yourself, and look for, grace from those in high places; from the powerful, favour; from the active and the good, advancement; from the many, affection; from the individual, love.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: It is a great error to take oneself for more than one is, or for less than one is worth.
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.text: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom. Mastering others is strength; mastering yourself is true power.
quotes.author: Lao Tzu

quotes.text: Every moment think steadily as a Roman and a man to do what thou hast in hand with perfect and simple dignity, and feeling of affection, and freedom, and justice, and to give thyself relief from all other thoughts.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: For at the same time that thou dost remind thyself that it is impossible that such kind of men should not exist, thou wilt become more kindly disposed towards every one individually.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: He who can propose to himself good and virtuous ends of life, and be true to them, cannot fail to live conformably to his own interest and the universal interest, for in the nature of things they are one.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: How strangely men act! They will not praise those who are living at the same time and living with themselves; but to be themselves praised by posterity, by those whom they have never seen nor ever will see, this they set much value on.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: I have often wondered how it is that every man loves himself more than all the rest of men, but yet sets less value on his own opinion of himself than on the opinion of others.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: If a thing is difficult to be accomplished by thyself, do not think that it is impossible for man: but if anything is possible for man and conformable to his nature, think that this can be attained by thyself too.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Neither must we value the clapping of tongues; for the praise which comes from the many is a clapping of tongues.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Remember this, — that there is a proper dignity and proportion to be observed in the performance of every act of life.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Meditations, Chapter 4, p. 32, also quoted in The International Encyclopedia of Prose And Poetical Quotations From The Literature of The World, p. 190

quotes.text: Understand however that every man is worth just so much as the things are worth about which he busies himself.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Whatever is in any way beautiful hath its source of beauty in itself, and is complete in itself; praise forms no part of it. So it is none the worse nor the better for being praised.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.source: Variant: That which is really beautiful has no need of anything. (trans. George Long)

quotes.text: If you have no confidence in self you are twice defeated in the race of life. With confidence you have won even before you have started.
quotes.author: Marcus Garvey
quotes.source: The Philosophy and Opinions of Marcus Garvey, compiled by Amy Jacques Garvey (1923), p. 10

quotes.text: The noble ought to bear with patience the evils of life, which Fortune brings upon them, when they have not themselves to blame.
quotes.author: Menander
quotes.source: Frg. 159 K.-A., Heniochos (tr. C. T. Ramage, 1864)

quotes.text: There is no greater delight than to be conscious of sincerity on self-examination.
quotes.author: Mencius

quotes.text: Any man that tries to rob me of my dignity will lose.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

quotes.text: A man must learn to stand upright upon his own feet, to respect himself, to be independent of charity or accident.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: A man who carries in his very presence an air of victory, radiates assurance, and imparts to others confidence that he can do the thing he attempts.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Believe in yourself; you may succeed when others do not believe in you, but never when you do not believe in yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: But self-respect must be accompanied by self-conquest, or our strong feelings may prove but runaway horses.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Courage, born of self-confidence, is the prod which brings out the last ounce of reserve force.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Dishonesty in all its phases is fatal to happiness, for no dishonest person can get his self-approval.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter L

quotes.text: Do not be afraid to show yourself. This shrinking into a corner and getting out of sight and avoiding publicity is fatal to self-confidence.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXXIII

quotes.text: Fear, in any of its expressions, like worry or anxiety, can not live an instant in your mind in the presence of the opposite thought, the image of courage, fearlessness, confidence, hope, self-assurance, self-reliance.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LIV

quotes.text: Generally shyness comes from a person thinking too much about himself—which in itself is a breach of good breeding—and wondering what other people think about him.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XVIII

quotes.text: Hardship is the native soil of manhood and self-reliance.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: If you do not think and act for yourself, if you do not assert yourself and push your own way, the forces about you will take command and push you.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: It does not matter what other people think of you, of your plans, or of your aims. No matter if they call you a visionary, a crank, or a dreamer; you must believe in yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Make yourself more competent for it. Show that you are abundantly worthy of better things.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: Never allow anybody or any misfortune to shake your belief in yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: No matter what others say or think of you, always hold in mind a lofty ideal of yourself, a picture of your own efficiency.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: No one can respect himself or have that sublime faith in himself which makes for high achievement while he puts half-hearted, mean service into his work.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLII

quotes.text: No one can respect himself who habitually botches his work, and when self-respect drops, confidence goes with it; and when confidence and self-respect have gone, excellence is impossible.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXII

quotes.text: Personal value is a coin of one's own minting; one is taken at the worth he has put into himself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXX

quotes.text: Self-confidence is not egotism. It is knowledge, and it comes from the consciousness of possessing the ability requisite for what one undertakes.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: The consciousness of not being genuine, not being what others think him to be, robs a man of power, honeycombs the character, and destroys self-respect and self-confidence.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLV

quotes.text: The great prizes of life are for the courageous, the dauntless, the self-confident.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: The lack of self-confidence and lack of faith in one's ideas in one's mission in life have caused innumerable failures.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter LXV

quotes.text: The loss of self-respect, the loss of character, is irreparable.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIX

quotes.text: The very intensity of your confidence in your ability to do the thing you attempt is definitely related to the degree of your achievement.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Those who have accomplished great things in the world have been, as a rule, bold, aggressive, and self-confident.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We are so constituted that every departure from the right, from principle, causes loss of self-respect, and makes us unhappy.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXII

quotes.text: We can not help being influenced by other people's opinion of us. It makes us, according to its nature, think more or less of ourselves, of our ability.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: We must lose ourselves before we can find ourselves. Self analysis is valuable only to learn our strength; fatal, if we dwell upon our weaknesses.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XIX

quotes.text: We radiate our faith, our confidence in ourselves or our doubts, and distrust.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: What miracles self-confidence has wrought! What impossible deeds it has helped to perform!
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: Whatever you do, don't set up in your own mind and in that of others a picture of yourself as a weak, ineffective, negative personality.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You can only do what you think you can. If you hold in mind a cheap, discreditable picture of yourself; if you doubt your efficiency you are shackled, you are not free to express yourself.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden

quotes.text: You forsake yourself when you lose your confidence.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XLIII

quotes.text: You will like yourself better when you have the approval of your conscience.
quotes.author: Orison Swett Marden
quotes.source: Pushing to the Front (1894) — Chapter XXII

quotes.text: To love oneself is the beginning of a life-long romance.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: 'Phrases and Philosophies for the Use of the Young', (1894)

quotes.text: It would be better for me... that multitudes of men should disagree with me rather than that I, being one, should be out of harmony with myself.
quotes.author: Plato

quotes.text: Power doesn't have to show off. Power is confident, self-assuring, self-starting and self-stopping, self-warming and self-justifying. When you have it, you know it.
quotes.author: Ralph Ellison

quotes.text: Conformity is the ape of harmony.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Discontent is the want of self-reliance: it is infirmity of will. Regret calamities if you can thereby help the sufferer; if not, attend your own work and already the evil begins to be repaired.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Insist on yourself; never imitate. Your own gift you can present every moment with the cumulative force of a whole life’s cultivation; but of the adopted talent of another you have only an extemporaneous half possession.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind. Absolve you to yourself, and you shall have the suffrage of the world.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The basis of good manners is self-reliance. Necessity is the law of all who are not self-possessed.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The objection to conforming to usages that have become dead to you is that it scatters your force.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The other terror that scares us from self-trust is our consistency; a reverence for our past act or word because the eyes of others have no other data for computing our orbit than our past acts, and we are loath to disappoint them.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The sentiment they instil is of more value than any thought they may contain. To believe your own thought, to believe that what is true for you in your private heart is true for all men,—that is genius.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The virtue in most request is conformity. Self-reliance is its aversion.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: The voyage of the best ship is a zigzag line of a hundred tacks. See the line from a sufficient distance, and it straightens itself to the average tendency. Your genuine action will explain itself and will explain your other genuine actions. Your conformity explains nothing.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Yield not one inch to all the forces which conspire to make you an echo.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: conversation, as reported by Charles J. Woodbury, Talks with Ralph Waldo Emerson (1890), p. 30.

quotes.text: Your conformity explains nothing. Act singly, and what you have already done singly will justify you now.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: Above all things, one should maintain his self-respect, and there is but one way to do that, and that is to live in accordance with your highest ideal.
quotes.author: Robert G. Ingersoll
quotes.source: The trial of Charles B. Reynolds for blasphemy (1887)

quotes.text: It is only when you have mastered the art of loving yourself that you truly love others. It's only when you have opened your own heart that you can touch the hearts of others. When you feel centered and alive, you are in a much better position to be a better person.
quotes.author: Robin Sharma
quotes.source: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari (1996)

quotes.text: If you do not express your own original ideas, if you do not listen to your own being, you will have betrayed yourself. Also, you will have betrayed your community in failing to make your contribution.
quotes.author: Rollo May
quotes.source: Ch. 1 : The Courage to Create, p. 12

quotes.text: The individual has always had to struggle to keep from being overwhelmed by the tribe. To be your own man is a hard business. If you try it, you'll be lonely often, and sometimes frightened. But no price is too high to pay for the privilege of owning yourself.
quotes.author: Rudyard Kipling
quotes.source: As quoted from “Interview with an Immoral,” Arthur Gordon, Reader’s Digest (July 1959). Reprinted in the Kipling Society journal, “Six Hours with Rudy…

quotes.text: The supposition that the world is ever in league to put a man down is childish. Hardly less childish is it for an author to lay the blame on reviewers. A good sturdy author is a match for a hundred reviewers.
quotes.author: Samuel Butler

quotes.text: Almost all absurdity of conduct arises from the imitation of those whom we cannot resemble.
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.text: A man must have the courage to be himself, and not the shadow or the echo of another.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: A man will respect the individuality of another if he wishes to be respected himself.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Admiration of great men, living or dead, naturally evokes imitation of them in a greater or less degree.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: In his presence, young men learned to respect themselves; and out of the root of self-respect there grew up the manly virtues.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Intellectual intrepidity is one of the vital conditions of independence and self-reliance of character.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Many persons give themselves a great deal of fidget concerning what other people think of them and their peculiarities.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Men often conquer difficulties because they feel they can. Their confidence in themselves inspires the confidence of others.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Nothing begets confidence in a man sooner than the practice of this virtue, and nothing shakes confidence sooner than the want of it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Poverty itself may be lifted and lighted up by self-respect; and it is truly a noble sight to see a poor man hold himself upright amidst his temptations, and refuse to demean himself by low actions.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Self-reliance of the best kind does not involve any limitation in the range of human sympathy.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Self-respect is the noblest garment with which a man may clothe himself—the most elevating feeling with which the mind can be inspired.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Such biographies increase a man’s self-reliance by demonstrating what men can be, and what they can do; fortifying his hopes and elevating his aims in life.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The duty lay in their way—it seemed to be the nearest to them—and they set about doing it without desire for fame, or any other reward but the approval of their own conscience.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The power of self-help will gradually grow; and in proportion to a man’s self-respect, will he be armed against the temptation of low indulgences.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: The zealous energetic man unconsciously carries others along with him. His example is contagious, and compels imitation.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: There is but one way of looking at fate—whatever that be, whether blessings or afflictions—to behave with dignity under both.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles

quotes.text: Thus it is good for men to be roused into action and stiffened into self-reliance by difficulty, rather than to slumber away their lives in useless apathy and indolence.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Character (1871) — Chapter XII--The Discipline Of Experience

quotes.text: Call to mind what honourable or brave deeds you have done; consider the good side of your own life.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 78 (On The Healing Power Of The Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: However, what you think of yourself is much more to the point than what others think of you.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 29 (On The Critical Condition Of Marcellinus), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you wish to set a value on yourself, put away your money, your estates, your honours, and look into your own soul.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 80 (On Worldly Deceptions), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: If you would wield a command that is profitable to yourself, and injurious to nobody, clear your own faults out of the way.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: No one, I think, rates virtue higher or is more consecrated to virtue than he who has lost his reputation for being a good man in order to keep from losing the approval of his conscience.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 81 (On Benefits.), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: One who can so revere another, will soon be himself worthy of reverence.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 11 (On The Blush Of Modesty), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Our lack of confidence is not the result of difficulty; the difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 104 (On Care Of Health And Peace Of Mind), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Praise the quality in him which cannot be given or snatched away, that which is the peculiar property of the man.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 41 (On The God Within Us), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Scorn the pleasure that comes from the majority’s approval. The many speak highly of you, but have you really any grounds for satisfaction with yourself if you are the kind of person the many understand?
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: The very soul must be happy and confident, lifted above every circumstance.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 23 (On The True Joy Which Comes From Philosophy), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: There is nothing that brings greater trouble on us than the fact that we conform to rumor, thinking that what has won widespread approval is best, and that, as we have so many to follow as good, we live by the principle, not of reason, but of imitation.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Dialogues and Essays, J. Davie, tans., (Oxford: 2007), p. 44.

quotes.text: What they wish to have heaped upon you are not really good things; there is only one good, the cause and the support of a happy life,—trust in oneself.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 31 (On Siren Songs), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: When men praise great incomes, he should praise the person who can be rich with a slender estate and measures his wealth by the use he makes of it.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 94 (On The Value Of Advice), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: You can tell the character of every man when you see how he gives and receives praise.
quotes.author: Seneca

quotes.text: Your greatest difficulty is with yourself; for you are your own stumbling-block.
quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 21 (On The Renown Which My Writings Will Bring You), trans. Richard M. Gummere

quotes.text: Perform anonymous service. Whenever we do good for others anonymously, our sense of intrinsic worth and self-respect increases.... Selfless service has always been one of the most powerful methods of influence.
quotes.author: Stephen Covey

quotes.text: We reap what we sow. We are the makers of our own fate. None else has the blame, none has the praise.
quotes.author: Swami Vivekananda

quotes.text: Praise is the best diet for us, after all.
quotes.author: Sydney Smith

quotes.text: Above all do not forget your duty to love yourself.
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.source: Letter to Hans Peter, Kierkegaard's cousin (1848)

quotes.text: In your own vigorous lives you show by every act how scant is your patience with those who do not see in the life of effort the life supremely worth living.
quotes.author: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: The wise treat self-respect as non-negotiable, and will not trade it for health or wealth or anything else.
quotes.author: Thomas Szasz

quotes.text: Whatever you may suffer, speak the truth. Be worthy of the entire confidence of your associates. Consider what is right as to what must be done. It is not necessary that you should keep your property, or even your life, but it is necessary that you should hold fast your integrity.
quotes.author: William Ellery Channing
quotes.source: Memoir of William Ellery Channing: With Extracts from His Correspondence and Manuscripts (1848), Vol. II. Part III. Chapter VII: Home Life

quotes.text: Hurry is the deathblow to calmness, to dignity, to poise.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: If you are sure you are right, do not let the voice of the world, or of friends, or of family swerve you for a moment from your purpose.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is daring to stand alone. Be an oak, not a vine.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: It is the day-by-day heroism that vitalizes all of a man's power in an emergency, that gives him confidence that when need comes he will and must be ready.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: It requires only greater effort, closer attention, deeper consecration; but the impossible does not exist for the man who is self-confident and is willing to pay the price in time and struggle for his success or development.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Let us ever turn our face toward the future with confidence and trust, with the calmness of a life in harmony with itself, true to its ideals, and slowly and constantly progressing toward their realization.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Life is an individual problem that man must solve for himself.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Man can develop his self-reliance by seeking constantly to surpass himself.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Man does not ask for flattery, he does not long for fulsome praise, he wants the honest, ringing sound of recognition of what he has done, fair appreciation of what he is doing, and sympathy with what he is striving to do.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: The constant looking backward to what might have been, instead of forward to what may be, is a great weakener of self-confidence.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The man who is self-reliant does not live in the shadow of some one else's greatness; he thinks for himself, depends on himself, and acts for himself.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: The world is busy with its own cares, sorrows and joys, and pays little heed to you. There is but one great password to success,—self-reliance.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: There are individuals with rare mental gifts, and delicate spiritual discernment who fail utterly in life because they lack the one element,—self-reliance.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: Tolerance is a calm, generous respect for the opinions of others, even of one's enemies.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: The Power of Truth (1902) — New York

quotes.text: We constantly eclipse ourselves by ourselves, and then we blame Fate.
quotes.author: William George Jordan
quotes.source: Self-Control, Its Kingship and Majesty (1899) — Contents

quotes.text: What the world needs and what individuals need is a higher standard of living, a great realizing sense of the privilege and dignity of life, a higher and nobler conception of individuality.
quotes.author: William George Jordan

quotes.text: As is our confidence, so is our capacity.
quotes.author: William Hazlitt

quotes.text: When you give a man a dole, you deny him his dignity, and when you deny him his dignity you rob him of his destiny.
quotes.author: Zig Ziglar

quotes.text: People with healthy self-esteem do not need to create pretend identities.
quotes.author: bell hooks

quotes.text: The lotus clouds the mind, saps the will, but doesn't change who you are.
quotes.author: Calypso

quotes.text: You can't win with a perfect defence.
quotes.author: Eumaeus

quotes.text: After years of war, no one could stand between my men and home. Not even me.
quotes.author: Odysseus

quotes.text: Fortune favors the brave.
quotes.author: Odysseus

quotes.text: The clearest view of a man is from below.
quotes.author: Odysseus

quotes.text: The power of the sacrifice is in the cost of the person making it.
quotes.author: Odysseus

quotes.text: In this world, a man does what he chooses. I do what I can.
quotes.author: Penelope

quotes.text: Love's not a sacrifice.
quotes.author: Penelope
